title: Abraham Benaroya and the Transformation of Otherness: The Dialectics of Socialist Inclusion in the Greek Left-Wing Press (1918–1924)
abstract: Abstract Studies of anti-Jewish representations in the Greek press of the 1910s–1930s have focused on right-wing dailies, assuming that class-based universalism precluded similar attitudes within the labor press. This article argues that socialist universalism did not eliminate the production of Jewish Otherness but relocated it. title: The Green Shift: Transforming the Indian Tourism Industry through Sustainability
abstract: Purpose: This study analyzes the transformation of India's tourism industry through sustainability adoption by examining key factors influencing environmental conservation, socio-economic development, community engagement, and responsible travel practices. It identifies the opportunities and challenges affecting the industry's long-term viability and inclusive growth. Methodology: The study is based on an extensive literature review and secondary data analysis. title: Prevalence of Dietary Supplement Use and Potential Medication Interactions Among Adults with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize the prevalence and correlates of dietary supplement use, identify commonly used supplements, and evaluate potential supplement-medication interactions among adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from 451 adults in the Approaches to Positive, Patient-centered Experiences of Aging with Lupus (APPEAL) study, an ancillary study of the population-based Georgians Organized Against Lupus cohort. title: SEVENTY YEARS OF THE BRAZILIAN FEDERAL COUNCIL OF CHEMISTRY (1956–2026): INSTITUTIONAL TRAJECTORY, PRESIDENCIES, AND PERSPECTIVES FOR THE CHEMISTRY PROFESSION - EN
abstract: Background: In 2026, the CFQ/CRQ System turns 70 (Law No. 2,800/1956), overseeing a sector responsible for ~11% of industrial GDP, but it lacked a chronological reconstruction based on its own official primary records. Aim: To reconstruct the System's legal genesis, establish a documented official chronology of its presidencies, and discuss current regulatory challenges. abstract: Ponto-Caspian kökenli bir bivalv türü olan Dreissena polymorpha (Pallas, 1771), monospesifik kolonileşmeleri sayesinde içsulardaki en önemli işgalci türlerden biri olup, birçok ekolojik ve ekonomik problemlere neden olduğu bildirilmektedir. title: A quantum-inspired multi-objective learning framework for real-time sustainable aquaculture water quality prediction
abstract: Management of sustainable aquaculture necessitates accurate prediction of water quality parameters, since environmental variability is an important factor in determining aquatic productivity and ecological stability. Traditional machine learning systems are usually limited by inefficient parameter optimization, feature overlap, and limited adaptability to non-linear and time-varying environmental trends. title: Coping Skills and Stress Management Strategies as Relative Predictors of Job Effectiveness among Business Education Lecturers in Colleges of Education, South West Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the association between coping skills and stress management techniques as relative determinants of job performance among business education instructors at South West Nigerian Colleges of Education. The study used a descriptive survey research design and was based on the transactional model of stress and coping (Lazarus & Folkman, 1984). title: Soil and Water Assessment Tool reveals dominant baseflow in semi-arid catchment with sand dams in Kenya
abstract: Introduction Increasing water scarcity and climate variability threaten rural livelihoods in semi-arid regions. Sand dams are widely used as Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to retain water within the sandy matrix of ephemeral riverbeds, yet their catchment-scale hydrological effects remain insufficiently quantified. Methods We applied the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT+) in a 22.35 km 2 ungauged ephemeral catchment in Makueni County, Kenya, containing 22 sand dams. title: A lightweight model for steel surface defect detection based on EDGI-YOLO
abstract: To address the limitations of YOLOv8n in steel surface defect detection–namely, its large parameter count and computational cost, insufficient multi-scale feature modeling capability, and poor scale adaptability of the detection head– we propose a lightweight improved model named EDGI-YOLO. The model is restructured along four dimensions. title: Multi-omics insights into bacterial and fungal bioremediation of Potentially Toxic Elements (PTEs): a critical overview of their applications
abstract: Potentially toxic elements (PTEs) are persistent contaminants of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems and heavy metals and metalloids represent a major environmental and health concern. Microbial bioremediation exploits the ability of bacteria, fungi, and microbial communities to modulate PTE fate through processes including biosorption, bioaccumulation, redox transformation, biomineralization, precipitation, chelation, and extracellular sequestration. title: Accuracy assessment of terrestrial laser scanning for estimating tree height, diameter at breast height, crown dimensions, and aboveground biomass
abstract: Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) provides dense three-dimensional observations of forest structure and has the potential to complement or replace labor-intensive conventional measurements for selected tree attributes. This study establishes an accuracy-assessment framework for estimating tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), crown dimensions, and aboveground biomass (AGB) from TLS point clouds. title: New records and invasion risk of Stenochrus portoricensis Chamberlin, 1922 (Schizomida: Hubbardiidae) in Brazil
abstract: Stenochrus portoricensis Chamberlin, 1922 is a schizomid native to the Caribbean and Central America and is notable for facultative parthenogenesis and a broad synanthropic distribution. It is widely reported as an exotic species in several regions worldwide, with recognized invasive potential. Here, we expand its known distribution in Brazil by documenting the first records from the state of Mato Grosso and new occurrences in tourist caves in Bahia. title: From molecular networks to the clinic: a systems biology–nanomedicine roadmap for osteoarthritis diagnosis, regeneration, and safety-by-design
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a severe, whole-joint illness that is characterized by the permanent destruction of articular cartilage. The failure of traditional therapies and early tissue engineering efforts is mainly due to their reductionist biological strategies and reliance on bulk, non-biomimetic materials that cannot replicate the complex nanoscale architecture of the native extracellular matrix. title: India, China and the China+1 Strategy: Trade, Investment and Policymaking in a Fragmented World
abstract: ABSTRACT COVID‐19 and geopolitical tensions have compelled global firms to diversify parts of their operations to other countries. Although India looks primed to gain from this ‘China+1’, the authors' research, including interviews with 50 executives, officials and experts across India, America, Europe and Singapore, paints a more cautious picture. title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the Endangered scaly-sided merganser Mergus squamatus with insight into its demographic history
abstract: The scaly-sided merganser, Mergus squamatus, is an Endangered piscivorous duck which has been declining since the late 1900s due to habitat loss, over-hunting, and climate change. Despite being a species of global conservation concern and subject to ex- and in-situ conservation efforts, genomic research has been limited, hindering our understanding of its population genetic status and evolutionary history. abstract: Abstract Collagen and its derivatives stand out as valuable biomaterials for applications in foods, cosmetics, healthcare products, medical equipment, and drug delivery carriers due to their high biocompatibility, biodegradability, and lack of toxicity and immunogenicity. However, the problem of microbial contamination in collagen is too important to ignore, which limits its further application in various fields. abstract: Currently, climate change and the dwindling availability of water resources necessitate sustainable water management strategies in arid and semi-arid agriculture. title: Wounded from Within: Trauma and the Body in Yesika Salgado’s and Rigoberto González’s Latinx Life Writings
abstract: Abstract This essay develops the conceptual framework of the wound as both a critical and interpretive method for reading the life writings of Salvadoran American poet Yesika Salgado and queer Chicano author Rigoberto González. Drawing on insights from trauma studies, somatic theory, and Latinx literary and cultural criticism, I examine how their works register the biological and internalized reverberations of historical, intergenerational, and intersectional trauma. title: The 1956 Suez crisis: Britain’s relative decline and the geoeconomics of British power
abstract: The Suez Crisis of 1956 is conventionally seen as a turning point in Britain’s decline as a world power. This article argues instead that the Suez Crisis exposed the consequences of a much longer process of relative economic decline. By 1956, slower productivity growth and declining international competitiveness had weakened Britain’s economic position, while the need to defend sterling left it increasingly dependent on American financial support. abstract: Manufacturing has historically aided as a first driver of economic development in advanced economies, contributing meaningfully to structural transformation, employment creation, and technological progress. title: Temperature–based quantitative detection of micro–internal leakage in heat–cycle isolation valves of nuclear power plants
abstract: The internal leakage of heat-cycle isolation valves in nuclear power plants impairs plant economics and may trigger environmental contamination or safety issues due to medium release. Non-destructive, on-line and quantitative detection methods are therefore urgently required. abstract: The growing prevalence of antibiotic resistance and biofilm-forming dental pathogens necessitates the development of alternative antimicrobial strategies. Staphylococcus epidermidis is an opportunistic pathogen associated with dental biofilms, oral microbial colonization, and implant-related infections, contributing to persistent infections and treatment challenges. title: New Orleans and the Illegal Transatlantic Slave Trade, 1857–1861
abstract: This study explores the role of New Orleans in the illegal transatlantic slave trade between 1857 and 1861. It argues that the city’s growing involvement in this trade was connected to broader debates and attempts to reopen the transatlantic slave trade in Louisiana, which had been prohibited since 1808. title: Roasting-induced changes in the metabolite profile of laver (Neopyropia yezoensis): Focus on mycosporine-like amino acids and antioxidant activity
abstract: This study investigated non-volatile metabolites in laver ( Neopyropia yezoensis ) roasted under different temperature/time conditions. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry-based metabolomics identified 69 metabolites, including mycosporine-like amino acids (MAAs) and their dehydrated derivatives. abstract: This study evaluated the effects of different pretreatment methods on the phytochemical composition and amino acid profile of “Nyama Asabo” (Diplazium esculentum) to determine the most effective processing method for preserving its nutritional quality in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. title: The PAXT connection is a modifier of rare codon-enriched protein expression

However, there are an increasing number of examples whereby rare codon-enriched genes are paradoxically highly expressed, suggestive of mechanisms to overcome the poor expression imposed by rare codons. title: Elevation-dependent classification of outdoor thermal stress in a tropical Andean country: a case study of Colombia
abstract: Outdoor thermal comfort in tropical mountain countries is shaped by air temperature, humidity, wind, solar radiation and topography, with elevation strongly controlling thermal stress (TS). This study evaluates how elevation modulates outdoor TS in Colombia and proposes an elevation-based thermal stress level (TSL) classification. title: Evolutionary and Deep Learning Models Highlight Deleterious Mutations Behind the History of Sugar Beet Breeding
abstract: Sugar beet (Beta vulgaris ssp. vulgaris) is a major global source of sucrose. Domestication and a history of breeding have shaped the distribution of deleterious mutations across the genome. abstract: Abstract Acoustic sensors and microphone array technologies are widely used in industrial condition monitoring and fault diagnosis, and their reliability directly affects monitoring stability and equipment safety. abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have undergone an unprecedented expansion of host range since 2021, moving from wild birds and poultry into dairy cattle, domestic cats, and other mammals, with sporadic human infections in Europe and North America ( Food and Agriculture Organization et al., 2025a ; Rolfes et al., 2025 ). abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue is a major vector-borne disease, with rising incidence driven by climate change, rapid urbanization, and increased international travel. Although early warning systems (EWSs) have shown promising predictive performance in endemic settings, limited evidence on implementation barriers from local end users hinders their integration into routine proactive vector control. abstract: Due to its rapid spread and the absence of approved antiviral treatments, Monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been declared as a global health emergency. This study aimed to identify possible drug candidates targeting MPXV vaccinia proteins D8L which is involved in host cell entry, and D4R/A20R Complex responsible for viral DNA replication and host cell entry. abstract: Abstract Hail simulation remains challenging in convection-permitting models, and diagnosing bias pathways is essential for targeted improvement. title: Practical Insights from Operationalizing a Remote Symptom Monitoring Program Using a Commercial Platform in a Canadian Community Cancer Clinic: A Post-Implementation Qualitative Evaluation
abstract: Remote symptom monitoring using electronic patient-reported outcomes reduces symptom burden and acute care use in oncology, but most programs have been established in academic centers or funded trials using purpose-built software. We examined how the REmote Symptom and Patient mONitoring System (RESPONSe) was implemented and subsequently funded as a recurrent clinical service at a Canadian community cancer clinic using a configured commercial platform, patients' own devices, and no formal institutional mandate. abstract: Previous Euphrates and regulated-river forecasting studies have often compared algorithms without quantifying how far prediction can proceed when reservoir releases, storage, withdrawals, and allocation rules are unavailable. abstract: The microbiota–gut–brain (MGB) axis and it’s the role in physiology and behaviors of the host with serotonin as a key signaling molecule have received much attention in recent years. 5-Hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP), an effective serotonin precursor, has regulatory effects on the MGB axis, but little is known about these effects in fish. abstract: This study investigates the persistent barriers to democratic accountability within Indonesian public administration by elucidating the evolving cultural logic termed modernized cosmogony. Drawing on historical institutionalism and critical realism-informed research, the research reveals how inherited sacred hierarchies, rooted in pre-colonial cosmologies, have dynamically adapted to withstand colonial, authoritarian, and democratic reforms. abstract: Airborne microplastics (MP) have emerged as a growing environmental and human health concern globally. abstract: Intravenous urography (IVU) is essential for evaluating urinary tract disorders but involves ionizing radiation exposure that may induce cancer risks. abstract: Soil health is a critical component of agroecosystems, supporting plant growth, nutrient cycling, and ecosystem services. title: Chemical characterization and source apportionment of carbonaceous aerosols during post-monsoon biomass burning and Diwali at an upwind site of Delhi
abstract: Severe post-monsoon haze in Delhi-NCR poses air-quality and health risks and reflects regional and urban emissions. Sonipat lies along the principal transport corridor linking the agricultural burning regions of Punjab and Haryana with Delhi and serves as an intermediate receptor for regional pollution. However, source apportionment at upwind locations remains limited. To address this gap, we measured composition-based PM 2.5 , defined as non-refractory PM 2.5 plus equivalent black carbon, at Sonipat from 25 October to 15 November 2023 using a Time-of-Flight Aerosol Chemical Speciation Monitor

title: Gut microbiota of dung beetles shows taxonomic turnover but relative functional stability
abstract: The dung beetle gut microbiota is essential for host health and plays a key role in regulating the biochemical processes underpinning grassland ecosystem functioning. Understanding how its taxonomic and functional composition varies across species may help predict the ecological consequences of changes in dung beetle communities driven by shifts in pastoral practices. Elucidating the mechanisms of microbial acquisition and potential transmission is also crucial. title: Dose-Dependent Effects of Sewage Sludge on Matthiola incana: A Sustainable Approach for Ornamental Plant Production
abstract: In recent years, the storage and disposal of sewage sludge, which have emerged as a source of pollution, have become a serious problem. In this context, the use of sewage sludge for agricultural purposes is seen as the most economical, practical, sustainable and environmentally friendly method. This study was conducted to evaluate the use of sewage sludge as a growing medium and its impact on the growth and development of Matthiola incana (‘İron Rose Pink’). The study was conducted in 2025 in an unheated glass greenhouse belonging to the Research and Application Center of Tokat Gaziosmanpaşa U

title: Inventing an interstice: les Français d’Asie, the canonisation and the location of Franco-Asian culture
abstract: This article focuses on the Belle Époque activities of an understudied literary and artistic grouping, Les Français d’Asie (1909–1914), led by Albert de Pouvourville, and uniting some of the key figures of the cultural and political sphere of that period, including Pierre Loti, Camille de Saint-Saëns, Claude Farrère and Albert Sarraut. title: Effect of starter ration supplementation on pre- and post-weaning growth performance of Dorper × Menz lambs
abstract: Pre-weaning nutrition is critical for improving lamb growth, as inadequate nutrient supply during early life can limit growth potential. This study evaluated the effects of starter ration supplementation, with or without vetch hay, on the growth performance of Dorper × Menz lambs. The experiment was conducted using a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with 36 lambs allocated to four treatments: dams’ milk + concentrate offered to their dams (T1), dam milk + vetch hay (T2), dam milk + starter ration (T3), and dam milk + starter ration + vetch hay (T4). title: Derivation of Dose Conversion Factors by Measurement of Patients’ Organ Size in Computed Tomography Machine
abstract: Diagnostic radiology requires an advance form of dosimetry, for its reliable use during exposures in Computed Tomography.Samples of some patient exposure data on Abdominopelvic region of the body was collected from a hospital for use.The organ length or dimension for the Anterior Posterior (AP), Lateral (LAT), Patient Weight and Computed Tomography Dose Index volume (CTDIvol), makes up the data used.The product of the conversion factor f size 16 or f size 32 , based on the patient, and the CTDIvol, gives the Size Specific Dose Estimate (SSDE).The CTDIvol mean was 8.85mGy, range 4.02 mGy -13.68

title: Sign, Structure, Labour: Layered Object Analysis of Three Design Mediations of Danzhai Miao Indigo Costume
abstract: Miao batik from Danzhai County, Guizhou, belongs to China's first national inventory of intangible cultural heritage, yet ceremonial indigo costume is less often worn as everyday dress while its signs travel through fashion and tourism. This article asks a design question rather than a safeguarding one: when fashion branding, structural reconstruction, and community making intervene in this practice, which layer of design does each actually change—sign, structure, or labour—and what does each leave untouched? title: Enhanced hyperspectral classification for geological mapping based on spatial–spectral novel framework of vision transformers and mamba models on PRISMA data at Arabian–Nubian Shield
abstract: Abstract Lithological mapping of arid Precambrian basement underpins mineral exploration across the Arabian-Nubian Shield (ANS), where rugged, poorly accessible exposures make field campaigns slow and costly, and where serpentinites, ophiolitic mélange, granitoids and hydrothermal alteration of economic interest occur in close spatial association. Spaceborne hyperspectral imaging resolves the narrow mineral absorptions that distinguish these units and offers a route to rapid, reproducible regional reconnaissance. title: Beyond renal support: biological modulation across pathophysiological domains during continuous renal replacement therapy — a randomized pilot study
abstract: Background Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is the preferred extracorporeal renal support modality for haemodynamically unstable critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI). Although regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) is primarily used to maintain circuit patency, its biological effects may extend beyond anticoagulation itself. We hypothesized that different anticoagulation strategies are associated with distinct biological modulation across complementary pathophysiological domains during CRRT. title: Explainable multi-target ensemble learning with optimized hyperparameters for predicting mechanical properties of eco-friendly concrete
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of compressive strength (CS), flexural strength (FS), and splitting tensile strength (STS) of recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) remains challenging due to the complex nonlinear relationships among mixture components and the high resource demands of traditional laboratory testing, which conflict with sustainability goals. To address these challenges, this study proposes an explainable multi-target machine learning (ML) framework for the simultaneous prediction of RAC mechanical properties. title: A Deep Learning-Powered Multi-Agent Framework with Responsible AI Governance for Trustworthy EEG-Based Neurological Disease Detection
abstract: Deep learning architectures have further accelerated the analysis of neurological disorders through EEG signals at a rate far above the clinical diagnosis. In this paper, we present NeuroMCP-Agent, which is a novel deep learning-based multi-agent framework for XAI-Enabled neuro-disease detection. Our method makes it possible to trust EEG-driven detection of seven neurological conditions, namely, Parkinson PD, epilepsy, schizophrenia, chronic stress, Alzheimer's disease, autism spectrum disorder ASD, and major depression. Moreover, more than a billion people around the globe are affected by the
journal: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Agent Systems

title: Multi-source data assimilation of Sentinel-2 reflectance and SMAP soil moisture into APSIM for maize biomass estimation
abstract: Crop growth models (CGMs) are valuable tools for agricultural monitoring. However, the need for many input parameters, the uncertainties related to model parametrization and structure, and the lack of spatial information motivate the application of techniques such as data assimilation (DA). This paper proposes a DA framework to improve maize biomass estimation. A particle filter (PF) was used to assimilate remotely sensed reflectance and soil moisture (SM) data, both independently and simultaneously, into the Agricultural Production Systems sIMulator (APSIM) model. European Space Research and Technology Centre

title: The Impact of 7Ps on Customer Satisfaction and Customer Loyalty: The Case of Cosmetics Customers in Bangkok
abstract: Aim/Purpose: This study addressed the intensifying competition faced by Thai cosmetics retailers from price-driven online platforms with variable product reliability. It examined how service quality, trust, store atmosphere, location, pricing, and promotion influence customer satisfaction and loyalty, informing strategies for sustaining competitive advantage in Thailand’s cosmetics retail sector. Introduction/Background: This study examined how the 7Ps marketing mix influences customer satisfaction and customer loyalty in Thailand’s cosmetics retail sector, with satisfaction serving as a media

title: What shapes resident segments? A predictive model of sustainability representation of food festivals
abstract: Although it is widely acknowledged that residents' support is crucial for sustainable tourism development and opinions about sustainable tourism at food festivals can vary among residents, most studies assume that these differences occur in a vacuum, without explaining these differing opinions. This paper argues that differential opinions have associated explanations. This study applies the three-step latent class approach to examine data from 460 residents in the context of the Macau Food Festival. journal: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management

title: Management contexts are associated with differences in the ecological value of urban green infrastructure: evidence from three contrasting urban green spaces in Yamoussoukro, Côte d’Ivoire
abstract: Not all urban green infrastructure has the same ecological value. A major factor potentially contributing to this heterogeneity, which remains poorly documented, is the management context of each green space. This study assesses associations between three contrasting management contexts and the floristic, structural and heritage ecological value of urban green infrastructure in Yamoussoukro, Côte d’Ivoire, and discusses their implications for urban planning. Three sites were compared: KONGHO (sacred forest, community-based management), the Yamoussoukro Urban Forest (FUY, institutional manageme

title: A Metrological Assessment of Precision and Accuracy of Earth’s Global Mean Surface Temperature Parameter and Some Consequences
abstract: The studies on climate change are currently conducted over a specific period of time extending back to the industrial era from 1850 onwards and are intended to comprise the entire Earth’s surface. In order to obtain the most recent numerical values of the parameters of interest, they are supplied by Climate Science and, in particular, by Meteorology Organizations. The paper aims to attempt to perform a strict and full metrological analysisconcerning the specific parameter of Earth’s Global Mean Surface Temperature (GMST), considered among the most important ones, as climate behavior is critica
journal: Journal of Global Warming and Climate Change

title: Mineral-dependent and calcium-inhibited adsorption of radium-226 onto quartz and kaolinite in a natural sand substrate
abstract: Radium-226 (226Ra) is mobilized following the disturbance of ore bodies containing uranium-238. The availability of radium-226 to aquatic organisms is governed by its aqueous speciation and sorption to mineral substrates. This study evaluated the influence of mineral phases, calcium (Ca) concentration, and organic matter content on the partitioning of 226 Ra over 48 h. Tests were conducted across three nominal 226 Ra activity concentrations (1, 5, and 50 Bq L -1 ) and four Ca levels (0.9, 7, 35, and 70 mg L -1 ) representative of freshwater systems both affected and unaffected by metal-mining

title: City and Community in Siegfried Kracauer’s Weimar essays
abstract: This article examines the evolution of Siegfried Kracauer’s reflection on Gemeinschaft during the Weimar Republic, situating it within broader debates on community, modernity, and urban life in 1920s Germany. It argues that Kracauer’s engagement with community cannot be reduced to authoritarian or völkisch interpretations, but unfolds through a com- plex analysis of loss, alienation, and collective experience in the modern metropolis. In his early writings, Kracauer depicts the big city as a space of existential alienation and spiritual homelessness, drawing critically on Georg Simmel’s figure
journal: European Journal of Creative Practices in Cities and Landscapes

title: Biofilm metabolic heterogeneity drives macrophage stress and immune evasion
abstract: Spatially confined biofilms generate distinct extracellular microenvironments that may shape host immune responses, yet their effects on macrophage function remain poorly defined. Here, we established an agar block model to generate two metabolically distinct Escherichia coli (E. coli) biofilm states as: Type 1 biofilms, in which the permeation of glucose does not exceed oxygen permeation and metabolism remains predominantly aerobic; and Type 2 biofilms, in which glucose penetrates deeper than oxygen and an anaerobic core forms. title: Bioaccumulation Potential and Phytochemical Profiling of Coffea arabica And Pueraria montana Leaves Obtained from Eyaa Community in Eleme Local Government Area of Rivers State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the phytochemical composition and metal content of Coffea arabica and Pueraria montana leaves collected from Eyaa Community, Eleme Local Government Area, Rivers State, Nigeria. Phytochemical screening was conducted using spectrophotometric methods, while metal content was determined with an atomic absorption spectrophotometer (AAS). The phytochemical analysis showed thatCoffea arabica contained higher concentrations of alkaloids (67.00 ± 0.01 mg/ml), polyphenols (11.03 ± 0.00 mg/ml), and tannins (0.99 ± 0.00 mg/ml), indicating its strong antioxidant and stimulant potent
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF CHEMISTRY AND CHEMICAL PROCESSES

title: Protest coordination across divisions: brokerage under democratic backsliding in Indonesia
abstract: Scholarship on civil society in Asia has often emphasized the structural constraints facing collective action under democratic backsliding. Yet less attention has been paid to the conditions under which fragmented civil society actors can overcome existing divisions and achieve coordinated protest without forming an integrated movement. This article asks how fragmented civil society actors achieve coordinated protest under conditions of democratic backsliding and how variation in local associational fields shapes this process. Drawing on protest mobilization in Yogyakarta and Surabaya, Indones
journal: Journal of Contemporary East Asia Studies

title: Dampened Diurnal Cycles of Hot‐Wet Extremes in Urban Areas Contrast With Thermally Driven Daytime Stress in Rural Landscapes of Beijing‐Tianjin‐Hebei Region
abstract: Abstract Hot‐wet extremes (HWEs) are intensifying in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region, but their fine‐scale diurnal urban–rural contrasts remain unclear. Using summer observations from 1,962 automatic weather stations during 2016–2024, we identify threshold‐exceeding HWE days and show that urban areas experience more compound day–night and independent nighttime HWEs, whereas rural areas are more often affected by independent daytime days. institutions: State Key Laboratory of Severe Weather

title: Physicochemical and microbiological quality of raw cow milk across agro-ecological zones in Jarso District, Eastern Ethiopia
abstract: Improving the physicochemical characteristics and microbial safety of raw milk is essential for strengthening Ethiopia’s dairy supply chain, yet information on how agro-ecological conditions influence milk quality remains limited. This study evaluated the physicochemical properties and microbial quality of raw cow milk collected from three agro-ecological zones in Jarso District, eastern Ethiopia. Seventy milk samples were analyzed using standard dairy analytical procedures. Agro-ecology significantly influenced ( p < 0.05) most physicochemical properties and microbial quality parameters. title: Trafficked and Rescued: Travails of the Chinese “Slave Girl” in Progressive Era California
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines the cultural and intellectual history of the Chinese “slave girl” in Progressive Era California. Joining a rich literature on how the movement of women across Europe and the Americas stoked cultural anxieties around sex work, gender norms, and “trafficking,” this article uses missionary documents and newspaper accounts to explore how slavery discourse collapsed variations in Chinese women and girls' experiences of freedom and unfreedom in America. title: Iron-refractory iron-deficiency anemia in pregnancy associated with a novel TMPRSS6 missense variant (c.248T>G): A case report from North India
abstract: Iron-deficiency anemia remains the most frequent cause of anemia in pregnancy and is usually amenable to treatment with oral or intravenous iron. Nonetheless, a minority of patients exhibit poor therapeutic response despite adequate dosing and compliance, warranting evaluation for uncommon etiologies such as iron-refractory iron-deficiency anemia (IRIDA). IRIDA is a rare inherited disorder with an autosomal recessive pattern, caused by mutations in the TMPRSS6 gene that lead to inappropriate hepcidin activity and disrupted iron regulation. title: Recurrent power outages and the mental health burden of grid reliability in Maryland
abstract: Power outages are increasingly shaped by aging infrastructure, climate stress, and rising electricity demand. Their mental health consequences remain poorly quantified, particularly for routine outages outside major disasters. Here, we link 15-min outage records with Maryland Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project State Inpatient Database records from 2018 to 2023 and estimate ZIP-quarter associations with hospitalizations for primary mental health diagnoses. title: Nitrogen-centered nutrient innovation for decoupling agricultural productivity from greenhouse-gas intensity: evidence, limits, and implementation pathways
abstract: Increasing agricultural production while lowering greenhouse-gas (GHG) intensity is a defining challenge for climate-smart agrifood systems. This critical review evaluates nitrogen-centered nutrient innovations through a boundary-explicit, two-axis framework: evidence confidence for a stated productivity-GHG decoupling outcome and implementation readiness in a specified context. title: Security within Insecurity? Unpacking the Complexities of Salafi–Jihādi Extremism, Jihādi Provision and Governance in Southern Africa: Insights from Cabo Delgado
abstract: Africa’s ungoverned margins are steadily becoming laboratories of rudimentary–proto governance for Salafi–Jihādi groups: from Nigeria’s Boko Haram, Somalia’s al-Shabaab to Mozambique’s Ansar al–Sunna. Although most Salafi–Jihādi groups in the continent have engaged in activities of radicalisation and sporadic terrorism, various nonstate actors are signifying a burgeoning desire for territoriality, jihādi provision and governance. journal: Journal of Central and Eastern European African Studies

title: Pollen on feathers: unlocking the potential to study avian life histories through palynology
abstract: Capsule Bird-associated pollen can be effectively retrieved from single-use gloves worn during ringing to reveal patterns in habitat use and migratory ecology.Aims We compared abundance and richness of bird-associated pollen retrieved from ringers’ gloves, bird bags, feather swabs and feather clippings from Pied Flycatchers Ficedula hypoleuca to establish optimal methods for avian palynological research. We also highlight real-world applicability through proof-of-concept analysis.Methods Thirty females from three sites were handled during routine ringing using new cotton gloves and bird bags.

title: Rethinking norms in the Outer Circle: The case of Namibian English
abstract: Abstract The article revisits Schneider and Schröder’s (2021) assessment of Namibian English (NamE) as a ‘non‑postcolonial’ variety that has moved from a phase of diffuse normative input into a yet uncompleted Phase 3 (‘nativization’) and that – due to ‘ethnic variation’ – remains well short of displaying the ‘homogeneity’ expected of Phase 4 (‘endonormative stabilization’). The article examines the historical record and draws on both perceptual and linguistic datasets collected across Namibian ethnolinguistic groups. title: Nanoengineered therapeutics for snakebite envenoming: Integrating recombinant antivenoms, targeted nanocarriers, nanobodies, toxin inhibitors, and translational challenges
abstract: Snakebite envenoming remains one of the most devastating neglected tropical diseases, causing an estimated 81,000–138,000 deaths and over 400,000 permanent disabilities annually, predominantly among rural populations in low- and middle-income countries. Despite the life-saving efficacy of conventional plasma-derived antivenoms, their therapeutic effect is often compromised by limited tissue penetration, delayed neutralization kinetics, immunogenicity, batch-to-batch variability, cold-chain dependence, and narrow species specificity. title: Validation of EarthCARE CPR reflectivity using the ACTRIS cloud radar network
abstract: The Earth Cloud, Aerosol, and Radiation Explorer (EarthCARE) satellite carries a cloud profiling radar (CPR) designed to observe global cloud properties. In this study, we assess the calibration of CPR reflectivity profiles by comparing them with seven calibrated ground-based cloud radars from the European Aerosol, Clouds and Trace Gases Research Infrastructure (ACTRIS). We compare the statistics of ice cloud reflectivities observed from space and from each ground site. title: Bioinspired Surface Enabled by Anisotropic Pyramid Structure Arrays for Directional Liquid Self‐Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Inspired by the phenomenon of directional liquid transport in natural organisms, various bionic surfaces with customized topological structures have been designed and fabricated, contributing to advances in such fields as microfluidics, microreactors, energy harvesting, biomedicine, etc. Despite extensive progress, bionic surfaces with directional liquid self‐transport capabilities still suffer from high technical thresholds, cumbersome fabrication processes, and contamination‐induced failure, limiting their widespread applications. title: From critique to praxis: reflections on the role of the critical accounting research community within UK academia
abstract: Purpose The interdisciplinary and critical accounting research community remains positioned at the margins of traditional academic projects, despite its longstanding role in academia. In this context, academics face job redundancies, resistance within accounting education and limited reflexive engagement with the community’s historical development. This study aims to explore how senior accounting academics understand, value and engage with critical accounting research. title: Bacterial extracellular vesicles as central mediators of microbiota–host communication
abstract: Bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are nanoscale, lipid bilayer–enclosed structures released by both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria that act as active mediators of microbial and host–microbe communication rather than simple byproducts of membrane turnover. title: A Coupled RF-GWO-CNN Model for Predicting Water Gross Alpha Radioactivity Using Routine Water Quality Indicators
abstract: Monitoring gross alpha radioactivity in water is essential for assessing the health risks associated with nuclear energy utilization. In the Jialing River basin (Nanchong), prediction is hindered by scarce samples, discontinuous monitoring, and the statistical fluctuations of low-background radiation. This paper proposes an integrated RF-GWO-CNN framework that couples Random Forest (RF) feature selection with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) tuned by Gray Wolf Optimization (GWO). title: Commercial Floriculture in Kerala, India: Major Cut Flowers, Production, Marketing and Business Prospects
abstract: Commercial floriculture in Kerala must reconcile the biological suitability of tropical ornamentals with the exacting requirements of a perishable, quality-differentiated market. This critical narrative review examines the principal cut-flower groups relevant to the state, their production systems, postharvest constraints, marketing arrangements and business prospects. Scholarly and institutional evidence published from 2000 to 22 July 2026 was selected through targeted live searches, reference tracing and bibliographic verification. journal: Asian Journal of Agricultural Extension Economics & Sociology

title: A style aware attention transformer for fine grained interior design style recognition
abstract: Fine-grained interior design style recognition is challenging due to the subtle, context-dependent nature of stylistic cues, which are often entangled with dominant semantic objects. While convolutional neural networks effectively capture local textures, they lack global reasoning, whereas Vision Transformers model spatial relationships but do not explicitly encode perceptual style attributes. title: Carbohydrate‐binding modules: powerful tools in the research and development of carbohydrates – a review
abstract: Carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) are independent domains generally appended in carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) with carbohydrate-binding functions. The primary roles of CBMs in CAZymes include targeting, proximity, disruption, and adhesion effects. Due to their capacity to recognize and bind to specific carbohydrate structures, CBMs have emerged as valuable tools with wide applications, greatly facilitating the research and development of carbohydrates. journal: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture

title: Short-term climate scenario sensitivity of a Riyadh office building: energy consumption, operational life cycle cost, and simulation-derived thermal comfort indicators
abstract: As climate change (CC) continues to reshape environmental conditions, combining projected climate data into building performance analysis is crucial for resilient design. This study investigates the influence of CC on energy consumption, economic outcomes, and simulation-derived thermal comfort indicators in a modern office building in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, characterized by hot-arid conditions and high cooling demand. title: Beyond technical capability: how institutional resistance shapes generative AI exposure in civil and environmental engineering occupations
abstract: Purpose This article introduces the Integrated Sociotechnical Exposure Framework (ISEF) to assess generative AI exposure in civil and environmental engineering by separating technical AI suitability (TA) from institutional resistance (IR). The contribution is an operational measurement framework, not a claim that institutional constraint is a new concept. Design/methodology/approach The framework is applied to 674 O*NET tasks across 28 occupations. title: Spectral Watermarking Techniques for Closed-Loop Resilience in Electrified Multi-Echelon Logistics
abstract: This paper develops spectral watermarking as the integrity observer of a closed-loop architecture for multi-echelon resilience under electrified logistics. The plant remains stock coupled to pack energy. The state observer remains a digital twin plus a shift-invariant FKF channel. The new object is a mark written into reserved FKF coefficients of lead-time, order, and current series so that a later detector can ask whether the continuous trajectory still matches the trajectory that was committed. title: The Quality of Ethnic Fermented Bamboo Shoots (Lemea) From Bengkulu (Indonesia) by Using Different Fermentors
abstract: Background: Lemea is a traditional fermented food originating from Bengkulu, Indonesia, and is produced from bamboo shoots and fish. Traditionally, lemea has been fermented using various simple containers, which may affect the fermentation process and the quality of the resulting product. Differences in container materials may influence moisture retention, microbial growth, and sensory characteristics during fermentation. journal: Journal of Innovation in Applied Natural Science

title: Cost-effective tariff-aware HVAC coordination in Saudi residential buildings using physics-informed deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Abstract When multiple On/Off split air-conditioning units in Saudi residential buildings activate simultaneously, the resulting peak demand spike stresses the electrical grid and inflates monthly bills under the kingdom’s two-tier tariff (0.18 SAR/kWh $$\leq$$ 6,000 kWh; 0.30 SAR/kWh above). journal: Journal of King Saud University - Engineering Sciences

title: Regulating private gardens under planning law: Challenges and opportunities encountered in the Low Countries
abstract: Abstract This article examines how planning law in Flanders (Belgium) and the Netherlands regulates residential gardens as nature‐based solutions, identifying both legal opportunities for and obstacles to activating the ecosystem services of gardens. The comparison and analysis focus on normative conditions, planning permission as a regulatory permission and enforcement. The EU's Nature Restoration Regulation makes this comparison a timely exercise, as it contains specific obligations for urban nature, which will likely lead to an increased focus by planning authorities on private gardens.
journal: Review of European Comparative & International Environmental Law

title: Damage detection, localization, and sizing in composite structures using modal shape and multi-head convolutional neural network
abstract: Abstract Owing to their favorable weight-to-performance characteristics, composite sandwich panels are extensively employed across engineering sectors; however, internal defects often escape identification when relying on conventional, visually-driven inspection routines. This study proposes a data-driven framework combining modal shape, image processing, and a multi-head convolutional neural network (CNN) for automated damage identification, localization, and extent estimation. journal: Machine learning for computational science and engineering

title: Influence of irrigation regime and microbial consortium application on pharmaceutical uptake in durum wheat irrigated with treated wastewater
abstract: The reuse of treated wastewater (TWW) in agriculture represents a promising strategy to alleviate freshwater scarcity, although the occurrence of pharmaceuticals (PhACs) raises concerns regarding their fate and potential transfer within the soil–plant system. This study investigated the combined effects of irrigation regime and beneficial microbial inoculation on the persistence, transformation, and plant uptake of PhACs in durum wheat cultivated under controlled pot conditions and irrigated with TWW. title: Getting military AI operational: US lessons for allies
abstract: In NATO’s multi-domain vision, artificial intelligence (AI) is considered the key to managing the enormous amount of data that is collected and exchanged. The article explores how military organizations can prepare for a future where AI permeates every level of operation – from administration to decision support and, ultimately, target engagement. The analyses focus on the practical application of AI within the US military prior to the second Trump Administration. title: Allosteric inhibition of human mitochondrial ClpP by hijacking the dordaviprone (ONC201) binding site
abstract: ClpP protease maintains proteostasis in human mitochondria and is overexpressed in cancers such as acute myeloid leukemia (AML). While activators such as dordaviprone (ONC201) have reached the clinic, the development of ClpP inhibitors has been hampered by paradoxical activation upon orthosteric inhibitor binding. Here, we report a series of quinazolinone-based compounds that allosterically inhibit human ClpP with nanomolar potency. title: GRAIN: Mapping the World's Irrigation Canals and Why It Matters for Water, Food, and Climate
abstract: Abstract The engineered channels that carry water from large dams and rivers to agricultural fields, known as irrigation canals, are the link between source (lakes and reservoirs) and sink (farmlands). These canals make cultivation of crops possible across millions of hectares of land. A comprehensive global map of irrigation canals has, until now, been missing. We introduce in this perspectives, a comprehensively prepared and curated geospatial data set called Global Registry of Agricultural Irrigation Network (GRAIN). title: MECHANISMS OF BACTERIAL MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE: FOCUS ON BIOCIDE-MEDIATED CROSS-RESISTANCE, GEOPOLITICAL DISSEMINATION, AND NOVEL THERAPEUTIC FRONTIERS
abstract: This article provides an in-depth review of the molecular mechanisms responsible for bacterial multidrug resistance (MDR), including efflux pump overexpression, enzymatic inactivation, target modification, and biofilm-associated tolerance. A structured literature search of major academic databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, and Cochrane Library) from 2010 to present was conducted to synthesize relevant molecular and clinical data. title: CMIP6 data usage: lessons learned from more than 200 million downloads
abstract: Earth system simulations from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP) are considered the gold standard in terms of representation of the Earth's climate system, its past and present states, and possible future evolution. As CMIP moves into its seventh phase, the increasing complexity of Earth system models (ESMs) means that there is a greater need for infrastructure resources to store, distribute and utilize CMIP simulations. title: A review of mRNA vaccines and host-directed therapeutics for multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens
abstract: Abstract The persistent threat of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens— Enterococcus faecium , Staphylococcus aureus , Klebsiella pneumoniae , Acinetobacter baumannii , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , and Enterobacter species (ESKAPE)—has necessitated messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) strategies beyond conventional antibiotics. title: Design of a Sanitary Landfill for Solid Waste Disposal in Kaduna North Local Government Area of Kaduna State
abstract: Effective solid waste management is a growing challenge in Kaduna North Local Government, Kaduna State, due to rapid urbanization and increasing waste generation. This study focuses on the design of a sanitary landfill that provides a sustainable and environmentally friendly waste disposal solution for the region. The research involves a comprehensive assessment of current waste generation rates, waste composition, recoverable materials and disposal methods. title: Quantification of Amlexanox in Beagle Dog Plasma by LC–MS/MS and Its Application in a Comparative Pharmacokinetic Study of Conventional and Sustained‐Release Tablets
abstract: ABSTRACT Amlexanox, a 5H‐benzopyranopyridine derivative with emerging therapeutic potential in metabolic and inflammatory diseases, lacks a validated analytical method for pharmacokinetic studies in beagle dogs. A sensitive LC–MS/MS method was developed and validated for amlexanox in beagle dog plasma according to ICH M10 guidelines. Propranolol served as internal standard. abstract: Surface ozone (O 3 ) is a harmful air pollutant and climate forcer. Although studies have explored increases in O 3 concentrations using climate models and evaluated the health impacts, most have emphasized precursor trends, whereas the underlying chemical mechanisms, particularly the reaction kinetics of O 3 formation have been neglected. title: A data driven assessment of structural barriers to electrical equipment manufacturing in Bangladesh: trade dependency, industrial competitiveness, and policy pathways
abstract: The rapid expansion of Bangladesh’s power and industrial sectors has led to a significant increase in demand for electrical equipment, a large portion of which is currently fulfilled through imports, resulting in sustained foreign currency outflows and supply chain vulnerabilities. This study investigates the feasibility, opportunities, and constraints associated with developing local assembly and manufacturing of electrical equipment, with particular focus on transformers and low- and medium-voltage panels. title: Bioenergetic Materials for Tissue Regeneration: Modulating Metabolism to Promote Cellular Anabolism
abstract: Tissue regeneration is an energy-demanding process that requires adequate ATP production to support cellular proliferation, biosynthesis, and tissue remodeling. Under pathological and age-related conditions, bioenergetic deficits impair intrinsic regenerative capacity by disrupting mitochondrial function, redox homeostasis, and anabolic signaling. Although conventional scaffold- and cell-based bioengineering strategies have advanced regenerative medicine, they generally do not directly address the metabolic dysfunction that limits tissue repair. title: Auxiliary Thrust Jet Engines: Design, Integration, and Performance Analysis
abstract: Fixed-wing surveillance aircraft built around electric or small internal-combustion propulsion offer good endurance but are speed-limited, which restricts their ability to reposition rapidly over long standoff distances or evade emerging threats. This paper presents the design, integration methodology, and performance analysis of an auxiliary thrust micro-turbojet engine intended to supplement the primary propulsion system of a long-range, high-speed intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) aircraft. title: Physics informed muon scattering tomography with momentum integration for nonintrusive monitoring of microreactor cores
abstract: Abstract Next-generation microreactors enable remote deployment and semi-autonomous operation, but compact, sealed, heterogeneous cores limit conventional safeguard approaches that rely on access and bulk accountancy. Limited inspection access and complex internal geometry reduce sensitivity to localized anomalies such as missing fuel. title: Synergistic preservation of fresh cut fruits and vegetables through cold chain logistics and antagonistic microorganisms: mechanisms and emerging applications
abstract: Fresh-cut fruits and vegetables are widely popular owing to their pleasant texture, rich nutrients and convenient consumption. Nevertheless, microbial contamination and physiological deterioration frequently emerge during processing and cold chain distribution, triggering quality degradation and shortened shelf life. Conventional single cold storage fails to efficiently suppress psychrotrophic spoilage microorganisms, whereas chemical preservatives carry hidden risks of toxic residues. abstract: ABSTRACT The demand for natural and multifunctional food preservatives has increased due to growing concerns about the safety and sustainability of synthetic additives. In this study, the ethyl acetate extract of Asphodelus microcarpus roots ( Am EA) was evaluated as a preservative, integrating antioxidant and antibacterial evaluation with an artificial intelligence (AI)‐assisted shelf‐life prediction approach. title: Sustainable soil stabilization: a comprehensive review of green technologies, industrial by-products, and bio-mediated methods
abstract: Abstract Soil stabilization is fundamental to geotechnical engineering, yet traditional cement- and lime-based methods impose significant environmental burdens through high energy consumption and CO 2 emissions. This review systematically analyzes sustainable stabilization technologies, including bio-mediated techniques (microbially induced carbonate precipitation [MICP] and enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation [EICP]), industrial by-product utilization (fly ash, ground granulated blast furnace slag [GGBS], steel slag, and cement kiln dust [CKD]), geopolymer and alkali-activated binders, and

title: Green biosynthesis of selenium nanoparticles by a novel Monoraphidium sp.: optimization, bioinformatic insights, and nanoparticle characterization
abstract: Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) offer unique biomedical and industrial potentials with reduced toxicity compared to inorganic selenium, yet sustainable and eco-friendly production methods remain underexplored. As a novel approach, this study reports the first biosynthesis of SeNPs using a locally isolated Monoraphidium sp., alongside optimization of cultivation parameters and bioinformatic analysis. title: Hippobosca equina as an emerging threat in northern temperate zones: Species distribution modelling under climate change
abstract: Climate change poses significant threats to arthropod vectors of veterinary importance. Hippobosca equina, the forest fly, is an obligate ectoparasite of ungulates with demonstrated capacity for pathogen transmission. We employed maximum entropy modelling to predict current and future global distribution patterns of H. equina under climate change scenarios. Using 1195 occurrence records and five bioclimatic variables, we generated models for present conditions and future projections (2050s and 2070s) under SSP 3-7.0 and SSP 5-8.5 scenarios. title: Impact of the GouM transporter on secondary metabolism activation and production yield in Streptomyces noursei strain CK‐15
abstract: Abstract Streptomyces noursei produces various bioactive secondary metabolites with agricultural significance; however, the regulatory mechanisms governing their production and secretion remain largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically characterized the secondary metabolic potential of S . noursei CK‐15 and investigated the role of the transporter gene gouM in regulating gougerotin efflux and global cluster interactions. title: Data-Quality and Single-Source-Of-Truth Frameworks for Inter Agency Reporting: A Review
abstract: Inter-agency reporting, the routine exchange of administrative data among public bodies to produce shared statistics, dashboards, and compliance returns, depends on the assumption that a figure reported by one agency will mean the same thing when consumed by another. In practice, that assumption is fragile. Divergent definitions, duplicated master records, and the absence of an authoritative reference source produce reconciliation disputes, delayed reporting cycles, and eroded institutional trust. title: Biological and Therapeutic Properties of Honey in Wound Healing
abstract: Background. Chronic and infected wounds remain a major clinical challenge due to impaired tissue regeneration, persistent inflammation, bacterial biofilms, and antimicrobial resistance. Aim. This review aimed to assess the biological and therapeutic properties of honey in wound healing, with emphasis on its mechanisms of action, clinical applications, and emerging therapeutic approaches. abstract: Soft soils in road subgrades pose considerable engineering challenges; however, stabilization with marble dust offers an environmentally sustainable alternative. In this study, a 100 × 90 × 90 cm tank was employed to assess soils blended with 0%, 3%, 6%, 9%, and 12% marble dust by dry weight at depths of 10, 20, and 30 cm. abstract: Introduction Urban soils in long-established mining and metallurgical cities represent persistent reservoirs of potentially toxic elements (PTEs), posing long-term ecological and human health risks. Ust-Kamenogorsk (Oskemen), one of Kazakhstan’s major non-ferrous metallurgical centers, has experienced more than seven decades of intensive ore processing and smelting. abstract: ABSTRACT The South Saskatchewan River Basin (SSRB) in southern Alberta is the only major Canadian watershed where water supplies are effectively fully allocated. This was the first region targeted for land‐use and water‐supply planning under new provincial legislation. This paper examines water allocation and management in the SSRB from the unique perspective of 900 years of annual river flow in the four major sub‐basins. title: Soil organic carbon, texture and oxide-associated processes regulate phosphorus availability across Nigerian agroecosystems
abstract: Abstract Background and aims Phosphorus (P) limitation constrains productivity in tropical soils, yet the combined roles of soil organic carbon (SOC), texture, reactive minerals, and acidity in regulating plant-available P remain insufficiently quantified across diverse agricultural soils. This study assessed the relative importance of soil properties and tested hypothesised direct and indirect relationships regulating P availability across Nigerian agroecosystems. abstract: Below every cultivated field lies a civilization of unimaginable complexity. abstract: Pesticide contamination in food and water systems poses significant risks to human health and environmental sustainability, necessitating the development of rapid, sensitive, and on-site detection technologies. This review explores recent advances in quantum dot (QD)-based nanosensors for ultra-sensitive pesticide detection. Owing to their unique optical properties, high surface-to-volume ratio, and tunable fluorescence, QDs enable detection at trace levels ranging from femtomolar to nanomolar concentrations, outperforming many conventional analytical techniques. abstract: Physicochemical features of Allanblackia and Soybean bakery fat and the impact of on baking performance of bread in terms of loaf volume, weight, height and oven spring was investigated. abstract: Forest gaps record disturbance, regeneration, and canopy structural change, yet estimates of gap closure depend strongly on the height threshold used to define when a gap is considered closed. This issue is particularly relevant for three-dimensional LiDAR analyses, where gap structure and dynamics can be quantified across vertical canopy layers. title: Degrowth-oriented entrepreneurial identity in rural agrifood: Evidence from women-led firms in Ireland
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of degrowth-oriented entrepreneurial identity, and theorises how it is formed and enacted in practice by combining degrowth research with rural women entrepreneurship, employing a Feminist Political Ecology (FPE) lens. abstract: The study was conducted to determine the food safety knowledge, attitude and practices of road-side vendors of ready to eat grilled catfish in Awka metropolis, Anambra state, Nigeria. abstract: The uncontrolled dismantling of electronic waste and end-of-life vehicles in low- and middle income countries has emerged as a significant, yet inadequately quantified, source of persistent organic pollutants to the terrestrial environment. title: Anticipating household rescue demand in hurricanes using socio-demographic data and machine learning
abstract: Hurricanes pose severe threats to human life, particularly for residents who shelter in place and later require emergency rescue. While significant existing work has focused on evacuation behavior and long-term recovery, less attention has been devoted to predicting rescue demand during the response phase of disasters. abstract: Safe drinking water remains essential for public health, particularly in developing regions where sachet water is widely consumed. abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks are a critical component of terrestrial carbon pools, influencing soil quality, agricultural productivity, and climate change mitigation. abstract: Bioplastics have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional fossil-based plastics because of their potential to reduce dependence on non-renewable resources and support the transition towards a circular economy. However, their environmental sustainability is determined not only by feedstock selection but also by polymer characteristics, product design, and the effectiveness of end-of-life management systems. abstract: Abstract High-resolution measurements of near-surface temperature are essential for understanding environmental responses to extreme weather events, yet are rarely available from dense, regularly spaced in situ measurement grids. Here, we analyse temperature measurements derived from a dense network of over 3,000 nodal seismometers deployed across a 6 km² area in North Yorkshire, UK, during the July 2022 heatwave, using data from embedded microcontroller sensors. abstract: Background Varicella imposes a sustained public health burden in China, where decades of voluntary single-dose immunization have been associated with recurrent school outbreaks and an age shift toward adolescents. abstract: Disaster-risk-reduction archives describe hazard events in prose that databases such as EM-DAT (Delforge et al., 2025) cannot ingest directly. We present an LLM pipeline that generates candidate georeferenced event records using a controlled hazard vocabulary and fixed schema, retaining evidence for review. Applied to 10,000 documents from PreventionWeb, the knowledge hub managed by UNDRR, it produced 3,572 records from 1,913 documents across 24 hazard types and resolved 81% of location mentions to OpenStreetMap geometries. title: HalifaxDT: A Wireless Digital Twin from Open Geospatial Data
abstract: Wireless digital twins can support site-specific analysis, planning, and experimentation for future wireless networks. However, constructing them at city scale remains challenging when accurate 3D city models are unavailable. This paper presents HalifaxDT, a wireless digital twin of the Halifax Peninsula in Nova Scotia, Canada, constructed from heterogeneous open geospatial and spectrum data. title: A Collisional Origin for Ice-rich Iapetus and Titan's Anomalous Eccentricity
abstract: We test whether collisions involving Titan can eject enough water-rich material onto sufficiently distant Saturn-bound orbits to form Iapetus, while also accounting for Titan's orbital eccentricity. Three-dimensional impact calculations and post-impact trajectories examine initially Saturn-unbound and bound impactors. In the oblique unbound case with a differentiated impactor roughly a tenth the mass of Titan at a speed of 10 km s\(^{-1}\), outgoing predominantly icy material from a selected population totaling about 3.5 times Iapetus's mass remains Saturn-bound for days after impact. title: Asteroids Impacting the Solar System Planets and the Moon. III. Real Impacts from Known Objects and LSST Discovery Predictions
abstract: Impact rates predicted using pre-impact source-population models and those inferred from observations disagree by a factor of a few to $\sim200$ across the Solar System planets and the Moon. An exciting opportunity for an additional observational constraint is the discovery of asteroids before impact and their tracking until impact. We evaluate this prospect based on both known objects and forecasts of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). title: Pseudo-Incrementality Testing: Measuring Advertising Lift from Naturally Occurring Interventions
abstract: We develop a method for measuring the incremental effect of advertising when randomized exper- iments are unavailable. Firms generate abrupt interventions in their own marketing as a byproduct of operations: budgets are cut, channels launch, programs pause. We propose a two-stage proce- dure that treats these events as quasi-experiments. The first stage discovers and dates interventions by exact Bayesian run-length inference on marketing activity series. title: Stress-testing Alignment Midtraining
abstract: When aligning frontier models through post-training techniques, it is not possible to directly demonstrate all of the behaviours we want a model to exhibit in all possible deployment environments; our model must generalise outside of the post-training distribution. One proposed solution is alignment midtraining (AMT), which continues pretraining on large volumes of alignment-relevant documents to encourage generalisation in later stages of training. title: Learning Air-Ground Motion Control with Temporal Mode Switching and Cross-Terrain Tracking
abstract: Passive-wheeled terrestrial-aerial bimodal vehicles (TABVs) combine aerial mobility with energy-efficient ground locomotion. However, reliable air-ground mode switching under limited onboard perception and robust ground trajectory tracking across diverse terrains remain challenging when targeting real-world applications. In this work, we propose a learning-based air-ground motion control framework for passive-wheeled TABVs: 1) a learned mode selector for autonomous air-ground motion mode switching. title: Distinct Population of Wolf-Rayet Stars in the Low-Metallicity Galaxy NGC 6822. Quantitative analysis of optical and UV spectra of the complete sample
abstract: Context: Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars are particularly rare in low-metallicity galaxies and remain poorly understood. Detailed studies of the presumably complete population of WR stars in the nearby Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) galaxy led to perplexing results. Aims: The nearby galaxy NGC 6822 has a similar metallicity to the SMC, and hence provides an excellent laboratory for a comparative study. We aim to derive the stellar and wind parameters of each known WR star in NGC 6822 by means of quantitative spectroscopy. The results are compared with the WR population of the SMC. title: Probing dark matter interactions with a RES–NOVA prototype cryogenic detector
abstract: Abstract We report on the operation of a 13 g PbWO $$_4$$ 4 crystal, grown from archaeological Pb and operated as a cryogenic calorimeter in an underground environment. Read out with a Ge thermistor, the detector achieves a low energy threshold and, for the first time, enables the derivation of a dark matter exclusion limit using PbWO $$_4$$ 4 as target material, for both spin-dependent interactions on neutrons and spin-independent interactions. title: A quasisymmetric analog of Grassmannian Schubert varieties
abstract: We show that the cohomology rings of toric Richardson varieties in the Grassmannian are finite truncations of the ring of quasisymmetric functions. We exhibit an affine paving of each such variety whose cell closures give rise to the basis of fundamental quasisymmetric functions. title: Quarkyonic matter suppresses neutron-star $g$ modes and reverses their mass trend
abstract: Gravity (g) modes are the only neutron-star oscillations that report on the composition of dense matter rather than on its stiffness, and work on hybrid stars has established that a first-order quark transition raises their frequency. Quarkyonic matter does the opposite. Quark-nucleon chemical equilibrium is maintained by the strong interaction, so the quarks acquire no thermodynamic freedom on an oscillation period and $c_s^2-c_e^2$ reduces to a positive-definite quadratic form in the lepton gradients alone. title: Non-stabilizerness and entanglement in $(2+1)$-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory using tensor networks
abstract: We study non-stabilizerness (magic) in the ground state of $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Hamiltonian lattice gauge theory with matter, formulated in the dressed-site basis in the hardcore-gluon truncation and restricted to the zero baryon-number sector. Using matrix product states, we compute three facets of magic: the second-order stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) $M_2$, its non-local component $M_2^{\rm NL}$, and a lower bound in terms of the anti-flatness $F$ of the entanglement spectrum. title: Turbulent gravitational wakes
abstract: We construct turbulent gravitational wakes in asymptotically AdS$_4$ spacetimes by solving the full non-linear Einstein equations in the characteristic formulation. Specifically, we show that a localized boundary deformation acting on a boosted black brane generates a wake whose boundary dynamics exhibit the formation of coherent vortical structures that are advected downstream by the background flow. title: Mag4: An Automated First-Principles Workflow to Extract Magnetic Interactions, from Pair Couplings to Four-Spin Ring Exchange
abstract: Abstract Chemists rationalize and design magnetic materials through structure-property relationships built on pairwise exchange couplings J, which energy-mapping methods now extract routinely from first principles. Yet whenever four magnetic centers close a loop, as in the CuO2 planes of the cuprates or the square nets of infinite-layer oxides, a four-spin ring (cyclic) exchange Jring can arise, reshaping magnetic ground states and corrupting the very J values used for design. title: Move-rb: Faster Bi-Directional r-indexes and Approximate Pattern Matching
abstract: Approximate pattern matching (APM) on highly repetitive texts is a central task in bioinformatics. Bi-directional r-indexes support left- and right-extension of a pattern and thereby accelerate APM algorithms based on search schemes, but existing variants -- br-index and b-move -- suffer from two bottlenecks: $O(σ)$ character-predecessor/-successor queries on the run-length-encoded BWT per extension, and predecessor queries on sparse bit vectors to maintain a value in the suffix array interval and to access the PLCP array while locating. title: VietPrism: A large-scale Vietnamese speech and deepfake corpus with diverse dialects and code-switching
abstract: Vietnamese speech research is constrained by resources that isolate automatic speech recognition from speaker, dialect, code-switching, and deepfake analysis. We introduce VietPrism, an open, multi-domain corpus that brings these dimensions together at scale: 993.4 hours and 403,941 bona fide utterances from 1,262 verified speakers across 8,388 real-world videos. title: Investigation of magnetic-field effects on photomultiplier tubes for the first Large-Sized Telescope of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
abstract: Photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) are widely used in imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes. Their response can depend on the telescope pointing direction through changes in their orientation relative to the geomagnetic field. Such a dependence was indicated during the calibration campaign of the CTAO LST-1. In this work, the LST-1 calibration data are analyzed to quantify the gain dependence in terms of the geomagnetic field, and dedicated laboratory measurements are performed to test the hypothesis that the observed dependence originates from magnetic-field effects. title: Mind the Gap: How SBOM Specification Ambiguities Lead to Divergent Software Bills of Materials. An Empirical Tool Study
abstract: Software Bill of Materials (SBOMs) will become mandatory starting in December 2027 under the European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) [8]. Although previous studies have highlighted significant differences among SBOM generators, the reasons for these discrepancies remain unknown, as does whether they stem from implementation errors or deliberate design choices. In this paper, we evaluate three widely used SBOM generators across more than 3,000 JavaScript and Rust projects, using a groundtruth baseline derived from dependency lockfiles. title: Journeys of Parents with LGBTQ+ Children: How Trauma and Healing Reshape Identity and (Mis)Informating Practices
abstract: This study examines how parents of LGBTQ+ individuals in South Korea navigate the emotional rupture fueled by fear, isolation, and disorientation after learning their children’s queer identity, encounter queer-related (mis)information as a way of coping with this emotional toll, and come to listen to queer realities relationally. title: Depressive symptoms are reflected differently across digital contexts
abstract: As more of everyday life takes place online, digital behavior may provide a potential window into how depressive symptoms are reflected in daily life. Yet digital mental health studies have produced mixed findings. These inconsistencies may partly reflect how digital behavior is measured: self reported use, single device studies, and aggregate screen time can obscure differences across devices, activities, and patterns of engagement. We combined monthly assessments of depressive symptoms with passively recorded mobile and desktop web traces from 1,146 adults in Germany over six months. We exam

title: $μ^2$-Bench: A Multilingual Machine Unlearning Benchmark
abstract: Undesired information such as harmful content and private data propagates through Multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) via direct training and indirect cross-linguistic spread. Multilingual Machine Unlearning (MMU) aims to remove such information, yet its evaluation remains underexplored, leaving unclear whether unlearning truly eliminates target knowledge across all languages. To bridge this gap, we introduce $μ^2$-Bench, an MMU benchmark that simulates the full pipeline of memorization, unlearning, and evaluation across diverse languages. title: Diffusion-Based Super-Resolution of Adriatic Sea Oceanographic Fields
abstract: High-resolution oceanographic fields are critical for resolving mesoscale and sub-mesoscale coastal dynamics, yet their generation remains constrained by both computational cost and observational sparsity. We present OcDiffSR, a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) for oceanographic super-resolution that reconstructs high-resolution sea-surface fields from coarse-resolution reanalysis inputs. Geometry beneath the Waves: Dense Priors for Sparse-View Underwater 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Underwater 3D reconstruction supports applications ranging from marine ecosystem monitoring and subsea inspection to underwater archaeology, education, and immersive visualisation. 3D Gaussian Splatting has made real-time photorealistic novel-view rendering practical, while underwater variants incorporate physically based image-formation models to separate medium effects from scene radiance. Their reconstruction quality, however, remains fundamentally limited by the geometry used for initialisation.

title: GeoCueFormer: Geometry-Guided Wavelet Representation and Prediction-Cued Dual-Stage Decoder for Underwater Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Underwater semantic segmentation is essential for marine ecosystem monitoring, yet remains challenging due to severe visual degradation. Light absorption and scattering often lead to color shifts, low contrast, and blurred boundaries, making shallow detail features unreliable. Existing underwater segmentation methods improve RGB feature aggregation or boundary prediction, but still lack an explicit mechanism to distinguish structure-related details from degradation-induced responses.
