title: Environmental DNA (eDNA) as a Next-Generation Tool for Biodiversity Monitoring: A Review
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is genetic material released by organisms into water, soil, air, and sediment. It has rapidly become a transformative tool for biodiversity monitoring, enabling the detection of species without physically capturing them. Initially applied primarily in aquatic environments, this non-invasive technology has expanded through metabarcoding techniques to multispecies assessments across freshwater, marine, terrestrial, and aerial ecosystems. title: Tsunami excitation by localized subsidence associated with crater formation: a numerical case study for the October 2023 Sofu Seamount event
abstract: Abstract The October 2023 tsunami from Sofu Seamount showed large amplitudes relative to the associated seismic activity, suggesting atypical non-tectonic source processes. Comparisons of pre- and post-event bathymetric data revealed substantial topographic changes at Sofu Seamount, including the formation of a crater-like depression at the central cone within the larger caldera. institutions: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology

title: Application of deep learning to estimate blue and fin whale call density in the southern California Current Ecosystem
abstract: Abstract Blue ( Balaenoptera musculus ) and fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) are dominant contributors to low-frequency ocean soundscapes, yet reliably extracting their calls from long-term passive acoustic recordings is methodologically challenging. Here, we train a multi-class deep-learning detector to identify five principal blue and fin whale call types (A, B, D, 20 Hz, and 40 Hz) from low-frequency spectrograms using a Faster R-CNN architecture combined with three rounds of iterative human review and hard-negative mining, progressively expanding and rebalancing the training set using
institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

title: La playlist de David Lynch
abstract: Un repaso por la evolución de la dimensión musical del cine de David Lynch, estrechamente ligada al diseño sonoro de sus películas y a su singular propuesta narrativa. Como música de fondo suenan temas de Angelo Badalamenti, Julee Cruise, David Bowie, Rammstein, Roy Orbison y las composiciones del propio David Lynch —este es un ensayo que se lee mejor con Spotify o YouTube a la mano—.

title: Legal frameworks for the Arctic blue economy: risks and regulatory responses
abstract: The Arctic blue economy offers new opportunities for the global energy transition and sustainable ocean development, yet its viability depends on a sound legal governance framework. Recent practice reveals three prominent legal deficits: ambiguous treaty authorization, conflicting legislative claims over Arctic shipping routes, and the absence of cross-border coordination mechanisms. title: Navigating knowledge gaps: An emissions inventory approach to understand plastic pollution from international shipping
abstract: Plastic pollution is a complex environmental problem, requiring tailored solutions based on an understanding of contributing sources and mechanisms. Shipping activities significantly affect local plastic loads and, to respond to this ongoing problem, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) is coordinating efforts to address plastic emissions from international shipping. A global, sector-specific assessment could inform such actions, but is currently not feasible due to fragmented and missing data. In this study, a generic plastic emissions inventory framework of ship-sourced plastic flow

title: Seasonal and developmental patterns of body condition in Arctic seals
abstract: Quantifying the body condition of free-ranging marine mammals remains a central challenge in marine ecology, particularly for species inhabiting remote or logistically difficult environments. As rapidly warming conditions threaten the long-term viability of many polar species, such data are urgently needed. Body condition is a key physiological indicator of individual health and informs understanding of population-level responses. Assessments of body condition based on a combination of mass, morphometric, and blubber thickness values can be robust, but are often time-consuming, resource-intens

title: Ecological risk and source apportionment of PAHs and OCPs in surface sediments of the Upper Gulf of Thailand
abstract: This study investigates the occurrence, distribution, and ecological risks of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) in surface sediments collected from 17 stations in the Upper Gulf of Thailand (uGoT). Total PAH concentrations ranged from 6.6 to 744.6 ng g -1 dw, with the highest concentrations recorded at the Chao Phraya river mouth, primarily driven by pyrogenic sources and localized petrogenic inputs from maritime activities. title: First records of the genera Mariaplax Rahayu & Ng, 2014 and Hexapinus Manning & Holthuis, 1981 from India, with descriptions of three new species (Crustacea, Decapoda, Brachyura, Hexapodidae)
abstract: Three new brachyuran crab species of Hexapodidae are described from the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal, based on material collected by FORV Sagar Sampada between 2015 and 2019, with the genera Mariaplax Rahayu & Ng, 2014, and Hexapinus Manning & Holthuis, 1981, reported from Indian waters for the first time. Mariaplax kochazhi sp. nov ., and M. albucus sp. nov . were collected from the Arabian Sea at a depth 30 m while Hexapinus clivus sp. nov . was collected from the Bay of Bengal. institutions: Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology

title: Grey eel catfish (Plotosus canius) fishing by women fishers in the Sundarbans, Bangladesh
abstract: The Sundarbans' women fishworkers play a crucial role in the delta's ecological economy by harvesting, processing, marketing, and inventing within the fishing sector. Through a case study in Koyra, a region in close proximity to the Sundarbans mangrove with a significant reliance on fisheries for local livelihoods, this study examined women's participation in small-scale fishing, particularly in grey eel catfish, Plotosus canius (locally known as Kain magur). During ‘Mora goan’ (the last phase of the full or new moon lunar cycle), a group of women, primarily widows and divorced women, fish Kai

title: A REVIEW OF HIGH-PRESSURE WATER-DRIVEN VALVE ACTUATORS: MECHANISMS, CYLINDERS, MATERIALS, AND SEALING TECHNOLOGIES
abstract: The shift towards sustainable and environmentally friendly industrial technologies has spurred a significant resurgence of interest in water hydraulics, particularly for high-pressure applications in sensitive environments such as nuclear power, food processing, and underwater robotics. This review examines high-pressure water-driven valve actuators, focusing on the design, materials, and sealing technologies of the driving cylinders. Gear-rack actuators serve as the primary case study, reflecting their widespread use in quarter-turn valve service, and are compared with alternative rotary and
journal: Journal of Manufacturing Science and Mechanical Engineering

title: Precise bearing estimation for weak targets with a single vector hydrophone under strong interference
abstract: Single-vector hydrophones face challenges in estimating weak moving target bearings under strong interference. This study introduces a method combining square-root cubature Kalman filtering with adaptive bearing interval constraints. Square-root cubature Kalman filtering optimizes initial bearing estimates, while adaptive bearing intervals together with a Gaussian window suppress directional interference. title: Two new species of Capitellidae (Annelida, Polychaeta) from the southern coasts of China
abstract: The annelid family Capitellidae Grube, 1862 remains poorly known in China, with only a few taxa reported to date. Based on specimens collected from coastal zones during recent ecological surveys, we describe two new species belonging to two small genera of Capitellidae. Barantolla multibranchia sp. nov . is superficially similar to B. sculpta Southern, 1921 in bearing dorsal branchiae on the posterior abdomen, a complete chaetiger 1, and an areolated epithelium on the anterior thorax, but it differs from the latter in having mixed chaetae in both rami of chaetiger 6 and in lacking cuticular sc

title: Orchidaceae Spirito-Sanctensis: A taxonomic and conservation synopsis of orchid diversity in the state of Espírito Santo, Brazil
abstract: The diversity of Orchidaceae in the state of Espírito Santo, southeastern Brazil, was reassessed 40 years after the last comprehensive survey conducted for the region. The study was based on the examination of herbarium specimens, a critical review of the literature, and targeted field expeditions carried out in different phytophysiognomies. A total of 730 taxa (728 species, one subspecies, and one variety) were documented, representing an increase of 130 taxa compared to the 600 previously recorded by Augusto Ruschi. Of these, 39% are currently included in a threat category on the official Re

title: CO2-emissions reduction potential of LNG compared with conventional fossil fuels and the influence of port manoeuvres
abstract: This study evaluated the CO 2 -emission reduction potential of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in maritime transport and examined the influence of vessel operational profiles on emissions performance. A roll-on/roll-off passenger case study indicated an estimated 17.07% reduction in CO 2 emissions using LNG relative to conventional-fuel use, which was lower than the 25%–30% reduction reported previously. title: A rare Arctic record of Haliphron atlanticus (seven-arm octopus) from Bodø, Norway
abstract: Abstract Haliphron atlanticus Steenstrup, 1861, the seven-arm octopus, is a large deep-sea octopod with circumglobal distribution, yet it remains poorly documented due to its inaccessible mesopelagic to benthopelagic habitat and elusiveness. Here we report a rare observation, based on disarticulated remains recovered from a stranding event in Bodø, Arctic Norway (67.27°N, 14.43°E) in March 2026, following an initial report by local citizens. The specimen was identified as an adult female based on morphological examination of recovered remains, including arms, egg clusters, distal oviduct, and

title: Finite Viscoelastic Modeling of Ice Shelves Using Glen's Flow Law and Depth‐Dependent Material Properties
abstract: ABSTRACT Ice shelves are floating seaward extensions of glaciers that form where land‐based ice flows into the ocean. Recent observations suggest that their mechanical behavior is suitably described by a viscoelastic Maxwell model, as this framework captures both the instantaneous elastic response and the time‐dependent viscous flow of ice. The constitutive framework in this contribution is formulated within a finite strain framework based on a multiplicative decomposition of the deformation gradient into elastic and viscous parts. title: Development and Internal Validation of a Risk-Based Safe-Manning Framework for Wing-in-Ground Craft
abstract: Purpose. This study developed and computationally verified a function-based method for determining core operational crew for wing-in-ground (WIG) craft. Methods. A frozen 37-source corpus was mapped to six safety-critical functions, six mission phases, a competence matrix, and phase loads. Bounded integer compositions were tested using an exact scalar max-flow/min-cut model, 20% reserve, utilization caps, role-removal screening, and 10,000-trial simulation. title: A Global Compilation of Blue Whale Strandings
abstract: ABSTRACT Marine mammal strandings are common occurrences that attract public and scientific interest. Stranding data can provide important information for rarely sighted species, but while regional and national stranding databases do exist in some areas, cross‐database communication and data sharing are limited. Here, we present the first global compilation of blue whale ( Balaenoptera musculus ) strandings based on museum specimens, published research, and unpublished verified sources. institutions: NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service Southwest Fisheries Science Center

title: Aqueous extract of Nasturtium officinale: a potential therapeutic approach to be explored in the fight against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: The rise in global bacterial resistance has made the development of new therapies an urgent challenge, positioning Pseudomonas aeruginosa as a critical priority pathogen. In this context, phytotherapy stands out due to the wide diversity of bioactive compounds with antimicrobial potential. Thus, the present study evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm efficacy of an aqueous watercress ( Nasturtium officinale ) extract against eight P. aeruginosa strains (one ATCC standard strain and seven multidrug-resistant clinical isolates), in addition to assessing its cytotoxicity in human keratinocy
journal: Journal of the Iranian Chemical Society
institutions: First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University

title: Benchmarking energy efficiency and regulatory compliance of ferries: a fleet-scale EEXI and EEDI assessment
abstract: The maritime industry is under increasing pressure to improve energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. This challenge is particularly significant for ferries, which operate close to ports and densely populated coastal areas. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) has introduced the Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) and the Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) as key technical measures for improving the energy performance of new and existing ships. This paper presents a comprehensive assessment of the energy efficiency of a fleet of 776 ferries, representing one
institutions: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Naval Architecture in Zagreb

title: Biomechanics and composition of fixed neurocranial tessellated cartilage from the neurocranium of four mobulid ray species with different depth ranges
abstract: Mobulidae are large filter-feeding cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes) that migrate in the world's oceans. However, how their skeletal tissues have adapted to varying environments remains poorly understood. In this study, skeletal adaptations were investigated in four devil rays (Mobulidae), inhabiting various depth ranges from the surface (Mobula eregoodoo 0-50 m, Mobula thurstoni 0-100 m) to deeper water (Mobula mobular 0-1112 m, Mobula tarapacana 0-1896 m). journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
institutions: Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces

title: An updated census of southern elephant seals Mirounga leonina at South Georgia using satellite imagery
abstract: Historically, South Georgia supported the largest breeding population of southern elephant seals Mirounga leonina globally. Yet since 1995, this population has remained largely unassessed and was presumed to be stable. Here, we provide an updated assessment of this sub-Antarctic population and demonstrate the application of sub-meter resolution satellite imagery as a valuable approach for censusing an extensive, remote, and challenging breeding population. title: Floristic diversity, vegetation structure and GIS based taxonomic analysis of the Zagatala State nature reserve (Azerbaijan)
abstract: This article presents the results of floristic, geobotanical, systematic and ecological studies conducted during expeditions to the Zagatala State Nature Reserve and surrounding areas in 2022-2025, along with a GIS-based analysis of these results.The investigation of species composition in the study areas allowed for the assessment of current floral biodiversity, revealing a total of 1109 species of higher spore-bearing, gymnosperm, and flowering plants belonging to 505 genera and 112 families.The total species richness recorded in this study (1109 species) is higher than previous reports from

title: Unravelling the magma source and plumbing systems beneath the submarine volcanoes of Bransfield Strait (Antarctica) with stable and noble gas isotopes
abstract: Abstract Oxygen and hydrogen isotope geochemistry, together with helium, neon and argon isotope systematics, are powerful tools for tracing magma sources and magma plumbing system processes beneath volcanic systems. Characterising them is crucial for understanding volcanic systems behaviour and improving volcanic hazard assessment. title: Influence of the western Pacific warm pool and East Asian climate on late Holocene typhoon activities affecting Taiwan
abstract: Reconstructing paleo-typhoon activity in East Asia is essential for understanding long-term changes in cyclone frequency and intensity under ongoing anthropogenic warming. This study investigates high-resolution laminated sediments from Core MD18-3574, retrieved from the western levee of the Gaoping submarine canyon (southern Taiwan), using hyperspectral imaging, XRF core scanning, grain-size analysis, bulk mineralogy, and radiocarbon dating to reconstruct typhoon events over the past 4200 years. title: Mercury cycling during the last glacial period in Arctic Lake El'gygytgyn, NE Russia
abstract: ABSTRACT Tectonic processes play a key role in the global mercury (Hg) cycle on geological timescales, by mobilising Hg from deep Earth reservoirs to the surface. These natural fluxes also introduce a dynamic component to the terrestrial Hg cycle that can interact with other environmental signals and influence Hg delivery to sedimentary records. For records extracted from tectonically active regions, this could complicate, obscure or even preclude accurate interpretation of sedimentary Hg responses to past centennial‐ to millennial‐scale environmental shifts. title: Extreme challenges in the coldest continent: 10 years of Antarctic adventure sport tourism (2014–2024), participation trends and qualitative risk analysis
abstract: Abstract Adventure tourism in Antarctica has expanded significantly over the past couple of decades and has brought along new challenges for managing human and environmental safety in one of the world’s most remote regions. This study provides a retrospective qualitative analysis of participation in and associated risks with adventure sport tourism activities conducted between 2014 and 2024, using data obtained from the International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators (IAATO). Activities examined include kayaking, polar plunges, scuba diving, mountaineering, skiing and endurance events.

title: Flight altitudes and the use of uplifts by adult lesser spotted eagles, Clanga pomarina, during postbreeding migration
abstract: We analysed 13 postbreeding migration tracks from five adult lesser spotted eagles using high-frequency GPS data. We focused on flight altitude and the use of thermals and orographic uplifts across diverse terrains from northern Germany to Lake Tanganyika. Climbing phases were associated with lower, and gliding phases with higher, ground speeds. The eagles exhibited obligate diurnal migration, with altitudes and speeds peaking around noon, consistent with solar radiation patterns. title: Operational management of Nile water intakes: assessing safe submergence against ship and wind-induced vortexing
abstract: Water intakes in navigable rivers like the Nile face significant risks of air-entraining vortices due to ship- and wind-induced surface fluctuations, which conventional static submergence criteria fail to address. This study evaluates these dynamic effects and develops an integrated framework for determining Safe Minimum Submergence Depth (SMSD) in the Aswan-Esna reach (158 cross-sections). title: Two new and unusual species of the genus Fauveliopsis (Annelida: Fauveliopsidae) and first records in coralline environments from the Alacranes Reef National Park, southern Gulf of Mexico
abstract: Fauveliopsidae are a family of small polychaetes, found across bathyal or abyssal bottoms in low abundance, with their occurrence in shallow waters very uncommon. However, examining polychaetes from dead coralline fragments collected at Alacranes Reef National Park in very shallow waters (0.5–1 m depth), we came upon two unusual fauveliopsids, whose morphological characteristics did not match any described species, while also differing significantly from one another. title: South Atlantic range extensions of the caridean shrimps Synalpheus pandionis Coutière, 1909 (Alpheidae) and Periclimenaeus perlatus (Boone, 1930) (Palaemonidae), identified using an integrative taxonomic approach
abstract: We report range extensions for two species of caridean shrimp, Synalpheus pandionis Coutière, 1909 and Periclimenaeus perlatus (Boone, 1930), from the continental shelf off Bahia, Brazil. These records represent the southernmost occurrences for both species in the south-western Atlantic. Synalpheus pandionis was found associated with the sponge Mycale ( Zygomycale ) angulosa (Duchassaing & Michelotti, 1864), while P. perlatus was found associated with the sponge Aplysina fistularis (Pallas, 1766). title: Do we need a Noah’s Ark to innovate? The value of biodiversity sampling for biomimetics and bioinspiration
abstract: Bioinspiration and biomimetics rely on biological diversity to generate novel design solutions, yet research remains heavily biased toward a small number of well-studied model organisms, often limiting innovation to incremental advances. A major challenge lies in determining how much biodiversity must be sampled to effectively capture the range of morphologies relevant to biological function and extract design principles. title: Mercury in Fish from Guanabara Bay, Southeast Brazil: Tissue-Specific Accumulation and Human Health Risks
abstract: Abstract Guanabara Bay is Brazil’s second-largest bay and has a long history of intense industrial and domestic pollution. Some local communities rely on fish as a primary protein source, justifying an assessment of mercury (Hg) contamination. This study determined total mercury (THg) concentrations in nine fish species and evaluated the toxicological risks associated with human consumption. title: İnsansız Deniz Araçları ve Savaşın Değişen Doğası: Modern Dönemde Deniz Operasyonlarının Teknolojik Dönüşümü
abstract: Teknolojik gelişmelerin 21. yüzyılda kaydettiği ilerleme modern savaş ortamı ve silahlanma yarışı gibi alanlar üzerinde gözlemlenebilir değişimler yaratmaktadır. Bu süreçte yapay zekâ, makine öğrenimi ve diğer modern teknolojilerin güvenlik sektöründe kullanımının yaygınlaşması bir taraftan askeri silah sistemlerinin kabiliyetini artırırken, diğer taraftan kara, hava ve deniz alanlarındaki operasyonel verimliliği ileri boyuta taşımaktadır. journal: Akdeniz Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi

title: Quantum game-theoretic reinforcement learning for autonomous vehicle navigation and communication in vehicular networks
abstract: Abstract Autonomous vehicle (AV) navigation and communication in highly dynamic vehicular networks require fast decision-making, reliable coordination, and energy-efficient connectivity. However, traditional Reinforcement Learning (RL) and game-theoretic approaches often suffer from slow convergence and limited scalability in dense multi-agent environments. title: An annotated district-wise account of Odonata (Dragonflies and Damselflies) from Uttarakhand, India
abstract: This study presents a list of 135 odonate species recorded from Uttarakhand, based on an extensive and critical review of published literature. Notes on the present status of some recorded taxa are included. The documented diversity includes 15 families and 73 genera, comprising 84 species of Anisoptera and 51 species of Zygoptera. Among the districts, Dehradun has the highest recorded species richness, followed by Nainital and Pauri Garhwal. Five species recorded are endemic to India. title: Structural attributes of dominant seagrass species modulate invertebrate assemblages within the Shark Bay world Heritage Area
abstract: Abstract The structural complexity of seagrass meadows plays a central role in shaping the diversity and composition of associated invertebrate assemblages. In the Shark Bay World Heritage Area of Western Australia, the dominant species Amphibolis antarctica and Posidonia australis differ markedly in their above- and below-ground morphology, yet the invertebrate assemblages they support remain poorly characterised. institutions: Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions
Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

title: Displacement and the Reshaping of Indigenous Livelihoods: A Review of the Literature on Mumbai’s Koli and Agri Communities
abstract: The Koli and Agri communities have occupied a visibly glaring space in the landscape of Mumbai since time immemorial.They have made their presence felt not only demographically, but also culturally and politically.However, despite being the city's age-old inhabitants and landowners, both communities have been pushed to the margins for various reasons.From facing a serious bout of identity crisis to being introduced to other religions, the Koli and Agri communities are plagued with a whole host of problems.As a permanent solution to these problems and also for a sense of security, the two commu

title: Thermoeconomic optimization of an ORC system utilizing main engine and cargo oil pump turbine heat
abstract: This study presents a thermoeconomic analysis and a genetic algorithm (GA)-based optimization of a dual-mode Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) system employing R1233zd(E) as the working fluid, designed for waste heat recovery aboard a 116,000 deadweight tonnage (DWT) tanker vessel. The system harnesses waste heat from two distinct operational phases: the main engine during navigation and the cargo oil pump turbines (COPTs) during cargo discharge, a configuration rarely explored in the existing literature. title: Western Writings on Ottoman Algeria: Between Historical Documentation, Ideological Bias, and Military Intelligence
abstract: This paper investigates Western writings on Ottoman Algeria as more than mere historical documentation.The records left behind by consuls, diplomats, captives, clergymen, travelers and intelligence agents form a rich and diverse body of texts that, despite this diversity, converges on a single common purpose: gathering strategic intelligence that paved the way for the French invasion of Algeria in 1830.The research rests on four main axes: a typology of Western authors and their backgrounds; the writing techniques used by these authors and their sources of knowledge; the political, religious,

title: Evolutions of Non‐oxygenated Compounds in Sunlit Subarctic Thermokarst Pond Surface Waters
abstract: Abstract With global climate change, ground subsidence caused by permafrost thawing leads to the formation of thermokarst ponds, where organics from eroding permafrost accumulate in part as dissolved organic matter (DOM). Surface waters were collected from two subarctic thermokarst ponds with distinct characteristics: one palsa‐affected pond, which is organic‐rich, and another lithalsa‐affected pond, which is organic‐poor. title: Moho mission to the foundations of continents: the ICDP DIVE drilling project in the Ivrea-Verbano Zone, Alps, Italy
abstract: Drilling has made it possible to explore the Earth’s interior, but still only to very shallow depths on the scale of the planet. Since 1960s, scientists have worked to reach the crust–mantle boundary known as the Moho. This boundary representing the foundations of continents is usually beyond the reach of our present-day technology. However, in some places on Earth, it is possible to reach the crust–mantle frontier without drilling to its original depth. title: First record of Terpsinoë musica Ehrenberg (Bacillariophyta) from Uganda and South Africa
abstract: African records of Terpsinoë musica Ehrenberg are scarce and mainly restricted to North and West Africa, with previous East African reports limited to Ethiopia and fossil material from Kenya. Here, we extend the geographic distribution of this species in Africa by including two new observations in East and Southern Africa: the first observation of the species in Uganda (East Africa) was in the guts of Oreochromis leucostictus collected from Lake George. institutions: South African Institute for Aquatic Biodiversity

title: A novel numerical approach to the study of riverbed morphometric and hydrological characteristics
abstract: Reliable prediction of riverbed evolution remains limited by the lack of high‑resolution morphometric data, especially for large rivers flowing through easily erodible soils. This study develops and implements a comprehensive numerical framework designed to reconstruct detailed riverbed geometry by combining multi‑source field and remotely sensed datasets. title: Scientific Research as Geopolitical Practice: Innovation, Diplomacy, Subversion
abstract: This article examines scientific research as a geopolitical practice. Drawing from IR literature on innovation in geopolitics, scholarship on science diplomacy and hybrid warfare theory, the article suggests that scientific research is best understood as a practice that simultaneously aims at furthering the national interest and at tackling global challenges through diplomatic means. title: Heavy metals in raw cow, goat and sheep milk: Associated dietary exposure and human health risk assessment in eastern Algeria
abstract: In recent years, the presence of heavy metals in milk has emerged as an important public health issue, owing to their potential detrimental effects on milk quality.The present study aimed to assess the occurrence and levels of heavy metals in raw cow, goat, and sheep milk obtained from eastern Algeria.Sixty milk samples were analysed for Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni and Fe using atomic absorption spectrometry.Results demonstrated that Fe (5.49 ± 21.93) was the dominant metal in cow milk, followed by Cu (0.86 ± 0.02) and Cr (0.56 ± 0.05).In goat milk, Fe (9.77 ± 0.69) and Cu (2.79 ± 0.04) were highest, while

title: Look-up tables for complex refractive index correction of particle sizes measured by common research-grade optical particle counters
abstract: Optical particle counters (OPCs) are widely used to measure the aerosol particle number size distribution over a large size range encompassing sub- and super-micron diameters. The measurement principle of OPCs is based on the dependence of light scattering on particle size. However, this dependence is not monotonic at all sizes as light scattering also depends on the particle composition (i.e., the complex refractive index, m ) and morphology. title: ‘My Single True Activity’: Sinéad Morrissey’s Found Architecture and Self-Conscious Ecopoetics
abstract: In this article, I will closely read Northern Irish poet Sinéad Morrissey’s more recent work to articulate a ‘found architectural’ mode of poetic attention. Her intricately formal poetry explores its own potential as an ecopoesis or ‘housebuilding’, self-consciously addressing climate catastrophe in ironising domestic registers and typographies. I argue that poems like ‘Found Architecture’, ‘Meteor Shower’ and ‘The Italian Chapel’ foreground the limits and complications of human-made artifice in the context of the overwhelming threat of environmental collapse. title: Recent Progress in Chinese Cyclostratigraphy and Its Earth System Science Implications
abstract: Cyclostratigraphy has made significant progress in China in interpreting deep-time sedimentary records, astronomical chronology modeling, and energy exploration applications, providing critical support for Earth system science research. title: Maritime decarbonization of shipping and ports: A system-oriented review of coordination, sequencing, and transition pathways
abstract: Decarbonization of global shipping and maritime ports has become a strategic priority for achieving international climate targets. Although research has expanded rapidly, existing reviews predominantly examine technological, operational, or policy dimensions separately, providing limited understanding of how interactions among vessels, ports, fuel infrastructure, and governance shape decarbonization pathways. abstract: ABSTRACT Legacy wells represent a critical consideration for offshore CO 2 storage projects, as they may provide potential pathways for fluid or gas migration if poorly constructed, undocumented or inadequately abandoned. Systematically assessing large numbers of legacy wells remains challenging due to heterogeneous data availability and the diversity of existing evaluation approaches. title: Aligning risk frameworks with fieldwork realities: extending Rasmussen’s model to scientific research settings
abstract: Scientific fieldwork is an essential component of research across many academic disciplines. Fieldwork entails numerous risks, ranging from interpersonal to environmental risks, and can often result in physical and mental injury or illness. Despite these potential harms, standardized frameworks for understanding, managing, and responding to incidents in fieldwork remain underdeveloped. abstract: This paper presents a systematic review of ship energy efficiency improvement and emission reduction technologies. Framed within the regulatory framework established by the IMO namely EEDI, EEXI, and CII the study analyzes ship energy consumption structures, emission characteristics, and compliance requirements. abstract: The wings of waterborne ground effect vehicles experience transition from submerged operation during takeoff to airborne flight near the free surface. abstract: Anadromous fishes experience different locomotory demands throughout their life cycle. We evaluated how functional locomotory traits change over ontogeny in anadromous Alosa pseudoharengus (Alewife). We found that as juveniles, a period in which predator avoidance, food acquisition and manoeuvring in complex environments are critical to survival, Alewife have traits conducive to higher turning performance. abstract: Abstract Cities are increasingly vulnerable to the intensifying effects of climate change, particularly in the form of heatwaves and the phenomenon of urban heat islands. abstract: Probing tasks in complex and unknown working environments are placing increasingly demanding requirements on robots in terms of terrain adaptability and locomotion agility. abstract: This article examines how the topography of Eastern Anatolia was described, named and given meaning in ancient sources, arguing that its mountains, valleys and river systems functioned less as a physical backdrop than as an active component of political strategy, imperial ideology and the construction of local identity and memory. In this study, we combine satellite-derived column concentrations, ground-based observations, flux diagnostics, and forward trajectory analysis to evaluate the cross-boundary transport responses of NO₂ and CO over southeastern Australia. abstract: Abstract This study re-evaluates the “dual city” model through the case of the VOC’s Zeelandia in the seventeenth century. title: Post-2020 conservation priorities are threatened by global mining
abstract: Abstract The United Nations has committed to halting and reversing biodiversity loss by 2030. Despite this commitment, mining remains a major driver of biodiversity decline, particularly in conservation priority zones (CPZs) and areas with high species extinction risk. Regardless of growing awareness, the full extent of current and future mining threats to biodiversity remains inadequately quantified, limiting effective global conservation strategies. title: From one tree to the canopy: an evolutionary design trajectory for tethered robotics in forest environments
abstract: Forest robotics has largely evolved along a ground-first and flight-dominant trajectory, treating the canopy as a region to observe or briefly access rather than a habitat to inhabit. In this Perspective, we propose an alternative canopy-first framework in which robots operate through anchoring, suspension, and tension-mediated interaction with the environment. title: The nature of science in Finnish primary school textbooks
abstract: Recent international assessments indicate a decline in Finnish students’ interest and performance in science, emphasising the need for more relevant and motivating science education. Including the nature of science (NOS) into teaching offers an approach to address this issue as NOS instruction has been shown to enhance students’ interest in science, challenge stereotypical images of scientists, and promote a more realistic understanding of scientific practices and processes. title: Analysis of the main mechanisms of ship hull degradation: synergistics, modeling, and monitoring methods
abstract: Corrosion wastage, fatigue damage and crack formation are the main mechanisms of degradation of ship hull structures. Their combined action leads to an accelerated reduction in load‑bearing capacity and complicates the prediction of residual life. abstract: In this paper, we calculate the two-sided (consumer and producer) market accessibility of the Greek islands, based on different measures of transport cost, namely, the actual network distance and the freight shipment cost from/to mainland regions and between them. abstract: Obese tourists represent a growing yet underexamined market segment whose decision-making processes remain insufficiently understood within tourism development research. This study investigates the psychological and experiential factors shaping obese tourists’ travel intentions by integrating social identity and complexity theories. abstract: In the early 20th century, Go Jae-hyung authored Simdogihaeng, a travelogue focusing on Ganghwa Island. This study explores the narratives in Simdogihaeng, leveraging theories of cognition and literature as its theoretical foundation. It defines “recognition” in narrative contexts through the lens of epistemology. title: Design and Stability Analysis of an Aerosonde UAV Using Linear Quadratic Regulator Control
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly important in surveillance, environmental monitoring, mapping, and scientific research, where flight stability and control performance are essential for safe and reliable operation. This study focuses on the modeling and stability analysis of an Aerosonde UAV using a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) control approach. title: Policy responses to overtourism
abstract: Overtourism has emerged as one of the most debated challenges affecting major tourist destinations, with Italy frequently cited as a prominent case. This paper examines the policy responses to overtourism in Italy, focusing on how institutional arrangements, interest groups, and public discourse shape the management of tourism growth. Drawing on existing literature and emblematic cases - most notably Venice and Florence - the study argues that overtourism cannot be understood solely as the outcome of excessive visitor numbers. abstract: Abstract The first clear evidence of advanced dairy production in the Southern Levant emerges during the Late Chalcolithic period. This shift is marked by the widespread discovery of clay churns across diverse geographic regions, alongside herd management practices and organic residue analyses that point to a dairy-oriented economy. title: An integrated AHP-DEMATEL-QFD-FBS framework for designing an in-carriage intelligent delivery cart for China’s high-speed rail
abstract: To address the problem that manual delivery services cannot adequately meet the needs of complex service scenarios in crowded high-speed rail cars in China, this study proposes an integrated design framework for in-carriage intelligent delivery carts. User needs were collected through questionnaire surveys, semi-structured interviews, and behavioral observation, and a need indicator system for high-speed rail in-carriage delivery services was constructed. AHP was used to calculate the initial weights of need indicators, and DEMATEL was applied to revise the interrelationships among indicators.

title: WARDING OFF A ROMAN INVASION IN AETHIOPIA (UPPER NUBIA) WITH TALL ELEPHANT TALES? REVISITING PLINY, NATURALIS HISTORIA 6.186
abstract: Abstract It has recently been suggested that the Romans baulked at the idea of expanding their empire beyond Egypt into Aethiopia (Upper Nubia) during the principate of Nero because they were tricked into thinking that a powerful army equipped with war elephants awaited them. This discussion aims to demonstrate that such a view, based on a minority reading of Pliny, HN 6.186 that plumps for 3,000 elephants once being stationed on the island of Meroë, is difficult to support on both textual and contextual grounds.

title: Boycotting racial capitalism
abstract: This article explores how racial capitalism in colonial Ireland was successfully challenged through the world’s first ever boycott. In the political economy of the late nineteenth-century, race and class were mutually constituted. The colonial landholding system of Ireland was a peripheral part of the British Empire. Catholic Irish tenants were cast as an inferior Celtic race in opposition to superior Anglo-Saxon Protestant English landlords. title: Rethinking “Dead” Objects: Baya Pandang and the Cultural Lives of Iban Artifacts in Sarawak Museum Collections
abstract: Museums are among the most important institutions safeguarding indigenous cultural heritage. However, their colonial institutional origins have often obscured the original uses, values, and meanings that cultural materials hold for the indigenous communities who created and continue to claim them. This study examines three Iban cultural objects held in the Sarawak Museum that are widely assumed, within a Western museological frame, to have lost their significance once removed from their original cultural and social context. Drawing on Iban epistemology, and specifically the concept of baya pan

title: Un oracional del siglo xv en aljamía hebraicoaragonesa: textos y vocabulario
abstract: The following pages present the transcription of a small corpus of texts in Hebrew-Aragonese aljamía, datable to the last third of the fifteenth century. These texts appear to have originally formed part of a prayer book intended for women. An appended vocabulary is included as an accompanying resource.

title: Термокарст и сукцессии растительных сообществ в бассейне р. Большой Хомус-Юрях в позднем плейстоцене и голоцене, Колымская низменность
abstract: Thermokarst lakes exert a significant influence on the formation of the Kolyma Lowland relief, affecting the high-ice sediments of the yedoma. Thawing and compaction of the ice complex result in the formation of taberal sediments. An outcrop of lacustrine and taberal sediments (31 m) is traced on the right bank of the Bolshoy Khomus-Yuryakh River. The discovery of a mammoth skull, with tusks preserved in the alveoli, in lacustrine sediments dated to >49,000 years ago, and palynological data permit to distinguish pollen zones of isotope stages (MIS) 5, 4, and 3. journal: Bulletin of the North-East Science Center

title: Proposal for defining the severity of environmental hypoxia
abstract: Every day, millions of people are exposed to environmental hypoxia, primarily due to living at or travelling to high altitudes for reasons such as work, tourism, business, or sports, e.g., mountaineering. Furthermore, hypoxic exposure at low altitudes (e.g., in hypoxia rooms or tents) is increasingly being used to pre-acclimatize individuals to high altitudes for activities such as athletic training, trekking and high-altitude climbing, as well as for preventive and therapeutic purposes. Especially for these applications a clear definition of environmental hypoxia severity is lacking, impeding

title: Mitigating the human link in emerging reptile fungal pathogen transmission
abstract: Handling wild reptiles is common among amateur herpetology enthusiasts, professional researchers, social media influencers, and photographers. However, the potential for these interactions to spread diseases that threaten wild reptiles remains underappreciated. With the rise in such interactions due to today's socially connected landscape and the offering of an increased number of wildlife-focused ecotourism trips, the possibility of increased spread of human-vector-mediated reptile diseases is substantial. This spread is a concern, especially for novel and emerging potentially catastrophic fu

title: Tourism opportunities created by COVID-19 pandemic in Vhembe District Municipality, Limpopo Province, South Africa
abstract: Like all other forms of pervasive disruption, COVID-19 disrupted the world's economic and social systems, while creating opportunities for some and devastating threats for others.The South African economy, through the tourism sector, was highly affected.This paper, therefore, investigated the opportunities created by the COVID-19 pandemic in the tourism sector, with a focus on South Africa's Limpopo Province, specifically the Vhembe District Municipality.The study employed quantitative methods supported by a descriptive research design.For this study, a survey questionnaire was distributed to

title: A Design of Relief Logistics System by Axioms
abstract: Aim: This study scientifically addresses aid logistics operations, a subfield related to disaster management. It aims to conduct a design study that will guide those in authority. The study is in line with the classical logistics flow, with a value-oriented lean perspective, and eliminates processes that are not beneficial to disaster victims and include waste. The application of the axiomatic design approach in logistics, particularly in relief logistics, is relatively new and is expected to contribute to the existing literature gap in this area.Method: This study presented a complete, separa
journal: İstanbul Gelişim Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Dergisi

title: Sociodemographic Analysis of the Art District in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico
abstract: This study presents a socioeconomic and demographic analysis of the Art District in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico, examining its role as a contributor to local economic and cultural development within the creative industries. Through the assessment of demographic variables and economic indicators, the principal enterprises and stakeholders of the district are identified, highlighting their role as a local economic engine. The analysis applies the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) — with focus on class 466313, retail of antiques and artworks — to characterize the sector a

title: Mineralogy of gold-telluride-sulfide ores of the Kokkiya deposit, Kazakhstan
abstract: Purpose. To establish the mineral-formforming sequence and clarify the features of gold-telluride-sulfide mineralization at the Kokkiya deposit based on the study of mineral assemblages, typomorphic characteristics of ore minerals, modes of occurrence of native gold and tellurides, and their spatial and paragenetic relationships. Methods. A total of 120 ore and host-rock samples collected from drill core were studied. The analytical methods included optical microscopy in reflected and transmitted light, scanning electron microscopy, electron-probe microanalysis, EDS/WDS analysis, and EDS mappi
institutions: "Institute of Metallurgy and Ore Beneficiation" JSC

title: Characterization of recombinase-based genetic parts and circuits using nanopore sequencing
abstract: Abstract Recombinases are versatile enzymes able to perform the precise insertion, deletion, and rearrangement of DNA and can act as a foundation for programmable genetic logic and memory. Crucial for their use are accurate measurements of function. However, these are often laborious, time-consuming, and costly to collect. To address this, we develop a semi-automated workflow that combines low-cost liquid handling robotics, multiplexed long-read nanopore sequencing, and a supporting computational analysis tool to enable the high-throughput and detailed characterization of recombinase parts and

title: Global warming of the troposphere vs global cooling of the thermosphere
abstract: Signs of anthropogenic pressure on the atmosphere in the form of global warming of its surface layers were noticed as early as the end of the 19th century. And the first facts indicating global cooling of the meso-thermosphere were identified at the end of the 20th century. The phenomenon was formulated in 1998 in the form of the concept “Cooling and sinking of the middle and upper atmosphere”. It is an alternative to the RDR model, which is based on the hypothesis of a twofold increase in the atmospheric carbon dioxide content, as it is categorically unable to explain the entire spectrum of o
institutions: Institute of Terrestrial Magnetism Ionosphere and Radio Wave Propagation

title: Carbon offset-aware economic scheduling using echo state enhanced variational mode decomposition and ARIMA forecasting for P2X-based city energy ecosystems with joint green-carbon certificate and socio-financial welfare
abstract: Urban energy systems in sustainable cities are facing increasing challenges due to the simultaneous integration of hydrogen-based conversion, carbon regulation, renewable energy uncertainty, and emerging electric mobility demands. This paper develops a low-carbon optimization framework for a Multi-Energy Distribution Network that coordinates electricity, gas, heat, and hydrogen infrastructures while incorporating Power-to-X technologies, hydrogen-enriched gas utilization, carbon capture, and aerial electric mobility. The proposed framework integrates ADTAN-driven Electric Taxi Drone demand mod

title: Landmark-aware visual localization for GNSS-denied UAV wind farm inspection via lifecycle binding and adaptive fusion
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a lightweight landmark-aware visual localization framework intended as a backup localization subsystem for UAV inspection in GNSS-denied wind farms. The system utilizes wind turbine towers as natural semantic beacons and integrates YOLOv12s and BoT-SORT for real-time detection and robust tracking. Absolute pose estimation is achieved via a bbox-based 2.5-D image–altimeter geometry model, a landmark binding lifecycle management strategy (LBL), and an adaptive spatio-temporal weighted fusion algorithm (ASTW). In five repeated RflySim trials, the combined framework ac

title: Women in Geosciences: an overview
abstract: This article examines the evolving role of women geoscientists, highlighting both progress and persistent inequalities that continue to shape this discipline. Although women now account for approximately 40% of researchers worldwide, their representation in Geosciences remains uneven, particularly in senior academic, leadership and decision-making positions. Data from the United States, Europe and at country level consistently reveal a pronounced “leaky pipeline,” whereby female representation declines progressively beyond the PhD stage, often falling below 20% among full professors. journal: JOURNAL OF GEOETHICS AND SOCIAL GEOSCIENCES

title: Entwining sound, space and narratives. Sound design approaches in exhibitions
abstract: This article explores the evolution of exhibition design, focusing on the integration of sound as a key narrative and experiential element. In recent decades, technological advances and discoveries in neuroscience have influenced the design of exhibition spaces, transforming them into multimodal experiences that go beyond mere visual engagement. Sound emerges as a central tool, capable of shaping the emotional, spatial, and narrative dimensions of exhibitions. Through case studies and interviews with exhibition and sound designers, I propose four sound design approaches – transparent, relation
journal: Museum Materials and Discussions Journal of Museum Studies

title: Multilevel risks and war related crisis severity shape tourist psychological distress and responses to crisis management
abstract: War-related crises exacerbate fear, insecurity, risk, and emotional tension. In light of these conditions, we propose and test a novel framework applying stress mindset theory to a war-crisis setting. Specifically, we investigate the effects of multilevel risks (personal, travel, and destination) on tourists’ psychological distress and subsequent emotional exhaustion. Furthermore, we examine the effects of emotional exhaustion on travel withdrawal intentions and travel choice satisfaction, while evaluating the moderating boundary effects of perceived crisis severity and crisis management. Prague University of Economics and Business

title: DISTURBING THE HEARTH: ARISTARCHUS’ HELIOCENTRIC UNIVERSE AS COURT PARRHÊSIA
abstract: Abstract Aristarchus of Samos’ heliocentric model of the universe has usually been treated by modern scholars as an astronomical controversy somehow removed from the ideological concerns of the Ptolemaic court in which it was produced. This traditional approach has not fully accounted for the contemporary reception of the astronomer’s work, which included accusations of disruption, and even impiety, by scholarly rivals. title: Auto‐Tuning Weights Model Predictive Control for Three‐State Switching Cell Boost Converters
abstract: ABSTRACT This work presents an improved robust model predictive control (MPC) for DC‐DC boost converters operating under polytopic uncertainty. The proposed controller guarantees constraint satisfaction for voltage, current, and duty cycle bounds while ensuring asymptotic stability through a common quadratic Lyapunov function. To circumvent the computational complexity of online optimization, the control law is synthesized offline via semidefinite programming (SDP) using linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), yielding a static state‐feedback gain. title: Globalization and the Underdevelopment of Africa: A Critical Analysis
abstract: The intensification of global social, political, economic and cultural relationships has brought positive gains for some parts of the world, but this cannot be said of all countries and regions of the world. Many countries in the Global South have not had a fair share of the benefits of globalization due to the exploitative activities of the developed countries and their control over international organizations. These exploitative and hegemonic actions have resulted in the direct and indirect underdevelopment of African countries. The article therefore delves into the conceptual analysis of gl

title: One new obligate commensal species of Coenaletes (Collembola, Coenaletidae) from the hermit crab Coenobita compressus (Crustacea, Coenobitidae) from Colombia
abstract: A new species of Coenaletes associated with the hermit crab Coenobita compressus H. Milne-Edwards, 1836, living in shells of Tegula atra Lesson, 1830 (Gastropoda: Tegulidae) on the seashores of Chocó, Colombia, is described and illustrated. The ontogenetic development, including measurements and ventral setation from first instar to adult, is provided. A key for the identification of the three species known in the genus is included.

title: A Spatial Database of Historical Fire in Westside Forests of the Pacific Northwest
abstract: Recent fire activity across forests west of the Cascade Crest in Oregon and Washington (the “westside”) has increased interest in the region's historical fire regimes. Substantial spatial information exists describing the location, extent, and timing of historical fires in the region, but these records represent independent efforts at local-to-regional scales, with considerable variation in data resolution, methodologies, discoverability, and metadata. To address the need for a systematic dataset of historical westside fire, we compiled a spatial database of over 7,300 fire perimeters and burn
institutions: Western Wildland Environmental Threat Assessment Center

title: Validação de modelo de análise da gastronomia como vetor de identidade cultural e desenvolvimento sustentável em cidades turísticas
abstract: "This study analyses gastronomy as a vector of cultural identity and sustainable development in tourist cities through a comparison between Juazeiro do Norte, Brazil, and Santiago de Compostela, Spain. The objective was to examine how residents and tourists perceive local gastronomic spaces across dimensions elated to hospitality, authenticity, affective memory, accessibility, and sustainability. This quantitative, descriptive, and comparative study drew on 625 structured questionnaires administered in gastronomic spaces, with 311 collected in Brazil and 314 in Spain. journal: PASOS Revista de Turismo y Patrimonio Cultural

title: Challenges of Goronyo Dam in the Agricultural Activities in Sokoto State 1984 -2025: From Historical Perspectives
abstract: Although the challenges encountered due to the Goronyo Dam disaster have caused agricultural backwardness, socio-economic and environmental effects in the area of study are worthy of discussion, therefore, this paper seeks to examine the nature and magnitude of the soil erosion, flooding, among others which is the major factor in this content. Also, identify the real causes of these and a historical review of the challenges of Goronyo Dam in agricultural activities in Sokoto State and other Dams as well. The paper has also examined the damages and changes it has coursed on vegetation covers, a
journal: African Journal of History and Archaeology

title: PIRATE FESTIVALS AROUND THE WORLD AND THEIR SIGNIFICANCE FOR LOCAL DEVELOPMENT
abstract: The shift of contemporary tourism toward experiential, cultural, and thematic experiences creates new opportunities for destinations seeking differentiation, an extension of the tourism season, and stronger local entrepreneurship. In this context, pirate festivals constitute a distinctive form of event tourism because they combine historical or mythological narratives, harbour landscapes, re-enactments, parades, music, and participatory entertainment. This article examines three international pirate festivals—Pirates Week in the Cayman Islands, the Gasparilla Pirate Festival in Tampa, and the
journal: Global Journal of Engineering and Technology Advances
institutions: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

title: Undisciplining service design: Towards a grammar of possibility
abstract: Despite its ambitions to transform service systems, service design has been critiqued for reproducing the status quo and normalizing others into dominant social expectations. To move away from the circulation of hegemonic structures, the service design discipline needs to be challenged. Drawing on queer theory, this paper explores how service design can be undisciplined to create a grammar of possibility for making service systems otherwise. Based on experiences from an experimental seven-week service design research and education collaboration with hospital-based mental health services in Nor
institutions: Oslo School of Architecture and Design

title: Biomorphology, transformation, and differentiation of joints and digits of the limbs in vertebrates
abstract: The study of morphogenesis, differentiation, and transformation of joints and digits of the vertebrate limbs is a fundamental task of comparative and veterinary anatomy, which can be directly integrated into the practice of clinical surgery and orthopedics. In this context, the anatomical and topographical features of the joints and limb autopodia of both extinct and extant vertebrate species are of particular importance. The purpose of this study was to conduct a biomorphological and comparative anatomical analysis of the patterns of evolutionary transformation, differentiation and muscular a

title: Books on the Road: Experiences of Reading in Robert Lee’s Travel Journal, 1824–1826
abstract: This article considers the reading life of the early-nineteenth-century British traveler and physician, Robert Lee (1793–1877). Drawing on evidence from Lee’s unknown manuscript travel journal penned during his travel to and residence in the Russian Empire in 1824–1826, where he worked as a family physician at Count M. S. Vorontsov’s household, it reconstructs his reading list and discusses the circumstances in which his reading acts took place. title: Efficient Coverage Path Planning via Gradient-Based Rectangular Segmentation
abstract: Coverage Path Planning (CPP) is the task of finding a route that covers every point in a region or volume (i.e., all reachable cells) while avoiding obstacles. A typical CPP solution proceeds in two main stages: partitioning the environment into subregions, and planning a path within and between these regions. Effective segmentation is critical for smooth and efficient operation. For example, dividing the area into rectangular cells allows a simple back-and-forth (boustrophedon) sweep in each cell, exhaustively covering it without overlap. In this paper, we propose an adaptive, gradient-based
journal: Journal of Automation Mobile Robotics & Intelligent Systems

title: Active layer microbial inocula restore missing functions across thawed permafrost soils
abstract: Abstract Microbial dynamics in thawing permafrost induce a climate feedback of uncertain magnitude. Upon thaw, active layer microorganisms may establish in formerly frozen layers and introduce missing functions. Here we test the prevalence of functional limitations and how active layer microorganisms can mitigate these across four widespread permafrost types over 389 days. By restoring functions with a multifunctional microbial community, we demonstrate widespread functional limitations, as increased CO 2 emissions across four permafrost types, and onset N 2 O emissions in two of those. institutions: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

title: Detrás del telón. El motivo visual de la cortina en el cine de David Lynch
abstract: En esta segunda parte, el motivo visual de la cortina se expande más allá de su presencia escénica para convertirse en un mecanismo que altera la percepción del espacio y fractura la identidad en el cine de Lynch. Su función opera como un dispositivo liminar que articula refugio, ilusión y tránsito, donde lo inestable se convierte cada vez más en la norma.

title: Parachiloglanis gurungi, a new species of torrent catfish (Teleostei: Sisoridae) from western Bhutan
abstract: A new species of Parachiloglanis is described, based on specimens collected from the Kalikhola stream, a tributary of the Jaldhaka River, Samtse Dzongkhag, Bhutan. Parachiloglanis gurungi, new species, differs from its congeners in having a white bar on anterior flanks on dorsum of the body, white spot at the upper caudal-peduncle base, short and deep caudal peduncle, long predorsum, and differences in vomerine toothplate shape. title: Behind the facades of Ctesiphon: an archaeometric study of stucco architectural decoration from the Sasanian and Early Islamic periods
abstract: Abstract Ctesiphon, the capital of the Sasanian Empire (ca. 224–651 CE), was a major center of political power and artistic production in Mesopotamia. Excavations conducted in the 1920s–30s by the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and the Metropolitan Museum of Art revealed an extensive corpus of stucco decorations from Sasanian and Early Islamic contexts. Their varied forms, decorative patterns, architectural contexts, and dates of production make these stuccos particularly valuable for comparative study. title: From internal peace to the discourse of holy war: Tracing discursive continuities from the peace of god movement to the letters of Catherine of Siena
abstract: In medieval Latin Christendom, the discourse of peace was not confined to the mitigation of conflict and the prevention of war; rather, it developed into an ideological mechanism that oriented collective energies toward specific purposes. This study investigates how, in Medieval Western Europe, the discourse of peace, initially intended to bring violence to an end, gradually ceased to aim at its complete elimination and was transformed into a politico-religious mechanism that reordered and externalized violence. Within this framework, the study analyzes whether there exists an intellectual and

title: Additions to the flora of Pakistan: three new records in the genera Achillea, Amaranthus and Cicer
abstract: This study is based on field surveys conducted during 2022-2024, during which three vascular plant species were recorded first time for the Flora of Pakistan.The newly recorded species Achillea ptarmica (Asteraceae), Amaranthus polygonoiodes (Amaranthaceae), and Cicer chorassanicum (Fabaceae) are documented here.Achillea ptarmica was collected from Khaplu in Ghanche district of Gilgit-Baltistan and subsequently cultivated in Islamabad for detailed study and identification.Amaranthus polygonoides was collected from the Lower Dir district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Islamabad Capital Territory and C

title: Rediscovery, new records, and conservation assessment of the rare orchids Bletia concolor and B. similis (Orchidaceae) in Michoacán, Mexico
abstract: Background: Bletia comprises 56 species distributed throughout the Americas, with its principal center of diversity in Mexico. Among them are Bletia concolor and B. similis, two rare species for which information on morphology, distribution, and ecology is limited. Neither species had been recorded for the last 13 and 62 years, respectively, since their most recent collections. Questions: How do the new records of Bletia concolor and B. similis contribute to the knowledge of their distribution and to the assessment of their conservation status? Studied species: Bletia concolor and B. similis.
publisher: Sociedad Botánica de México, A. C.

title: Updated checklist of non-psoroptidid Astigmata in China (Acariformes)
abstract: This paper presents a revised checklist cataloging 160 species across 61 genera in 17 families of non-psoroptidid Astigmata known to occur in China. Among these, eight species have been newly documented since the 2010 review, and a further nineteen previously overlooked species have now been incorporated. Furthermore, one erroneous record, Sancassania karnatakaensis (Krishna Rao & Ranganath), has been corrected by its removal. The updated binomial name, Chinese name, and detailed information regarding hosts, distribution, and other relevant data are provided for each species.

title: Colonial memories in landscapes and waterways: the vital materialism of troubling childhood histories
abstract: This article shares a postqualitative, new materialist approach to memory work and storytelling, foregrounding the entangled colonial histories embedded in water and landscape. With its life-giving properties, water is a vital matter through which we can rethink histories to connect with the more-than-human and decolonise ourselves. Using new materialism, we create a watery assemblage (images and text) to challenge our thinking around the colonial histories embedded in the waterscapes. We consider situated epistemologies that emerge through thinking with water, waterways, landscapes, humans, a

title: Distributed Agent-Based Scheduling of Smart Port Operations under Cost and Emissions Constraints
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a distributed, emission-aware scheduling framework for smart port energy management, designed to coordinate heterogeneous flexible electric loads under operational, economic, and environmental constraints. The proposed approach addresses the coordinated scheduling of refrigerated containers (reefers), plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), and shore-to-ship power supply systems, with the objective of reducing total operational cost while satisfying asset-level constraints and ship-level and port-level emission limits. institutions: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

title: A Study of the Expression of Historical View by means of “Minor Characters " in Historical Dramas: An Example Relating to the CCTV Adaptation of “Romance of the Three Kingdoms"
abstract: Among the key media used to form collective memory or to convey historical concepts and the narrative point of view adopted in such dramas it has a direct bearing upon the audience ' s ideas of, and attitude toward, history. The present paper deals with the CCTV adaptation of Romance of the Three Kingdoms as an object of investigation, and considers—among other things—the particular historical outlook embodied by this classic historical drama (as seen) through civilian figures, common soldiers, or helpers .It reports on findings that show that with strict regard for the great narrative of the
journal: Scientific Journal Of Humanities and Social Sciences

title: Techno-Economic Assessment of LOHC-Based Hydrogen Export from Australia to Japan
abstract: Abstract This study develops a corridor-specific techno-economic framework for LOHC-based hydrogen export from Australia to Japan and applies it to four representative carrier systems: toluene/methylcyclohexane (TOL/MCH), dibenzyltoluene/perhydrodibenzyltoluene (H0-DBT/H18-DBT), N-ethylcarbazole/perhydro-N-ethylcarbazole (H0-NEC/H12-NEC), and benzene/cyclohexane (BZ/CH). The framework integrates carrier-specific process simulation, maritime logistics, regional cost assumptions, heat-supply options, and deployability factors within a unified hydrogen-to-hydrogen supply chain boundary. title: From Nahda to Naksa: Some Marxist Perspectives on the Arab National Question
abstract: This article examines the trajectory of Arab nationalism through a Marxist lens, analyzing its historical emergence, political ascendancy, and eventual decline. It posits the Palestinian question as central to the development of Arab nationalist consciousness and anti-imperialist struggle, arguing that the fragmentation of a unified Arab stance reflects broader geopolitical defeats and the consolidation of dependent capitalist relations. The article provides a historical overview of Arab nationalism’s evolution from the intellectual Nahda movement into state ideologies like Nasserism. It then
journal: Agrarian South Journal of Political Economy A triannual Journal of Agrarian South Network and CARES

title: Two new threatened Inversodicraea (Podostemaceae) species from waterfalls in Sierra Leone: I. joulei and I. lebbiei
abstract: Summary Two threatened new species of Podostemaceae belonging to the genus Inversodicraea , I. joulei and I. lebbiei , both from the Republic of Sierra Leone, are described and illustrated. A first record in Sierra Leone of the genus Lestestuella is also reported. Inversodicraea is the most species-rich genus of Podostemaceae in Africa and now comprises 38 species. institutions: International Union for Conservation of Nature

title: Unshackled?: China, the ‘unequal treaties’, and the limits of international law, 1919–1929
abstract: Abstract The post-1919 international order extended to China formal sovereign equality while offering few legal means to exercise it. The Sino-Belgian treaty dispute of 1926–29 reveals this: when China abrogated its 1865 treaty with Belgium and Brussels sued at the Permanent Court of International Justice, the institutions that promised peaceful revision could not deliver it without the consent of the powers whose privileges were at stake. title: A Perspective on the Historical Role and Future of Bactris Gasipaes as a Food Crop
abstract: Peach palm (Bactris gasipaes) is a domesticated perennial of the tropical Americas historically cultivated within Indigenous agroforestry systems. Interdisciplinary evidence indicates that it functioned as a staple in pre-Columbian Amazonia, embedded in diversified, human-managed forests. Despite its nutritional and agronomic potential, modern development efforts have not integrated it into contemporary food economies, largely due to a mismatch with prevailing models based on annual monocultures. Current production focuses on palm heart, while fruit use remains localised. This article argues t

title: From collective action to collective rescue: rethinking distribution and cooperation in climate governance under common peril
abstract: Distributive conflict is central to climate governance but is often treated as an external obstacle to cooperation. This conceptual paper argues that such conflict is partly generated by the dominance of a Collective Action Problem (CAP) cooperation grammar, which frames climate mitigation as managing a shared resource and makes agreement over individual contributions a precondition for action. Once institutionalized, CAP embeds distributive questions into the authorization of action itself, contributing to delay and deadlock. The paper introduces a Common Rescue (CR) cooperation grammar, illu

title: Engaging the public to unveil urban biodiversity: a decade of ant monitoring in Italy
abstract: Abstract Citizen science (CS) has become an increasingly effective approach in biodiversity research, helping to overcome data gaps that are difficult to address through conventional methods. In entomology, CS initiatives have grown significantly, yet ants (Hymenoptera: Formicidae) remain underrepresented, partly due to challenges in species identification. The Italian “School of Ants” (SoA) project aimed to fill this gap by engaging over 6,000 participants from diverse backgrounds between 2012 and 2023 to monitor urban ant diversity across the country. title: Seasonal decoupling of climate and human activity on litter and dung decomposition across the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau
abstract: Abstract In grassland ecosystems of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, litter and dung decomposition are essential for nutrient cycling and productivity. Using remote sensing data, field observations, and machine learning, we examined spatiotemporal patterns of litter decomposition mass (LDM) and dung decomposition mass (DDM) from 2000 to 2020. Both showed increasing trends: during the growing season (GS), LDM rose from 76.1 to 105.8 kg ha-1 and DDM from 16.9 to 26.6 kg ha-1. institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: Royal Idealism in the Achaemenid Persian Empire and Its Iconographic Reflections in Anatolia
abstract: The Persians, who established an empire in the mid-sixth century BCE, came to control a vast portion of the ancient world. Centered in Iran, this imperial formation was governed by the Achaemenid dynasty. Although the Achaemenids adhered to Zoroastrian religious traditions, they also incorporated earlier Mesopotamian ideological and political models—particularly those of the Assyrian Empire—into their imperial discourse and legitimizing strategies. In this context, Persian rulers did not hesitate to represent themselves and their political actions in ways reminiscent of Assyrian royal ideology

title: A review of structural design for in-wheel motors in new energy vehicles
abstract: The in-wheel motor (IWM) drive system represents one of the most promising architectures for new energy vehicles (NEVs), offering distinct advantages in drivetrain efficiency, vehicle packaging flexibility, and independent wheel torque control. This review systematically examines the structural design aspects of in-wheel motors, encompassing electromagnetic topologies, mechanical integration, thermal management, and fault-tolerant configurations. title: Mejoramiento de la calidad en taza del café a través de modificaciones al proceso de fermentación espontánea
abstract: El café es la segunda bebida más consumida en el mundo, después del agua, y está transitando de un producto comercial a uno de alta calidad. El presente estudio investiga el impacto de la maceración y adición de fuentes de carbono sobre los atributos sensoriales en taza del café, utilizando frutos provenientes de dos altitudes: 650 y 1,200 masl. Se aplicó un diseño en parcelas divididas, donde los tratamientos fueron el proceso de maceración carbónica y los subtratamientos la adición de fuentes de carbono. title: BEYOND MADNESS: A RE-EVALUATION OF THE STRATEGIC RATIONALE BEHIND THE BYZANTINE–SASANIAN WAR OF 572
abstract: The reign of Emperor Justin II (565–578) is commonly overshadowed by that of Justinian I and is frequently portrayed in traditional historiography as an irrational and hubristic interlude, largely because of the war launched against the Sasanian Empire in 572. This article reconsiders that judgement by reassessing the strategic rationale behind Justin II’s decision and the factors that shaped the war’s trajectory. title: Mongolian Loanwords in Kazakh: A Semantic and Cultural Analysis
abstract: This study provides a detailed analysis of Mongolic loanwords in Kazakh in terms of their historical origins, phonological and morphological adaptation, and semantic change. The main source of the research is Kazak Tiliniŋ Kirme Sözder Sözdigi (The Dictionary of Borrowed Words in the Kazakh Language), which represents a comprehensive corpus of borrowed vocabulary. title: The limits of models in the debate on Great Moravian centres
abstract: The paper examines the limits of existing models used to interpret the functioning of Great Moravian centres through the case study of Bojná-Valy in Western Slovakia. While recent debate has been structured around Jiří Macháček’s triad of models (agrarian hinterland, autarky, and local market) critically revised by Michal Hlavica, this study argues that such frameworks are insufficient when applied to non-standard sites. title: “ … based on the skewed theory building of the postcolonial movement”: Media conflicts surrounding postcolonial studies and antisemitism in Germany
abstract: The increasing recognition of postcolonial studies gave rise to a revisionist counter-movement on the conservative side in Germany, which went largely unnoticed until 2019. In the course of media conflicts over antisemitism in recent years, however, a majority opinion emerged in the liberal and left-wing camps that fundamentally suspected and criticized postcolonial studies as antisemitic. title: A digital specimen of the extinct Imperial Woodpecker: integrating museum scans, historical film and animated feather articulation
abstract: The Imperial Woodpecker ( Campephilus imperialis ), the world’s largest woodpecker species, is presumed extinct following the collapse of old-growth pine forest in its endemic range in the Sierra Madre Occidental, Mexico. Here, we present a detailed, animated 3D reconstruction of an adult female C. imperialis , built from photogrammetric scans of a physical museum study skin and parameterised against historical footage of the species in the wild. title: Representations of air tragedy in Chinese press: a corpus-driven critical discourse study
abstract: This article examines discourses surrounding air tragedies, aiming to investigate differences in ideological stances adopted by Chinese journalists toward three social actor groups associated with the crashed China Eastern Boeing 737. By integrating theories and methodologies from corpus linguistics and critical discourse studies, and employing corpus linguistics software, the study reveals that Chinese media constructs a positive representation of the “Our” group (the Chinese government and China Eastern Airlines) while framing the “Others” group (Boeing) negatively.
