title: Teaching Thoughtful Statistical Inference: Stories for the World Beyond p < 0.05
abstract: ABSTRACT Statistical hypothesis tests and p values are poorly understood by many students of statistics. Poor application and misinterpretation of statistical inference procedures are common in published research. Over‐reliance on the “ p < 0.05” threshold to claim “statistical significance” often masks weaknesses in the evaluation of statistical evidence. abstract: Purpose This qualitative study sought to understand opioid use following spinal cord injury (SCI) and identify capacity for improving patient safety from the perspective of people with lived experience and healthcare providers (HCPs).Materials and methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 23 participants (14 HCPs; 9 people with SCI) from January to September 2025, using interpretive description. title: Baseline indices of cardiorespiratory fitness for predicting acute mountain sickness: an interpretable four-task ensemble model
abstract: Background Acute mountain sickness (AMS) poses formidable challenges for individuals venturing into high-altitude (HA) environments. Early and precise prediction of AMS is crucial for the timely identification of high-risk individuals and the development of effective treatment strategies. We sought to develop and validate an interpretable Acute Mountain Sickness Four-Task Ensemble (AMS-FTE) model for predicting AMS occurrence and severity according to the old and new LLS definitions. title: ‘The worst of all Turkish peoples’: Ibn Faḍlān’s travel account as British naval intelligence
abstract: Abstract The tenth-century CE Arabic travel account of Aḥmad Ibn Faḍlān has seen many reactions, receptions, and afterlives in Islamicate languages and in European settings. These relate both to the identity and presumed authority of Ibn Faḍlān as an eyewitness observer and presumed diplomat, and to the contents of his account. Considering different presentations of Ibn Faḍlān’s role and identity, this article approaches reactions to and uses of Ibn Faḍlān’s descriptions of the Bāshghird, particularly within a 1918 British military intelligence document, in order to consider Ibn Faḍlān’s poten

title: How can we measure AI-skill demand using online job advertisements? Comparing indicators using German labour market data
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into work processes drives growing demand for AI-related skills. Researchers and policy makers need a reliable measure of regional AI-skill demand to understand and react to these changes. We discuss the advantages and disadvantages of indicators including absolute numbers, shares, and location and normalised location quotients. title: GREEK ATHEISM: A REALITY
abstract: This article is a response to Thomas Harrison’s lively thesis that atheism in ancient Greece is not a historical reality but ‘fundamentally, a scholarly mirage’. Repurposing and updating the arguments from the influential work of Lucien Febvre, The Problem of Unbelief in the Sixteenth Century , Harrison reasons that atheism could not have emerged in the age of Socrates and Plato: all we have from this period are empty accusations of atheism, a religious mentality which was incompatible with total unbelief, and a society in which religion dominated every sphere of personal and public life. title: Does capitalist risk-taking justify profits?
abstract: Abstract The profits collected by owners of companies are commonly taken to be a just and rightful compensation for the economic risks that they take. However, in the last two-and-a-half centuries, the risk-taking that follows with ownership has been drastically reduced as a consequence of legal and organizational changes, including incorporation, limited liability, and diversified investment. abstract: En la presente publicación se realiza una propuesta funcional y simbólica para el conjunto áureo procedente del santuario tartésico de El Carambolo (Camas, Sevilla). abstract: This study analyses the discursive construction of the defendant in a corpus of twelve criminal court rulings on chemsex (39,856 words) issued by the Provincial Court of Madrid (2023–2025). Using Fillmore's frame semantics and Sbisà's taxonomy of presupposition triggers, two AI systems (Claude and ChatGPT) independently annotated eight frames across three functional levels: criminal act, institutional apparatus, and accused subject. title: Feeding power
abstract: Even after 150 years of archaeological research on fortified centres, to which key central functions in early medieval Central Europe are generally attributed, we still do not have a clearer idea of how their populations were supplied with basic goods in practice. This text follows on the discussion opened by Jiří Macháček (2026) for Great Moravian agglomerations. It presents a systematic analysis of possible subsistence strategies, consistently linking them to the social profile of the inhabitants of the centres and to the property regimes that determined the forms of exchange. title: The materiality of postapartheid: post-racial signifiers in Gray Hofmeyr’s Yankee Zulu (1993) and Mad Buddies (2012)
abstract: In 1994, South Africa transitioned from apartheid rule to a post-apartheid democracy, with a constitution in place. Significant scholarship has since covered the many constitutionalised aspects of the period after the end of apartheid: governance, political, social, cultural, and economic, among others. title: Four Case Studies in Comparison and Analogy: Political and Religious Culture, Conversion, Genealogy, and Time in Latin Europe and Medieval Japan
abstract: Our article follows two related objectives. We, first, reconsider the relationship between religion and politics by eschewing the uniform modern State–Church model and questioning its Eurocentric tenets. To do so, we focus on the Middle Ages and pair our decentring perspective with a comparison between Latin Europe in the 9th to 13th centuries and medieval Japan from the late Heian period to the Kamakura and early Muromachi eras (10th to 14th centuries). title: Research on indicator system and comprehensive evaluation of low-altitude airspace use efficiency based on ADS-B data
abstract: This study addresses the growing need for effective low-altitude airspace management driven by the rise of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and urban air mobility (UAM), including e-VTOL aircraft serving the expected UAM concept. The research develops a comprehensive airspace efficiency evaluation system based on ADS-B data, which offers real-time flight information. A TOPSIS-based evaluation model is proposed, incorporating seven core indicators: flight density, total flight time, capacity, traffic flow, specific aircraft flight counts, traffic composition, and altitude utilization. title: ‘Bump them up! Just give them a chance!’ Gender, Ethos and Collective Filmmaking in South Africa
abstract: This article is the outcome of the exploratory phase of a research project on collective filmmaking in South Africa that focuses on the lived experience of workers in the audiovisual industry. The first part offers a brief overview of South African colonial history and multilingual culture, of early film exhibition and production in South Africa, of the development of the Afrikaans film industry under apartheid and of its institutional transformation in the post-apartheid period, highlighting how social and political factors shape the industry's evolution. title: Bajo asedio: la defensa de Filipinas de las incursiones neerlandesas (1600-1648)
abstract: La Compañía de las Indias Orientales neerlandesa (VOC), a lo largo de su enfrentamiento con la Monarquía Hispánica, realizó durante casi medio siglo más de una veintena de ataques de diferente índole sobre las Filipinas. El archipiélago se convirtió en un frente estratégico y activo de la guerra entre la Monarquía Hispánica y la República Neerlandesa durante la primera mitad del siglo XVII. title: Prácticas trans-archivísticas y archivo fotográfico en Argentina. Memoria travesti, comunidad y acceso en el Archivo de la Memoria Trans y la Biblioteca Claudia Pía Baudracco
abstract: This article examines Archivo de la Memoria Trans and Biblioteca Claudia Pía Baudracco as community-based archival experiences that reshape the way photographic archives are understood in Argentina. Drawing on a qualitative and situated approach, it analyzes the transition from intimate and dispersed memories to a public infrastructure of preservation, description, access, cultural circulation and historical repair. title: Characterizing Wildlife Response to Biomimetic and Conventional Underwater Vehicles
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are a promising alternative to divers for scalable collection of natural ocean ecology data. However, these robots may disturb local fauna and cause drastic behavioral differences compared to other monitoring techniques, decreasing their value as scientific tools. A promising prospect is to make AUVs that are more biomimetic, with the hope that taking on the form and behavior of a non-predatory animal may reduce adverse responses. title: Characterizing Refraction-Induced Ranging Bias in Underwater Collaborative Localization
abstract: This work studies how refraction-induced bias on acoustic ranging affects multi-agent collaborative localization in a range of oceanographic conditions and spatial scales. While multi-agent range-aided navigation, which uses range measurements to either fixed infrastructure or other agents, is a promising solution to the challenges of large-scale underwater localization, its accuracy depends strongly on the quality of range measurements. title: Vision-based Underwater Formation Control With Input Saturations via Barrier Lyapunov Functions
abstract: In this work, we propose a communication-free framework for vision-based formation control of fully actuated underwater robots subject to sensing constraints, collision-avoidance requirements, and input saturations. Recentered barrier Lyapunov functions encode sensing and collision-avoidance constraints, while command-filtered backstepping extends the design to the second-order vehicle dynamics. title: Global Exponential Stabilization of a 3D Nonholonomic Vehicle in Spherical Coordinates
abstract: Many spatial (3D) vehicles, including AUVs and fixed-wing aircraft, are effectively nonholonomic and subject to limited actuation, such that continuous time-invariant stabilization is fundamentally obstructed by Brockett's necessary condition. To overcome this obstruction, we exploit the geometric singularity of spherical coordinates to design a backstepping continuous, time-invariant feedback law that exponentially stabilizes a 3D nonholonomic vehicle actuated solely by forward surge velocity, pitch rate, and yaw rate. title: Partial-Scan-and-Move Source Seeking for Mobile Robots
abstract: This paper presents a partial-scan-and-move strategy for source seeking with a mobile robot equipped with an offset scalar sensor. At each robot position, the sensor collects source field measurements while the robot rotates. Instead of requiring a complete circular scan before every move, we ask when the measurements collected over only part of the circle are already sufficient to determine the next action. title: Parameterized Complexity of Spanner Problems with Independent Weights and Lengths
abstract: In this paper, the parameterized complexity of the multiplicative $α$-spanner problem with independent weights and lengths on undirected graphs is considered for the first time. All prior FPT results (except one on DAGs) assume basic instances (i.e., with unit weights and lengths) and are parameterized in the stretch factor $α$ and the (in practice typically non-constant) number of removed edges. title: The Global Carbon Budget as a cointegrated system
abstract: Summary The Global Carbon Budget, maintained by the Global Carbon Project, summarizes Earth’s global carbon cycle through four annual time series beginning in 1959: atmospheric CO2 concentrations, anthropogenic CO2 emissions, and CO2 uptake by land and by ocean. We analyze these four time series as a multivariate (cointegrated) system. abstract: Thermosolutal dendritic solidification involves interface evolution, solute diffusion, heat transfer, and melt flow over markedly different time scales. In lattice Boltzmann simulations, a single numerical time interval may place different transport processes in unfavorable relaxation ranges, while asynchronous updates require consistent transfer of phase-change contributions. abstract: The classical theory of the wind-driven surface layer of a rotating ocean closes the momentum balance with a local flux-gradient law, in which the turbulent stress at a given depth is proportional to the shear at that depth. It predicts a surface current deflected forty-five degrees from the wind, which exceeds most direct measurements. This study asks what follows when locality is relaxed. title: Central stars of newly discovered infrared nebulae: eruptive Be stars PY Gem and HD253659
abstract: The presence of a nebula around massive hot stars often works as an indicator that the object is either in an advanced evolutionary stage or a rare product of close binary interaction. Here, we focus on two Be stars - PY Gem and HD253659 - whose nebulae were detected with the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer. title: The Tidal Venus Phenomenon: Demographics and Case Studies
abstract: Abstract The demographics of terrestrial planets and their orbits reveal a vast diversity in overall planetary energy budgets. Terrestrial exoplanets in short-period or eccentric orbits can experience intense tidal heating that, combined with stellar irradiation, may trigger runaway greenhouse conditions analogous to Venus. abstract: Multiple stable states-the coexistence of two or more distinct ecological configurations under identical environmental conditions-have attracted sustained interest in ecology, yet the field still lacks a unified framework connecting ecological mechanisms to dynamical models. title: A multi-scale approach for wall-bounded WCSPH--RANS simulations
abstract: Achieving sufficient near-wall resolution remains challenging for wall-bounded turbulence simulations using weakly compressible smoothed particle hydrodynamics (WCSPH), as local particle refinement imposes restrictive time-step requirements. This work proposes a multi-scale near-wall approach within the Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) framework to improve near-wall predictions without refining the SPH particle distribution. title: Hydroelastic waves near shear flows
abstract: In this paper, we prove that symmetric, doubly-periodic, three-dimensional hydroelastic waves of small amplitude, bifurcating from a non-uniform shear flow, are necessarily two-dimensional to leading order. A detailed analysis of the solvability condition at quadratic order reveals that all Fourier coefficients with transverse dependence vanish identically. The dimensional reduction is controlled entirely by the vertical structure of the shear flow and is robust under changes to the dynamic boundary condition.

abstract: We consider the stabilization of two-dimensional periodic hydroelastic waves in deep water beneath a massless nonlinear Cosserat sheet by means of a localized pres- sure feedback. For sufficiently regular solutions, under an explicit condition relating gravity, flexural rigidity and the localization profile, we prove a uniform spacetime estimate and a localized dissipation observability inequality. abstract: Language models are increasingly trained on the outputs of other models, forming chains that we call lineages, in which a trait present in one generation can pass to the next. Prior work on subliminal learning has shown that a teacher's trait can transmit to a student through filtered data carrying none of the trait's content. abstract: We replicate the distributional-semantics extractive summarisation method of Mohd, Jan and Shah (2020) and adapt it to Hindi, substituting a Devanagari-appropriate component at every language-specific step. abstract: Abstract Precipitation trends can arise from both dynamic factors (changes in atmospheric circulation) and thermodynamic factors (changes in atmospheric moisture content). Disentangling these contributions can aid in understanding regional climate change and improving projections. title: Tectonics on early Earth driven by Earth's changing shape during tidal recession of the Moon
abstract: Few fragments of Earth's earliest crust have survived, and so this formative period of our planet's history is shrouded in mystery. To leverage the limited data available, it is important to understand all the processes that could have shaped our young planet. Here, I explore a previously neglected aspect of early-Earth dynamics: rotation. title: PlainMap: a lightweight, restartable mapping pipeline for ancient and modern DNA
abstract: Mapping sequencing reads to a reference genome requires preprocessing and alignment choices that can vary with library type, fragment length, sequencing platform, and reference genome. These considerations are particularly important for ancient and historical DNA, where short and damaged fragments can make the most appropriate mapping strategy difficult to determine a priori. abstract: Abstract Sulfur chemistry has emerged as an important probe of exoplanet atmospheres in the JWST era, although observational constraints have thus far been largely limited to SO 2 and H 2 S in warm and hot exoplanets. Recent JWST observations have revealed CS 2 in several cooler gas giant exoplanets, yielding a new tracer of sulfur chemistry. abstract: This study investigates storm-to-storm variability and hemispheric differences in magnetosphere-ionosphere (MI) coupling during the extreme (G5) geomagnetic storm of May 10-11 and the severe (G4) storm of October 10-11, 2024. abstract: Under certain conditions, gravity currents spontaneously develop large-amplitude streamwise undulations on their free surfaces ('roll waves'). The effect of channel geometry on this instability is investigated herein. Via a section-averaged stability analysis conducted independently of the rheology of the flowing material, convex open channels are found to be stabilising, relative to unconfined flows. abstract: In-Context Learning (ICL) has become a cornerstone of modern LLM deployment. However, existing ICL post-training methods have a critical blind spot: they excel at extracting patterns from demonstrations while often neglecting context authority, the ability to determine whether contextual information should govern the final answer. abstract: Type IIP supernovae (SNe,IIP) exhibit a significant diversity in their explosion properties, yet the physical mechanisms driving this diversity remain unknown. abstract: The persistence of beta-blockers like atenolol in aquatic environments necessitates efficient remediation strategies, such as enzymatic biodegradation. abstract: Machine learning approaches have shown potential to automate the creation of seismic catalogues, but their abilities and performance are still questioned and being tested. abstract: Marine debris poses persistent environmental and human-health risks, while recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have expanded the accessibility of image-classification tools. abstract: The precise estimation of permeability is a difficult task due to the nature of heterogeneous reservoirs. abstract: Generative AI depends on training with very large volumes of data, and the acquisition and use of that data has become a focal point for copyright infringement and for privacy and security risks. abstract: The rapid development of technology has transformed teaching, learning, and assessment processes, creating opportunities for the use of Artificial Intelligence tools in educational contexts. abstract: Abstract Lightning‐ignited wildfires (LIWs) are a major contributor to burned area in Northern California and have increased substantially in size over recent decades. abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasts are essential for flood risk management and impact mitigation. Coupling hydrological models with machine learning techniques has gained increasing attention as a means to improve forecast skill, with post-processing emerging as a promising approach to correcting systematic model residuals. title: Planetary foresight: envisioning an early warning system for climate tipping points
abstract: Climate tipping points present significant long-term challenges, with critical thresholds at risk of being crossed within this century. Crossing these thresholds would lead to widespread self-perpetuating changes, from unprecedented sea-level rise to inhospitable weather extremes, for which humanity is inadequately prepared. To build preparedness, humanity requires a better sense of when such thresholds could be crossed, over what timescale the effects might unfold, and what the impacts would be. title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Ship Roll Motion Prediction with Adaptive Loss Balancing
abstract: Accurate prediction of ship roll motion is essential for maritime safety and stability assessment. Physics-based methods can provide physically interpretable predictions, but high-fidelity numerical simulations usually require considerable computational resources, limiting their application to efficient and long duration roll motion prediction. In contrast, purely data driven models are computationally efficient but may lack physical consistency. abstract: Flexible sensors have shown significant potential for sport-specific monitoring owing to their lightweight, soft, stretchable, conformable, and wearable characteristics. This review summarizes the applications of flexible sensors in typical sports, including basketball, volleyball, table tennis, football, badminton, tennis, swimming, and running, with a particular focus on their roles in performance assessment, sport-specific motion recognition, and injury risk monitoring. abstract: The current study examined the impact of AI-mediated digital environments on identity formation and civic participation among young Nigerians and evaluated the role of media literacy in ethical participation in the digital age. The motivation behind this enquiry was the growing exposure of Nigerian citizens, in particular the younger generation, to misinformation, online manipulation, and algorithmic identity formation, with the background of weak media-literacy systems. abstract: The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase-1 (PDK1)/protein kinase B (AKT) signaling axis is dysregulated in breast cancer progression and therapeutic resistance. title: Artificial intelligence and its socioeconomic impact: navigating the path between economic transformation and labor market disruption
abstract: The accumulation of human knowledge has been a key driver of civilization's progress. In recent decades, rapid technological advances, fueled by innovation and scientific research, have transformed the pace of change, creating new economic, social, and ethical challenges. abstract: Adélie penguins (Pygoscelis adeliae) are vital bioindicators of environmental change in Antarctica. This study evaluated the state-of-the-art You Only Look Once version 11 (YOLOv11) deep learning-based object detection model and very high-resolution (VHR) drone images to comprehensively census nesting Adélie penguins on Cape Hallett, Ross Sea, Antarctica. abstract: High-accuracy environmental characterization is essential for reliable mooring system design and safety assessment of wave energy converters (WECs). This study employed the Finite-Volume Community Ocean Model (FVCOM) and Simulating Waves Nearshore (SWAN) to simulate tidal and wave conditions over 2005–2024. abstract: Reliable short-horizon drift estimates can support maritime search planning when environmental forcing fields are incomplete. However, trajectory-derived predictors can inadvertently contain information from the forecast interval, random splitting can mix strongly related observations across data partitions, and complex models can appear skillful without outperforming simple motion extrapolation. abstract: Traditional landslide susceptibility models often rely on statistical methods applied to limited point-based samples, which can limit the spatial continuity of predictions. This study proposes a GIS-integrated, pixel-based machine learning approach that operates directly on raster data to generate continuous landslide susceptibility maps. abstract: Underwater defect detection (UDD) from images is essential for the safe operation and maintenance of hydraulic structures. However, UDD remains challenging because of substantial variations in appearance, limited annotated data, and degraded underwater image quality. abstract: Accurate fish counting seeks to estimate the total number of fish within an image and is widely applied in fields such as sustainable aquaculture management, aquatic ecosystem monitoring, and population management. However, challenges arise due to variations in fish pose, occlusion resulting from aggregation, and background interference from elements such as aquatic plants, rocks, and suspended particles. abstract: Wind is a dominant load for coastal bridges, yet long-term wind field data are often lacking, making accurate design wind speed evaluation challenging. abstract: Abstract Underwater image enhancement (UIE) is still difficult. This is mainly due to wavelength-dependent light absorption, scattering, and environmental noise, which lead to low visibility, color distortion, and loss of fine details. title: Automotive aerodynamic reduced-order prediction based on physics-guided block design neural network
abstract: To address the high computational cost of CFD simulations, the increased sample requirements caused by high-dimensional design variables, and the limited generalization capability of traditional surrogate models in automotive aerodynamic optimization, this study proposes a Physics-Guided Block Design Neural Network (PG-BDNN) for aerodynamic reduced-order prediction. abstract: Accurate solar irradiance forecasting is a key prerequisite for reliable solar photovoltaic (PV) operation, effective energy management, and system optimization. Conventional forecasting methods, such as historical averaging, persistence models, and coarse-resolution numerical weather prediction outputs, often exhibit limited performance in coastal and microclimate-sensitive environments where irradiance is characterized by rapid and nonlinear atmospheric variability. abstract: Accurate forecasting of agricultural exports is essential for supporting production planning, trade management, and evidence-based policymaking. However, forecasting cocoa exports remains challenging because export volumes are influenced by interconnected environmental, climatic, and economic factors. This study proposes an integrated forecasting framework for Indonesian cocoa export volumes by incorporating remote sensing indicators, climatic indices, and economic variables into statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid forecasting approaches. This study evaluates the Spatial Multi-Attention Conditional Neural Process (SMACNP), a probabilistic deep learning framework, for the daily spatial interpolation of air temperature and precipitation, marking the first application of its localized encoder variant to the challenge of gridding climate data from a sparse station network. abstract: Submerged floating tunnels (SFTs) are prone to accidental impact hazards such as ship anchoring and vessel collisions. Existing displacement prediction methods suffer from limited working condition coverage, ambiguous nonlinear multi-factor coupling mechanisms, and the black-box limitation of traditional machine learning (ML). abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is one of the major causes of vision loss worldwide; early detection can help prevent permanent vision loss. Several deep learning approaches have been developed for retinal image analysis, yet they often face practical challenges in accurately diagnosing diabetic retinopathy. Class imbalance is a common issue in DR, where disease stages share subtle visual traits, and models tend to overfit to the training data. title: Digitalization of paper smooth sheets using hydrographic data from the Gulf of Patience and the port of Korsakov (Sakhalin Island, Russia)
abstract: In the context of reconstructing ports and other hydraulic structures, historical paper smooth sheets are particularly significant for tracking bottom mark dynamics over time. However, the integration of paper smooth sheets into modern digital surveying systems remains challenging. This paper introduces an artificial intelligence (AI)-based method for digitally harmonizing old (paper) and new smooth sheets intended for subsequent analysis of coastal zone dynamics and bottom topography.

abstract: Precise thermal regulation in thermoelectric systems is challenging due to nonlinear dynamics, thermal inertia, and environmental disturbances. Although machine-learning techniques can address this challenge by modeling complex spectral relationships, they generally require sufficiently large and representative labeled training datasets. abstract: Background Malaria in pregnancy remains a significant public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa. abstract: Maritime decarbonisation requires transparent use of verified emissions data without overstating what regulatory datasets can explain. abstract: Herbal medicines represent a rich source of bioactive compounds with significant therapeutic potential. However, the discovery of herbal drugs is challenged by complex phytochemical compositions, variability in biological activity, limited standardization, and labor-intensive experimental screening. abstract: Finding novel treatments is a long and complex process involving extensive drug discovery, experimental testing, and preclinical research. abstract: Abstract Operational wave prediction systems provide critical information across a range of marine industries and for public safety. Three coastal gradient zones (0–10 km, 10–20 km, and 20–30 km from the coastline) were established to examine variations in urban land, cropland, and water. Simufact Welding was used to simulate multi-layer wall deposition and predict distortion behaviour. Experimental validation showed that the unclamped substrate ends experienced a maximum distortion of 4.50 mm due to thermal shrinkage and bending effects. abstract: Mineral scale deposition is one of the most persistent flow assurance challenges in the oil and gas industry, causing formation damage, reduced injectivity and productivity, equipment fouling, pipeline blockage, and substantial economic losses. The increasing application of seawater injection, produced-water reinjection, and enhanced oil recovery (EOR) techniques has intensified scaling problems by promoting the mixing of incompatible waters and altering reservoir geochemistry. title: Integrating compaction energy into predictive models for pervious concrete permeability
abstract: Pervious concrete is an innovative material that effectively manages stormwater runoff. This study aims to develop predictive models for the permeability of pervious concrete, with a particular emphasis on the role of compaction energy. A comprehensive modelling approach was adopted, incorporating Linear Regression, Two-Factor Interaction model, Quadratic model, and Artificial Neural Network to examine the relationships between permeability and key mix design variables. abstract: Abstract Modeling earthquake clustering in space and time is central to understanding seismicity patterns and improving forecasting. The Epidemic‐Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) model, grounded in the Hawkes process, has long been the standard approach for describing aftershock triggering through fixed, empirically defined kernel functions. title: Algal Biodiversity as a Sentinel of Freshwater Ecosystem Health
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are among the most biologically productive yet ecologically vulnerable habitats on Earth, facing escalating pressures from nutrient enrichment, climate change, industrial pollution, and expanding urbanization. Algae encompassing a phylogenetically diverse assemblage ranging from unicellular phytoplankton and benthic diatoms to filamentous green algae and colonial cyanobacteria serve simultaneously as foundational primary producers and sensitive environmental recorders. title: A three-dimensional framework for analyzing transformative capacity in coastal adaptation: embeddedness, influence and reproduction
abstract: Coastal social-ecological systems (SESs) around the world are under considerable pressure from climate change and anthropogenic disturbances. Transformative adaptation (TA) has attracted substantial attention for delivering pathways towards sustainable, climate-resilient development. However, existing coastal adaptation practices remain constrained by systemic limitations and fragmented approaches, underscoring the need for conceptual synthesis and systematic evaluation of various adaptation interventions to pinpoint core barriers and generate actionable insights. title: Analysis of the impact of weather factors on the behavior of pelagic commercial fish and the possibility of detecting their schools and aggregations using unmanned aerial vehicles
abstract: The paper examines the influence of weather and hydrometeorological factors on the behavior of pelagic commercial fish and the effectiveness of detecting their schools and aggregations using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The focus is on the Pacific saury, one of the most challenging targets for detection in the North-Western Pacific Ocean. abstract: Nowadays, there are a large number of ground-based neutron monitors. These detectors measure neutron fluxes produced by the interaction of primary cosmic rays (CR) with Earth’s atmosphere. Since their invention in the 1950s, they have become very popular for studying variations of CR intensity on different time scales. title: Advancing hydrological and cryospheric simulations in Indus River Basin: First comparative evaluation of GESSI-3/ESSI-3 and a CNN–LSTM deep learning framework
abstract: Hydrological models of glacier-fed river systems are critical for assessing climate impacts, yet conventional single-variable calibration, often against discharge alone, may obscure key climate sensitivities and internal dynamics. To address this, we conduct the first multi-variable, basin-wide evaluation of process-based and deep learning hydrological models across the climatically diverse Indus River Basin (IRB). title: Hybrid application of response surface methodology modelling and machine learning exploratory prediction for reducing sugar recovery from potato peel waste for bioethanol production
abstract: Global interest in bioethanol production from waste lignocellulosic biomasses (LCB) has heighten, however, current efforts are often constrained by lack of predictability of outcome in terms of sugar recovery towards bioethanol produced. Thus, focusing on reducing sugar (RS) recovery, this study models reduced sugar release from nano-based PPW pretreatment. title: Estimation of dissolved oxygen in reservoirs from UAV-drone, Sentinel-2 and Landsat-9 multisensor data using stacked-ensemble machine learning: review and case study experimental results
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of dissolved oxygen (DO) in reservoir systems is essential for assessing aquatic ecosystem health and informing water management decisions. This study develops and validates a stacked ensemble machine learning (SE-ML) modeling framework for estimating DO concentrations in a dam water reservoir by comparing multispectral reflectance data from UAV-drone, Sentinel-2 MSI, and Landsat-9 OLI-2 sensors. title: Analysis of the coupling characteristics and influencing mechanisms between civilized rural development and green agriculture in China based on explainable machine learning and the GWR model
abstract: In the context of rural revitalization and ecological civilization construction, understanding the relationship between civilized rural development and green agricultural development is essential for achieving sustainable rural transformation. Using panel data from 31 Chinese provinces from 2012 to 2020, this study constructs a multidimensional evaluation framework and applies the Coupling Coordination Degree Model (CCDM) to examine the spatiotemporal evolution of the two systems. title: INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL PARA EL CRIBADO DE RETINOPATÍA DIABÉTICA: PRECISIÓN DIAGNÓSTICA, IMPLEMENTACIÓN EN ENTORNOS REALES Y DESAFÍOS ÉTICOS
abstract: ABSTRACT Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of preventable blindness among working-age adults, and its prevalence is increasing in line with the global spread of diabetes mellitus. Objective: To analyze the scientific evidence published from 2016 to 2026 regarding the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI) for DR screening, its application in real-world clinical practice, and the ethics of its use. title: Machine learning for one day ahead prediction of high fire weather index conditions from area weighted ERA5 data in mersin
abstract: Abstract Severe fire weather places sustained pressure on preparedness in Mediterranean forests. We developed a retrospective benchmark for classifying next-day Fire Weather Index (FWI) conditions in Mersin, Türkiye, from hourly ERA5 reanalysis covering the 2003–2025 fire seasons. Canadian FWI components were calculated independently at 41 ERA5 cells intersecting the province and then aggregated with polygon-intersection area weights. title: Empirical Determination and Modelling of Compressive Strength of Cement Composites with Waste Tyre Rubber
abstract: Incorporating waste tyre rubber into cement composites could pose a sustainable strategy for reducing tyre waste, whilst simultaneously preserving natural resources. Accurate prediction of the compressive strength is essential for the efficient development and application of the new material. This study presents the experimental research and a new proposed machine learning modelling framework aimed at predicting the compressive strength of conventional and rubber-modified cement composites containing recycled rubber derived from end-of-life vehicle tyres. title: Architecture driven design of continuous steel wire reinforced FDM composites: Experimental investigation and mechanics-informed machine learning of structure–property relationships
abstract: Continuous fiber reinforced FDM composites treat reinforcement content as the main design variable, while through thickness placement remains unexplored. This study establishes reinforcement architecture as a design parameter governing tensile and flexural performance of 0.20 mm stainless steel wire reinforced ABS composites. An in situ FDM platform embedded wires while varying fiber volume fraction (V f ), through thickness position, stacking sequence, symmetry, raster orientation, and build orientation. title: Present-day thermal regime of the Xihu Sag, East China Sea Shelf Basin: constraints from an updated well database and logging-derived thermal conductivity
abstract: Introduction Continental margin rift basins are characterized by highly variable present-day heat flow reflecting differential lithospheric extension. The East China Sea Shelf Basin, situated at the convergent boundary of multiple plates, represents a unique tectonic setting where Cenozoic rifting has produced an anomalously high thermal state that remains poorly documented. abstract: Abstract The collapse of the Fundão dam in southeastern Brazil released large quantities of Fe-rich tailings into the Doce River basin, generating a long-term legacy of mining-derived sediments enriched in potentially toxic elements (PTEs). Although Fe oxyhydroxides are recognized as major geochemical hosts of contaminants, their long-term mineralogical evolution and relationships with PTE partitioning in tropical fluvial–estuarine systems remain poorly understood. title: Development of RADEC-Based Deep Learning Lesson Planning to Enhance Fifth-Grade Students’ Critical Thinking Skills in Integrated Science and Social Studies
abstract: Critical thinking is an essential 21st-century competency, yet its development in elementary education is often constrained by instructional planning that provides limited opportunities for higher-order thinking. This study developed and evaluated RADEC-based Deep Learning Lesson Planning integrating the Read, Answer, Discuss, Explain, and Create stages to support fifth-grade students’ critical-thinking skills in Integrated Science and Social Studies (IPAS). abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater‐based artificial leaves are fundamentally constrained by anodic surface poisoning and insufficient photovoltage for bias‐free reaction under complex electrolytes. title: Price Behavior of Selected Marine Fish Species in Colombo Market Sri Lanka
abstract: In Sri Lanka, fish provide about 50% of the animal protein consumed, which is nearly three times the global average. The country’s fisheries, including marine, inland, and aquaculture sectors, play an important role in food security and livelihoods. However, significant price fluctuations have impacted stakeholders such as fishers, traders, and consumers. This study analyzes price trends and seasonal patterns of six selected fish species (large pelagic and small pelagic) consumed by Sri Lankans, which are commonly available in the Colombo market. title: AI‐Powered GPR Characterization of Peatland Underground Cavity Induced by Smoldering Wildfire: A Laboratory Proof‐of‐Concept
abstract: ABSTRACT Global peatlands are increasingly vulnerable to severe and persistent wildfires under climate change. Once ignited, peat fires often smolder beneath the surface, forming underground cavities that are challenging to detect using conventional sensing techniques. This work proposes a novel approach that integrates ground‐penetrating radar (GPR) with artificial intelligence (AI) to estimate the geometry of idealized air‐filled cavity analogs, providing a support basis for characterizing and quantifying the fire‐induced underground cavities. title: Comparison of biological matrices for the quantification of blood protein fractions in sea turtles Caretta caretta
abstract: Caretta caretta is the predominant sea turtle nesting along the coasts of the Mediterranean Sea. It is listed as a vulnerable species in the IUCN red list, because it is threatened by human activities. Protein electrophoresis is an important diagnostic tool in sea turtles rehabilitation, providing information on inflammatory, nutritional and epatic status. abstract: ABSTRACT Marine protective coatings often fail prematurely under the coupled effects of mechanical damage, UV irradiation, microbial fouling, and corrosion, because conventional barrier‑type systems lack adaptive interfacial regulation and integrated protective functions. Herein, a GO‑HHU‑CuPN‑EP coating is fabricated via a room‑temperature aqueous supramolecular self‑assembly strategy. title: Interpretable multi-task learning for corrosion state prediction of carbon steel in simulated marine atmospheric environments from rust morphology
abstract: Accurate assessment of corrosion states from surface morphology remains challenging in marine atmospheric environments, particularly when morphologies appear macroscopically similar despite different corrosion conditions. A multi-task deep learning model (MultiTask-ResNet50) is developed to predict chloride concentration level (classification), corrosion period, and corrosion weight gain (regression) from a single corrosion morphology image. title: AI-based decision support tools for short-term forecasting and aeration control in wastewater treatment plants
abstract: Introduction Effective operation of wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) requires timely and informed decisions to maintain process stability and energy efficiency. This paper presents two artificial intelligence (AI) tools designed to support WWTP operators in short-term decision-making.Materials The tools were developed and evaluated using historical operational data from the Alcantarilla municipal wastewater treatment plant in Murcia, Spain. abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming university life and the way educators and students engage with knowledge. Generative assistants, intelligent tutors, and adaptive systems offer opportunities to personalize learning, provide immediate feedback, and address diverse educational needs. However, their use also raises concerns regarding privacy, academic authorship, algorithmic bias, and technological dependency. abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive hydrogels are promising for wearable sensors in human motion detection owing to their skin‐like softness, strain sensitivity, and biocompatibility. However, their practical application in aqueous environments is severely hindered by swelling‐induced mechanical deterioration and electrical instability. Herein, a tough, anti‐swelling conductive hydrogel for underwater sensing is reported, enabled by a “silk nanofiber‐mediated controlled‐swelling‐locking” (SNF‐CSL) strategy. title: An integrated data-driven and experimental methodology for toroidal propeller design improvement
abstract: This study presents a data-driven hydrodynamic optimization framework for toroidal propellers. As a representative engineering application of artificial intelligence (AI), the framework offers an efficient route toward the advanced design of underwater propulsion systems. The framework is based on an experimentally validated high-fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model, where open-water test data are used to validate the numerical methodology. title: Multi source Earth observation and machine learning framework for mapping land degradation vulnerability in salinity- and hydrothermal-stressed regions of the southern main Ethiopian Rift
abstract: Soil erosion and land degradation are the main environmental challenges disturbing ecosystem services, agricultural productivity, and community livelihoods in Ethiopia. The Southern Main Ethiopian Rift is one of the regions experiencing high levels of soil erosion and land degradation, driven by active geological processes and anthropogenic activities. However, the contribution of these geological processes to salinization and their subsequent impact on soil erosion and land degradation in the region remains poorly understood and insufficiently studied. title: Insights into WRF-Chem Sensitivity in a Coastal Region of Morocco: Chemical Mechanisms, Nesting Options, and Physical Parameterization
abstract: The performance of the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with chemistry (WRF-Chem) depends on the accuracy of input data and parameterisation schemes. This study examined the sensitivity of WRF-Chem version 4.4.2 to various domain configurations, chemical mechanisms, and physics parameterizations. The model was applied to predict air quality pollutants (PM₁₀, O₃, CO, NO₂, SO₂) and meteorological variables (wind speed and temperature) for the first time over the Moroccan city of Agadir, which features complex topography and land use. abstract: Rhamnolipid production by a crude-oil-adapted Pseudomonas aeruginosa SC1 strain was statistically optimized using glycerol as the carbon source and ammonium sulfate as the nitrogen source, and the relationship between biomass formation and biosurfactant synthesis was evaluated. The strain, isolated from crude-oil-contaminated soil using Bushnell–Haas medium, was cultivated in a defined mineral medium. title: Source Term Estimation for Atmospheric Pollutant Releases from Sparse Sensor Networks: A Methodological Review and Comparative Assessment
abstract: Determining the location, release strength and temporal profile of an unknown atmospheric pollutant source from concentration measurements recorded by a small number of ground-based sensors is a core problem of environmental monitoring, industrial safety and emergency response. abstract: Pollutant dispersion in the wakes of fixed cylindrical marine structures is strongly influenced by interactions between vortex shedding and oscillatory currents, yet the role of their relative timescales in cross-stream spreading remains unclear. title: Improving SST Prediction Accuracy of Ina-Flows Model in Karimun Jawa and Bira
abstract: Sea surface temperature (SST) is an important parameter in ocean-atmosphere interaction, but BMKG Ina-Flows model outputs may still contain systematic bias. This study evaluates the accuracy of Ina-Flows SST predictions and improves their performance through machine learning-based bias correction at MAWS Karimun Jawa and Bira. The dataset consists of Ina-Flows SST outputs and MAWS observations from 1 December 2023 to 7 December 2024. abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) has been progressively incorporated into clinical laboratories as a tool to support data processing, result interpretation, and diagnostic decision-making. However, the use of complex models has raised concerns regarding transparency, interpretability, and the ability to supervise algorithmic decisions, particularly when these decisions may influence patient care and safety. In this context, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has gained relevance by providing mechanisms intended to facilitate the understanding of predictions generated by AI models.

title: Intelligent Fuzzy Inference-Based Decision-Support System for Marine Main Diesel Engines
abstract: The subject of the study is the development of an intelligent decision support system based on fuzzy logic for marine diesel engines, aimed at improving diagnostic accuracy and operational reliability under conditions of incomplete, uncertain, or fragmented data. title: Unravelling the role of increased model resolution in simulating surface temperature fields using explainable AI
abstract: Abstract Minimizing climate model biases is essential to reduce uncertainties in future climate projections. Despite recent advances, improvements between generations of Earth System Models (ESMs) remain modest, largely due to continued reliance on subgrid-scale parametrizations. These are required because CMIP6 model resolutions are too coarse to explicitly simulate small-scale processes such as ocean mesoscale eddies and deep atmospheric convection, which strongly influence climate patterns. title: Identification of immune cell mitochondrial dysfunction characteristics and clinical predictive biomarkers in sepsis via multi-cohort machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis involves dysregulated host responses with mitochondrial dysfunction as a key mechanism, yet its immune cell landscape and clinical utility are unclear. METHODS: We integrated five GEO datasets (GSE65682, GSE95233, GSE54514, GSE26440, GSE26378) comprising 1,256 samples. title: Enhancing Meta Fuzzy Functions via Dynamic Pruning: A Nationwide Air Temperature Forecasting Framework for Türkiye
abstract: This study proposes a novel Pruned Meta-Fuzzy Functions (PMFF) framework to forecast nationwide air temperatures across 81 cities in Türkiye. While existing literature often focuses on single models or standard hybridizations, these approaches frequently struggle with noise inherent in meteorological datasets and lack the necessary generalizability to perform across diverse topographical and climatic regions. title: Linking landscape structure and resource availability to coastal bird responses under Spartina alterniflora invasion
abstract: The invasion of Spartina alterniflora has profoundly altered habitat composition, landscape patterns, and resource availability in coastal wetlands. However, the large-scale mechanisms through which these changes affect birds with different habitat requirements remain poorly understood. title: Cascading magmatic unrest and aseismic faulting in the Aegean Sea enabled by elastic stress relay
abstract: Magma reservoirs commonly exist in clusters and situate within complex fault networks, yet sequential triggering of unrest at multiple reservoirs and faults is rarely observed. title: Exploring the added value of assimilating satellite altimeter measurements in a North Sea wave model using the Deterministic Ensemble Kalman Filter
abstract: Abstract This study reports on the impact of assimilating satellite altimeter measurements with the Deterministic Ensemble Kalman Filter (DEnKF) using a regional SWAN wave model for the North Sea. We assimilated satellite altimeter measurements over a 3-month period (December 2021 - March 2022) from the following satellites: nadir CFOSAT, Haiyang-2B, Cryosat-2, Jason-3, Sentinel-3, Saral and Altika. title: Marine-Derived Bioactive Peptides as Immunomodulatory Agents: Organoid-Based Platforms and Translational Perspectives
abstract: Marine environments harbor immense biodiversity that yields peptides with potent immunomodulatory, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory activities. These marine-derived immunomodulatory peptides act as molecular mediators of host defense and immune homeostasis across taxa ranging from fish to humans. title: Engineering synthetic microbial communities for soil restoration: from rational design to multi-scale biogeochemical applications
abstract: Soil degradation caused by intensive land use, pollution, and climate stress threatens food production and ecosystem function. Single-strain inoculants often perform inconsistently because they do not persist or compete well in resident soil microbiomes. Synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) combine complementary microbial functions in defined consortia. Their performance, however, depends on community composition and environmental context. title: Beyond regional greening: Nonlinear GPP trajectories and their environmental associations in eastern coastal China
abstract: Coastal ecosystems are highly vulnerable to synergistic environmental pressures, yet traditional linear assessments may hide their short-term dynamic responses. To examine these responses, this study developed an integrated diagnostic framework that combined the Mann–Kendall test, BFAST01, and spatially validated XGBoost–SHAP to characterize GPP trajectories in Shandong Province from 2000 to 2022. abstract: Small-scale fisheries are complex social–ecological systems in which environmental change interacts with socioeconomic constraints, shaping the vulnerability of fishing-dependent communities. This study assessed socioeconomic vulnerability and fishers’ perceptions across 12 artisanal fishing communities along the marine–coastal margin of the Magdalena Department, Colombian Caribbean. abstract: ABSTRACT Ruthenium (Ru)‐based materials are promising catalysts for alkaline water electrolysis; however, their practical application is severely limited by insufficient activity and poor stability. abstract: Introduction Recreational activities such as birdwatching, or “birding,” are among the most commonly studied cultural ecosystem services. However, the benefits these services provide, particularly within avian-estuarine habitats, remain mostly under characterized. We identify, distinguish, and compare stakeholder perceptions of cultural ecosystem service benefits associated with birdwatching across two major estuaries situated within US coastal flyways. abstract: Petroleum hydrocarbons pose a major global environmental threat to both land and marine ecosystems. Taking the significant wave height and mean wave period during two typhoon events in the South China Sea as research objects, the numerical simulation results are compared with buoy observation data. abstract: Understanding how water mixes at estuaries, where rivers and streams meet the ocean, is important for maintaining fresh water quality.

abstract: Fungi play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystems as decomposers, pathogens and endophytes, yet their significance in marine environments is often understudied. abstract: This paper presents an integrated floating dual-chamber Wave Energy Converter system designed for offshore wave energy harnessing in the Aegean Sea. The study utilizes optimized geometric configurations and mooring characteristics for an Oscillating Water Column, which incorporates a dual coaxial hollow cylindrical structure. title: Training-free post-disaster damage estimation with incomplete satellite images by integrating open data and fractional hot deck imputation
abstract: Abstract Analyzing satellite imagery is an essential step after a severe natural disaster for monitoring the level of damage and making the best decision. The current study proposes a fast post-disaster damage framework incorporating the remote sensing of imagery, entropy calculation, object detection using an advanced machine learning (ML) model, and missing data curation. abstract: Introduction Maritime chokepoint disruptions can substantially degrade shipping services even when the underlying network remains structurally connected. This study examines the Red Sea–Suez disruption and evaluates alternative recovery strategies. abstract: A structural and economic optimization framework applicable to floating semi-submersible platforms, demonstrated here for a 15 MW offshore wind design, is presented. A genetic algorithm was developed that can seek a multi-objective solution to minimize mass whilst respecting the constraints of loads acting upon the system. title: Intelligent classification method for surrounding rock in subsea tunnels: multi-source parameter perception and model construction
abstract: Accurate surrounding rock grade identification is essential for the safe and efficient construction of subsea tunnels. Conventional surrounding rock classification methods are mainly developed for mountain tunnels and general underground engineering, and they do not sufficiently characterize subsea-environment-related deterioration caused by high-head groundwater, seawater intrusion, hydrochemical erosion, and weathering. abstract: This study investigates the flow and heat transfer characteristics of the Once-through Cooling System (OCS) in a nuclear power plant under cold source disturbances. Based on an energy transport model of the Cold-End System it systematically analyzes the influence of various cold source disturbance factors on system operation, including seawater temperature, tide level, and condenser cleanliness coefficient. title: Projected expansion of Tetranychus truncatus Ehara (Acari: Tetranychidae) in China under future climate scenarios: A MaxEnt modeling approach
abstract: Tetranychus truncatus Ehara, the cotton red spider mite, is an economically significant polyphagous pest that infests economically important crops such as maize, soybean, cotton, and various fruits in China. Its rapid reproduction, broad host range, and increasing insecticide resistance cause significant agricultural and horticultural losses. abstract: Accurate reconstruction of unsteady wakes around offshore cylindrical structures is important for assessing wake interference, flow-induced loads, and the hydrodynamic environment of pile groups, marine risers, and related systems. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide a mesh-free surrogate modelling approach for such unsteady flows, but their accuracy depends strongly on collocation-point placement in evolving wake and boundary-layer regions. abstract: The exponential growth of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in edge devices, embedded systems, and data centers has intensified the demand for efficient and scalable processor architectures. This paper provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of RISC-V and ARM architectures in AI applications, examining their architectural features, performance characteristics, energy efficiency, and ecosystem maturity. abstract: Accurate prediction of road surface temperature (RST) is essential for proactive winter road maintenance and traffic safety management. However, existing approaches – ranging from physics-based models to data-driven methods – either require detailed pavement thermal parameters that are rarely available at operational road meteorological stations, or lack the capacity to simultaneously exploit local meteorological analogues and long-range temporal dependencies in an interpretable ensemble framework. abstract: Introduction Land-based cultivation using alternative water resources, such as saline groundwater (brine), offers a promising strategy for the sustainable production of the green macroalga Ulva compressa . Because Ulva growth and morphogenesis depend strongly on associated bacteria, understanding microbiome dynamics during acclimatization to brine is essential for stable biomass production. Environmental wireless sensing networks (WSNs) can meet this need, but few researchers currently implement this infrastructure themselves, instead relying on legacy data loggers that require manual data retrieval or commercial telemetry systems that are too often hindered by financial and logistical constraints, e.g., sensor lock in, proprietary data models, recurring cellular fees, and lack of programmatic data access (e.g., APIs). abstract: ABSTRACT Fluid mud (FM) is a transient high‐concentration sediment layer commonly observed in highly turbid estuaries, exerting significant influences on sediment transport, channel evolution, and navigation conditions. However, the formation and dissipation mechanisms of FM under extreme weather conditions remain poorly constrained due to the limited availability of field observations during storm events. abstract: This paper analyses the challenges of digital education in higher education within the field of communication, focusing on the tension between instrumental digital literacy and the development of critical thinking. Based on a qualitative exploratory approach grounded in theoretical analysis and teaching experience, the study examines how students appropriate digital technologies in educational contexts. title: Identification of granitic pegmatites based on GF-5 hyperspectral data and LSTM-Transformer model
abstract: Lithium is a key strategic mineral to support new energy and advanced technology, mainly enriched in granitic pegmatite. The integration of hyperspectral remote sensing and deep learning frameworks has emerged as a leading approach for quantitative identification of pegmatites. However, deep learning algorithms are often limited by the scarcity of labeled samples and the challenge of extracting features from high-dimensional spectral data. title: An AI-driven evidence ecosystem for cardiometabolic nutrition: bridging the gap from multiomics to patient empowerment
abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases remain a primary global health challenge, with nutritional interventions serving as a critical pillar of management. However, the rapidly expanding volume of nutritional research, spanning high-dimensional multiomics, real-world continuous monitoring, and highly heterogeneous clinical trials, has created fragmented knowledge silos, leading to a profound translation lag between scientific discovery and clinical practice. abstract: ABSTRACT Electric vehicle (EV) charging demand forecasting is vital for maintaining smart grid (SG) stability, enhancing energy management (EM), and supporting large‐scale EV integration. Nevertheless, current forecasting techniques often fail to maintain high prediction accuracy as well as computing efficiency while capturing complex spatial and temporal dependencies. abstract: Coastal urbanization requires spatial models that distinguish historical change from conditional projections. This study reconstructed land-use and land-cover dynamics in Makassar, Indonesia, from 2005 to 2025 and projected built-up expansion to 2035 using an integrated artificial neural network–cellular automata (ANN–CA) framework and Bayesian Weights of Evidence (WoE). title: A Probabilistic multi-objective optimization framework for offshore wind turbine jacket substructure under aero-hydrodynamic loading using surrogate models
abstract: The significant inherent uncertainties in the design and optimization of offshore wind turbines make it necessary to adopt a probabilistic approach to ensure structural reliability and performance. This study proposes a probabilistic multi-objective optimization approach for the offshore wind turbine (OWT) jacket based on dynamic responses predicted by surrogate models. abstract: Superhydrophobic coatings often lose their water-repellent properties after repeated abrasion and environmental exposure, creating a need for reliable methods to predict coating durability. This study developed a machine learning-based framework to predict the water contact angle (WCA) behaviour of Cu–Zn and polypropylene stearic acid (PP-SA)-modified coatings under ageing and cyclic wear conditions. abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) brings with it significant challenges and transformative benefits. This literature review examines these points, highlighting a lack of funding, a lack of adequate technological infrastructure, a shortage of specialized experts, and a reluctance to change as the main impediments to implementing AI. abstract: As hydrological trends shift in response to a warming climate, accurate characterization of hydrologic conditions and hydrologic change are imperative for water resources management, which is particularly important in the Canadian Prairies. abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) has the potential to revolutionize rapid diagnostic decision-making in Emergency Departments (EDs). However, the socio-psychological dynamics of human-machine collaboration in life-or-death scenarios remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Introduction Ecological restoration projects are rapidly expanding in size, complexity, and frequency globally, driven by international agreements and an increased recognition of the efficacy of actions for biodiversity. Upscaling restoration will increasingly necessitate the restoration of multiple physically or functionally connected habitats concurrently, including across ecological realms (i.e. marine, freshwater, and terrestrial). abstract: In operational coastal monitoring of spatially fragmented intertidal habitats, labelled datasets are structurally constrained by the limited spatial extent of target species, yet the relative influence of training strategy versus architecture on segmentation performance remains poorly characterised. abstract: This paper explores Instagram as a platform for visual and emotional narratives of disaster across the response and recovery phases. Focusing on the extreme flooding that affected western Germany in July 2021, the study analyzes approximately 2,700 Instagram posts collected over a three-year period. It employs a mixed-methods approach combining generative artificial intelligence with qualitative and quantitative analyses. title: U-Net-based time-series mapping of tidal flat areas and carbon sink variations under fluctuating tidal levels
abstract: Tidal flats are crucial for carbon storage but are threatened by human activities. Satellite remote sensing data and deep learning methods help extrapolate field-based carbon measurements to broader spatial and temporal scales. abstract: Abstract A wide selection of linear and non‐linear dimensionality reduction techniques is evaluated on synthetic tsunami data that is the basis for tsunami hazard assessment and computational forecasting. The data were computed from earthquake rupture forecasts (ERFs) supplying initial generation conditions and a linear long‐wave Green's function approach to efficiently calculate tsunami propagation. title: Algorithmic Governance and International Law: Reconciling Sovereignty and Cross-Border Accountability
abstract: Abstract This article interrogates the concept of artificial intelligence (AI) sovereignty as an emerging site of normative tension within international law. As states increasingly assert jurisdiction over AI technologies and digital infrastructures, established doctrines, particularly those concerning territoriality, jurisdiction, and accountability, are under strain. abstract: Abstract The essay by Patriotta and Weick (2026) constitutes one of the last scholarly contributions by Karl Weick. abstract: ABSTRACT Materials manufacturing has entered into a new era with the rapid development of technologies. abstract: Modeling of complex systems is based on established theories and concepts, but also on innovative constructions that harmonize the system with the requirements foreseen for its operating life. The problems of system interaction are concentrated at each coupling interface between them, where the harmonization of inputs and outputs of matter, energy and information, the management of coupling variables, the mutual compatibility of systems, the harmonization of error handling procedures, data processing protocols and reliability are achieved. title: Physics-Informed Hybrid ANN-P&O Optimal-Flux Control for Energy-Efficient Induction Motor Drives
abstract: This paper proposes a physics-informed hybrid artificial neural network (ANN) and perturb-and-observe (P&O) optimal-flux controller for reducing losses in a field-oriented induction motor drive. The ANN rapidly estimates the optimal rotor-flux reference from measured operating variables, and a bounded P&O search locally refines this estimate using averaged input power. abstract: Breast cancer remains a major global threat to women’s health, and its marked molecular, spatial, and temporal heterogeneity continues to limit the accuracy of early diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment-response prediction. abstract: This article examines the phenomenon of "memetic warfare" as a growing threat to cognitive security and democratic processes. The authors argue that memes – due to their virality, simplicity, and humorous nature – can be an effective tool for narrative manipulation, capable of shaping public opinion, deepening social polarization, and amplifying political and extremist propaganda. abstract: Abstract Functional redundancy is a key biological concept that offers critical insights into microbial ecosystem stability and responses to environmental perturbations. Existing methods to quantify redundancy typically rely on gene annotations as functional units, limiting their ability to capture complex or partially characterised traits and making analyses from metagenomic data—often fragmented or incomplete—challenging. abstract: The popularisation of artificial intelligence assisted learning tools in higher education gives new technical circumstances for the promotion of college students’ autonomous learning ability. title: Environment-adaptive automatic ship collision avoidance system
abstract: Maritime collision accidents remain a critical safety concern despite advances in electronic navigation technology, particularly under adverse weather conditions where reduced visibility and heavy seas substantially degrade a vessel's maneuvering capability. abstract: Abstract Global decarbonization targets are accelerating the low-carbon transition of the construction industry. Driven by the need to meet global decarbonization targets while mitigating the environmental burden associated with tailings stockpiles, the use of tailings as supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) to partially replace ordinary Portland cement (OPC) has received considerable attention. title: Hybrid metaheuristic NNHGS algorithm for PID controller tuning in UAVs
abstract: Controller tuning for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is a challenging task due to their nonlinear and coupled dynamics. This study validates the hybrid Neural-Network Hunger Games Search (NNHGS) algorithm, which integrates a Kohonen neural network with the Hunger Games Search (HGS) metaheuristic to dynamically adapt the search space during optimization. abstract: Rice security is at the center of national defense because of the growing geopolitical unrest in the Asia-Pacific region, especially in the South China Sea, which puts Indonesia’s food supply at risk through marine channels. Using a Systematic Literature Review in accordance with PRISMA 2020, this study synthesizes 63 peer-reviewed articles, official documents, and institutional reports from Scopus, Web of Science, ProQuest, and regional databases to develop an integrated defense logistics strategy for Indonesian rice security. This study explored teachers’ latent resistance to AI-supported teaching by examining how teachers described AI use, set professional boundaries, justified cautious or selective engagement, and identified conditions that might reduce such resistance. abstract: ABSTRACT This study advances groundwater nitrate management from correlation-based predictions toward causation-based prescriptions, enabling direct translation of scientific modeling outputs into actionable land use management strategies. A nationwide dataset of 3,569 groundwater well samples collected across South Korea between 2023 and 2024 was integrated with high-resolution land use, elevation, and hydrogeologic unit data. abstract: Accurately predicting Ultimate Bearing Capacity (UBC) is crucial for the safe and efficient design of foundations in geotechnical engineering. Yet, traditional methods remain time-consuming, costly, and environmentally disruptive. This study applies Support Vector Machine (SVM) models to develop a data-driven predictive framework for UBC estimation using optimized feature selection techniques and validated using experimental data and Finite Element Method (FEM). abstract: The northern boundary of the African plate is one of the most complex and segmented plate boundary systems worldwide, extending from the Azores Triple Junction in the Mid-Atlantic Ocean to the Gulf of Aqaba in the eastern Mediterranean. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems along the Guangdong coastline serve as a vital blue carbon sink, yet their carbon sequestration potential under changing climatic conditions requires rigorous assessment and forward-looking evaluation. This study develops an integrated framework combining remote sensing techniques and spatial modeling approaches to quantify historical changes and project future trajectories of mangrove blue carbon stocks in Guangdong Province, China. abstract: Real-time assessment of fish feeding intensity is essential for demand-based feeding in intensive aquaculture, yet existing methods rely on external spectrogram preprocessing and large annotated datasets, limiting practical deployment. This study proposes an end-to-end approach that reformulates feeding intensity recognition as an audio instruction-following task using the multimodal large language model Qwen2.5-Omni-3B. abstract: Spectral reconstruction from RGB images has become an essential approach for enhancing plant disease detection, particularly when hyperspectral data are not readily available. This study proposes a novel framework that reconstructs 3D hyperspectral cube from RGB oil palm leaf images by integrating Visible (VIS) and Near-Infrared (NIR) bands. abstract: Dissolved oxygen (DO) is a key indicator for assessing the ecological health of nearshore harbors and managing the aquatic environment. Its concentration dynamics are governed by the nonlinear coupling of multiple factors, and obtaining accurate, interpretable estimates remains a central challenge in water quality modeling. abstract: Southeast Asia faces a critical energy trilemma of rapidly rising electricity demand, persistent fossil fuel dependence, and increasingly ambitious decarbonization targets. abstract: ABSTRACT The conversion of biomass into biofuels is a crucial step towards sustainable energy transitions. These processes are multi‐scale phenomena that require advanced computational modeling. This study synthesizes bibliometric analysis and visualization to examine the scientific advancements and future trends in computational modeling for biomass‐to‐biofuel transformation. title: Photochemical Aging of Atmospheric Black Carbon Promotes Nitrate Coating in a Chinese Megacity
abstract: Abstract Black carbon (BC) aerosol critically influences climate and haze, yet the mechanisms driving its coating and light absorption enhancement remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Industrial pump units require condition recognition models that remain reliable under measurement noise and can reject health states that are not observed during training. abstract: Abstract Accurate representation of bead geometry is essential for establishing reliable process-geometry relationships in laser-directed energy deposition (L-DED). In contrast to existing approaches that focus on constructing complete process maps within a single manufacturing process, this work leverages experimentally derived scalar bead descriptors (width, height, and area) from a source process to enable data-efficient reconstruction of process maps for a different target manufacturing process. abstract: Introduction Seismic facies segmentation is a fundamental step in subsurface geological modeling, but reported accuracies are difficult to compare because random splits of overlapping patches can leak spatial information across training and test sets. abstract: While machine learning (ML) models have shown considerable promise for modelling complex environmental phenomena such as floods, their adoption in flood mapping is often constrained by limited interpretability. This study develops an integrated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-enhanced framework for satellite-based flood extent mapping using multispectral and topographic variables. abstract: Abstract Escherichia coli is a major commensal and opportunistic pathogen inhabiting the gastrointestinal tract of warm-blooded animals, including marine mammals. Among its lineages, sequence type 131 (ST131) is a globally disseminated high-risk clone associated with severe infections. Prophages are common in intestinal bacteria, and their induction has been hypothesized to influence bacterial population dynamics and gut homeostasis. abstract: This study assesses how the China-Thailand Railway may reshape Thailand's trade with Guangxi by altering the relative competitiveness of road, rail, and sea freight. abstract: The Lessepsian round herring Etrumeus golanii is increasingly recorded in the Aegean Sea, but its body shape has not been quantitatively compared with that of native small pelagic fishes occurring in the same assemblage. In this study, the body shape of E. golanii , Engraulis encrasicolus , and Sardina pilchardus was examined using 281 specimens collected from the same purse seine haul in the southeastern Aegean Sea. abstract: Large-scale eradication of the invasive Spartina alterniflora on China’s coasts is implemented to restore wetland ecosystems, yet it introduces a critical yet overlooked environmental trade-off: massive plant residue input may destabilize sediment organic carbon (SOC), the core part of coastal blue carbon.
