title: Extreme North American heatwaves in 1941 and 2021 drove widespread but contrasting impacts
abstract: The 2021 Western North American heatwave was among the most extreme heatwaves ever recorded. Recent work has identified one event of comparable magnitude and location in 1941. However, little is known about the impacts of the 1941 heatwave. Here we review 357 issues of 25 news publications from before, during, and after the 1941 heatwave, and we uncover widespread impacts including mortality, water shortages, crop damages, wildfires, flooding, and changes to social customs and behaviours. title: Blue Cities, Green Laws: Legal Models for Urban Climate Resilience in the Global South
abstract: Blue cities are cities that plan themselves around water rather than against it: rainwater is stored, recycled and reused, streets and parks are given permeable surfaces, wetlands and lakes are protected and restored, and coastal settlements are defended by mangrove belts and flood-resistant construction. Rivers, lakes, drainage, drinking water supply, sewage and storm water are treated as one interconnected system, and nature-based solutions such as rain gardens, bioswales and urban forests are preferred to concrete drains that push water downstream. abstract: Background: Quota-based fisheries management aims to reconcile stock conservation with efficient access, yet harvesting entitlements may evolve from public allocations into asset-like interests. abstract: GEDSI groups in coastal areas still face limited access to information, training, technology, and decision-making in productive economic activities, including whiteleg shrimp farming. This community service activity aimed to improve the knowledge and understanding of GEDSI groups in Dadap Village, Sambelia District, East Lombok Regency, regarding sustainable, inclusive, and environmentally friendly whiteleg shrimp farming practices. abstract: Informal patron-client arrangements in capture fisheries can combine vessel finance, employment, social assistance, and market control, creating both protection and dependency. This study examined how boat owner-crew labor relations are reproduced and how a feasible transformation could be designed at Tenau Coastal Fishing Port and Oeba Fish Landing Base, Kupang City, Indonesia. abstract: A range of recent studies have developed methods and data to attribute past and present global temperature change to individual emitters. We perform simulations that attribute the amount of global warming due to corporations, governments and other entities into the future. We utilize the Finite Amplitude Impulse Response (FaIR) model run until 2500, and the Carbon Majors dataset, a database with the emissions history associated with the top 178 oil, gas, coal, and cement producers. abstract: ABSTRACT Sirenians are a lineage of herbivorous marine mammals morphologically specialized for exploiting aquatic vegetation in shallow‐water habitats. In manatees ( Trichechus ), continuous horizontal tooth replacement may represent a solution for mitigating heavy dental wear incurred by a diet of abrasive plant material. In this study, we examine patterns of dental wear in manatees by quantifying two properties of the occlusal surface across the dental arcade. abstract: Understanding the richness and distribution of Contracaecum spp. in aquatic ecosystems is important because these zoonotic nematodes circulate through complex food webs involving invertebrates, fish, birds, and occasionally humans. This study investigated the species richness and distribution of Contracaecum spp. in Iranian waters through a literature review combined with morphological and molecular characterisation of adult specimens collected from piscivorous birds. title: Improving landcover data governance in developing countries
abstract: Recent advances in open-access satellite imagery and processing tools have accelerated the production of national-scale landcover (LC) maps for land use planning and ecological monitoring. While such technological democratisation has expanded analytical capacity, it has also generated a new governance challenge: the coexistence of multiple, independently produced LC datasets without institutional coordination or custodianship. title: STRENGTHENING PEDIATRIC EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS IN REMOTE AND EMERGING TOURISM DESTINATIONS UNDER SAUDI VISION 2030
abstract: Saudi Arabia's rapid development of remote coastal, desert and heritage tourism destinations create a distinctive pediatric emergency preparedness challenge. Children differ from adults in airway anatomy, physiology, medication dosing, equipment needs, communication and psychosocial response; low-frequency, high-acuity events can therefore expose serious capability gaps in isolated facilities. title: Travel Motivations and Destination Attributes in Online Tourist Reviews: A Qualitative Study of Cittaslow Demre, Antalya
abstract: This study examines how visitors describe their travel motivations, destination experiences, and practical concerns in online reviews of Demre, Antalya. The researchers organized 210 unique TripAdvisor reviews, posted between 1 January 2021 and 1 July 2026 across five attraction groups, in a structured analytical matrix; stated visits range from 2020 to 2026. abstract: This article investigates the discursive construction of ideological antagonism in the speeches of Nigel Farage (UK), Marine Le Pen (France), and Santiago Abascal (Spain), focusing on how each leader produces and legitimizes polarized “us-versus-them” frameworks. Drawing from Critical Discourse Analysis (van Dijk, 1998; Wodak, 2015), the study examines a small corpus of high-stakes public speeches during electoral or national moments in which the “enemy” is explicitly named–be it immigrants, elites, supranational institutions, or political rivals. title: POPULATION GROWTH AND THE AVAILABILITY OF SOCIO-COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE CENTRAL ARRONDISSEMENT OF GRAND-POPO, BENIN
abstract: This study analyzes the impact of population growth on the availability of socio-community infrastructure in the central district of Grand-Popo, Benin. It is based on a review of existing literature and a field survey of 227 households in the Onkuihoué, Houssoukouè, and Ewe-Condji neighborhoods. abstract: : Across Europe, various strategies are employed to manage escalating natural hazard risk. While long-standing threats like flooding and wildfires have historically impacted populations and property, the increasing intensity and frequency of these events, driven by climate change, are necessitating more proactive risk management, sometimes involving community relocation. abstract: Against the backdrop of the in-depth advancement of the Silk Road Economic Belt initiative, environmental protection in the overseas investment of Chinese enterprises has increasingly attracted the attention of the international community. From the perspective of international environmental law governance, this paper systematically examines the basic principles that should be established for the environmental legal system of the Silk Road Economic Belt. title: Malay Manuscripts as Cultural Memory: Islamic Knowledge Transmission in the Malay-Indonesian World
abstract: This article examines Malay manuscripts as media of cultural memory in the transmission of Islamic knowledge in the Malay-Indonesian world. Rather than treating manuscripts only as philological sources, material objects, or historical documents, it asks how material form, textual patterning, and social use jointly stabilize knowledge across generations. title: Multifaceted dynamics in variety and seed choices: the case of pumpkin farmers in northern Vietnam
abstract: Abstract Smallholder farmers’ crop variety and seed choices shape agro-biodiversity and livelihood sustainability. However, existing studies often overlook the dynamic, context-specific nature of these choices. We explored how introductions of hybrid pumpkin affected farmers’ pumpkin variety choices, seed sourcing, and seed management strategies across spatial and temporal contexts. We interviewed 72 stakeholders and 178 households from 3 ethnic groups in 15 villages at 2 altitudes in northern Vietnam. title: Environmental Degradation and Tyre Waste Management Challenges in Nigerian Cities
abstract: The rapid pace of urbanization and vehicular growth in Nigerian cities has resulted in a substantial surge in end-of-life tyres (ELTs), many of which are indiscriminately discarded in open spaces, drainage channels, and public environments. These ELTs constitute a mounting environmental hazard, contributing significantly to soil, air, and water contamination, while also posing risks to public health and urban infrastructure. Although environmental protection frameworks exist in Nigeria, there remains a notable absence of targeted policies specifically addressing the management of scrap tyres.

title: Sources and environmental impacts of Kura River pollution under anthropogenic pressures in Azerbaijan
abstract: The Kura River is Azerbaijan’s principal river system and supports drinking-water supply, irrigation, hydropower, fisheries and riverine ecosystems. At the same time, its transboundary character and intensive human use make it vulnerable to multiple forms of pollution. This study examines the principal anthropogenic sources of Kura River pollution and their environmental implications by integrating two independently prepared research dossiers with a targeted review of scientific and institutional literature. abstract: This paper studies the dilemma and optimisation ideas of liability division in international cargo multimodal transport. It will not provide new empirical data but will collect existing legal and policy research on multimodal liability systems to clarify how uniform, network and modified systems distribute responsibility, and where practical and doctrinal gaps exist. abstract: Territorial well-being analysis requires integrating two complementary families of information: objective indicators (equipment, composite quality-of-life scores) that characterize structural conditions, and subjective perceptions (citizen survey verbatims, interviews) that reflect lived experience. abstract: In recent years, the world has witnessed an increase in both the frequency and severity of natural disasters. These disasters have had devastating effects on communities, thereby causing loss of life, displacement of people, and destruction of infrastructures. abstract: Improving employee performance is essential for strengthening public service delivery, and this concern underlies the present research at Kantor Kesyahbandaran dan Otoritas Pelabuhan Kelas IV Bengkalis. Although the institution already applies a system of reward and punishment intended to raise employee performance, whether this system actually works as intended had not yet been tested empirically. abstract: The ultimatum game (UG) and the dictator game (DG) are two of the most prominent tools in experimental and behavioural social sciences. Originally designed to study bargaining behaviour and decision-making in economics, these simple yet versatile scripts have come to be viewed by many as reliable instruments for measuring prosocial preferences, such as altruism, generosity, or sensitivity to social norms. abstract: Growing sustainability claims in tourism have intensified concerns about credibility and greenwashing. abstract: The rapid expansion of the nickel processing industry in Morowali Regency has intensified environmental degradation and contributed to increasing cases of Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) among local communities. abstract: Abstract What socio‐economic, cultural, subjective, or institutional factors might motivate a socially marginalized, economically constrained fisher to voluntarily release a highly valuable catch such as a sawfish? This study looked at fishers' attitudes (ability, willingness, and challenges) toward the live release of Critically Endangered sawfish in Bangladesh. title: Assessing the Sustainability Performance of Fishing Harbors Under Uncertainty: A Gaussian‐Neutrosophic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Fishing harbors are increasingly required to meet sustainability expectations associated with the environmental, social, and economic development goals. Accordingly, assessing their sustainability performance has become an important concern for both policymakers, harbor operating organizations, and harbor managers. This study develops a decision support system (DSS) within a neutrosophic environment to evaluate the sustainability performance of small‐scale fishing harbors. title: Routing strategies in container shipping: a simulation approach for managing port-skipping
abstract: The maritime network plays a crucial role for all economic sectors, but there are various events (such as port congestion, geopolitical tensions, extreme weather, …) that can affect the scheduling of maritime services. This could cause a decrease in service quality (which impacts on the image of the shipping company) and an increase in costs. To try to reduce the effects of these situations, a shipping company can decide to adopt a port-skipping strategy. abstract: Rapid and precise design review is imperative during the bidding phase of offshore wind projects; however, reliance on PDF-only drawings, which lack extractable geometric data, poses significant challenges. Conventional manual methods for digitizing these documents and estimating steel quantities are labor-intensive and error-prone, making it difficult to produce accurate quantity takeoffs within the tight timelines of the bidding phase. abstract: Atmospheric water generation (AWG) yield is typically treated as a fixed hardware property. However, for power-constrained condensation devices, the binding design variable is how cooling budgets are allocated across time and air mass. abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater discharge plays a key role in maintaining habitat suitability for cold‐water fish by generating streamflow and modulating temperatures. However, the thermal influence depends on groundwater source depth and how far groundwater travels from the point of discharge to a receiving stream. In the unglaciated Kenai Peninsula Lowlands (KPL), Alaska, groundwater originates from shallow hillslope groundwater (HGW) or deeper aquifer‐outcrop groundwater (AOGW) sources. title: Digital Twins for Smart Governance and Policy Directions in Smart Cities
abstract: The rapid urbanization of the 21st century has intensified pressure on cities to address challenges in housing, transportation, healthcare, energy, and waste management, all of which are compounded by climate change and increasing inequality. In response, smart cities have emerged as a solution that leverages technology to enhance governance and resource efficiency. A key innovation within this framework is the digital twin, a dynamic, real-time virtual replica of urban systems that enables simulation, prediction, and evidence-based policymaking. abstract: Preserving water quality has become a critical priority due to the increasing pressure on water resources from population growth, production activities and climate change. This article reviews recent studies on water quality monitoring in lakes, rivers and reservoirs, with a focus on lessons relevant to local decision-making. Using a structured literature review approach, we synthesised and interpreted research on water quality monitoring systems used in aquatic ecosystems affected by eutrophication and turbidity. title: Taxonomic and Cytogenetic Complexity Complicate Forecasts of Climate-Driven Habitat Change in Rhexia (Melastomataceae)
abstract: Abstract Rhexia (Melastomataceae), a temperate genus composed of 13 species in eastern North America, provides a useful system for evaluating how taxonomic and cytogenetic complexity influence projections of climate-driven habitat change. Ecological niche models (ENMs) incorporating climatic and edaphic variables were used to estimate current and future habitat suitability for diploid, polyploid, and mixed-cytotype species. title: A narrative synthesis of approaches for communicating environmental evidence to decision-makers in the context of environmental impact assessments
abstract: : Environmental impact assessments (EIAs) are tools used for assessing the social, environmental, health, and economic impact of development projects. These assessments are intended to inform evidence-based decision-making, yet failures to efficiently communicate evidence to practitioners limit their value. While researchers have worked towards identifying best practices for communicating evidence to decision-makers, there are still relatively few reviews on the topic, especially within the EIA context. title: The embodiment of Balinese Hindu philosophy “ Tri Hita Karana ” in contemporary visual art: case study on Mangu Putra’s painting
abstract: The foundational Balinese Hindu philosophy Tri Hita Karana, which emphasizes harmonious relations among the divine (Parahyangan), humanity (Pawongan), and the environment (Palemahan), has long governed Balinese socio-cultural practices, spatial planning, and customary law. However, how this philosophical framework is formalized and translated into the painterly strategies of contemporary fine art remains insufficiently explored. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of climate change on rice transplanting timings in Japan, focusing on Hyogo and Niigata Prefectures. Using time‐series Sentinel‐1 SAR imagery, we identified transplanting dates based on the sharp decrease in backscatter coefficients during the ponding period. abstract: ABSTRACT Rifts host a substantial proportion of the world's hydrocarbon resources because lithospheric extension commonly generates sustained subsidence, thick sedimentary fills and laterally connected migration systems that enhance petroleum‐system efficiency. title: An Exploratory Accounting Approach for Balancing Environmental Impacts of Point and Diffuse Sources in Nitrogen Trading
abstract: Nutrient trading between point and diffuse sources of nutrients offers an integrated watershed nutrient management approach to achieve nutrient reduction goals that benefit both the terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. This market-based approach requires quantification of the environmental impacts of nutrients derived from different sources. This environmental impact depends on the forms, concentrations, loads, transport, and processing of nutrients within waterways. title: Wind Energy and Green Hydrogen Production: A Sustainable Vision for Nigeria
abstract: The planet cannot survive without a sustainable approach to development, and global energy systems are rapidly evolving to meet the growing demand for clean, renewable alternatives. In this context, wind energy plays a crucial role, particularly in regions rich in abundant wind resources. Since wind energy is free and has no emissions, it can provide the electricity needed to manufacture green hydrogen (GH2), which makes the combination of wind and hydrogen production a promising solution in the energy transition. title: Brief communication: Limitations of medical X-ray computed tomography for estimating ice content in permafrost samples
abstract: X-ray Computed tomography (CT) is increasingly used to estimate ice contents in permafrost samples. In this study, CT-derived estimates of volumetric ice content obtained from medical CT scans were compared with laboratory measurements for 261 samples from northern Canada (Nunavut and Yukon). The results shows that medical CT systematically underestimates ice content in sediment-rich and organic-poor samples, and overestimated it in ice-rich, organic-rich samples. abstract: Clear adaptation outcomes are essential for driving climate action and assessing progress. However, developing a shared vision of desirable adaptation outcomes and the steps to achieve them requires a shared understanding of what constitutes a well-adapted place and what resources are needed to enable communities to create and implement such visions. The third Scottish National Adaptation Plan (SNAP3) has “communities creating climate resilient places” as a key outcome. abstract: Abstract The Planetary Boundaries framework defines a Safe Operating Space for humanity by setting biophysical boundaries to critical Earth System components, including the water cycle. This framework is a promising paradigm to address the challenges posed by increasing anthropogenic pressures and climate change impacts on water systems. title: Mixed-species biofilms in food systems: from community assembly to ecology-informed management
abstract: Biofilms in food-processing environments present multifaceted challenges for food safety, quality, and public health. These microbial communities, forming on a variety of surfaces within food-processing facilities, are responsible for persistent contamination, increased tolerance to cleaning and disinfection, and the transmission of spoilage organisms and pathogens. abstract: In the last decades, political theorists have turned their attention to territorial rights and their normative justification. Here I suggest that, despite their differences, normative theories of territory share five assumptions: statism, groupism, sedentarism, anthropocentrism and resourcism. abstract: Virus-virus interactions can profoundly shape viral ecology and evolution, yet they remain poorly understood, particularly in haloarchaea. Upon characterization of a spindle-shaped virus, Tebenquiche spindle-shaped virus 1 (Tebi-SV1), isolated from Halorubrum strain TLS-6, we detected the presence of a second virus, Tebenquiche pleomorphic virus 1 (Tebi-PV1), that coinfects host cells. abstract: This study utilized the Scopus database to examine 2,626 publications published between 2014 and 2024, involving 7,712 authors from 797 different sources, with an annual growth rate of 11.48%, focusing on the environmental impacts of mining activities. The analysis revealed the evolution of scientific research over time by identifying the most influential journals, as well as the most active countries, while highlighting the core concepts that define this research field. abstract: The rapid growth of tourism and urban activities has significantly increased household waste generation in Bali, while existing waste management systems face persistent capacity and behavioral challenges. Although socio-economic determinants of waste behavior have been widely examined, empirical studies that explicitly link household sustainability perceptions to community-based waste management mechanisms, including TPS3R, remain limited. abstract: The legal protection of conservation areas has become increasingly important in achieving sustainable tourism, yet previous studies have generally examined conservation law enforcement, protected area management, and sustainable tourism separately. This study examines the effectiveness of legal protection for the Ujung Kulon National Park ecosystem in supporting sustainable tourism development. abstract: Emys orbicularis is a freshwater ectotherm turtle sensitive to climatic variation and landscape quality. Because this species is structured into several evolutionary lineages with distinct biogeographic histories, modelling it as a single unit may obscure lineage-specific responses to climate change. abstract: Diarrhea remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality for children under five, despite reductions in its global burden in recent decades. However, climate change, and its associated meteorological conditions - heavy rainfall, temperature, flooding - has the potential to impede or reverse progress, particularly in low-income, climate-vulnerable communities. title: Optimising the Pioneer Shipping Route Considering Wave Variations
abstract: Pioneer shipping is a government-subsidised maritime services that connect remote areas in the Indonesian Archipelago. This paper applied a genetic algorithm variant to optimise pioneer shipping routes while accounting for variability in wave conditions. The algorithm is implemented on a real shipping network in East Java comprising two main routes, and several improvement scenarios are evaluated, including optimisation of existing routes, route fractioning, and route merging. title: RiverFlow Analyzer: A python-based, multi-algorithm optical flow tool for River surface velocity estimation
abstract: Surface flow velocity is a fundamental variable for river monitoring, discharge assessment, and flood analysis, but conventional in situ measurements remain difficult to acquire during hazardous or rapidly evolving flow conditions. We present RiverFlow Analyzer , a Python-based framework for non-intrusive river surface velocimetry from video data, designed to integrate geometric rectification and multi-algorithm optical flow analysis within a single workflow. abstract: Hydromorphological (HyMo) conditions are increasingly recognized as key drivers of ecological quality in lakes and reservoirs, yet their role in Mediterranean systems remains poorly understood. abstract: Daily to seasonal weather information remains rare in Quaternary science, because proxy archives typically resolve only seasonal or annual means. abstract: Abstract Research on the fishing industry typically centres the male-dominated catching sector, neglecting the post-harvest fishery historically sustained by fishermen’s wives. This study explores social change and migration in Scotland’s fish-processing sector, in Northeast Scotland, where non-UK workers comprised up to 70% of the processing workforce in 2019, the highest regional proportion in the UK (Seafish 2019). title: Snake diversity based on rescue records in urban Jaipur, Rajasthan, India
abstract: We documented the snakes of Jaipur City, Rajasthan, India, using rescue records generated through a structured volunteer network, comprising primary data collected between January 2024 and October 2025, supplemented by historical records. A total of 787 primary rescue events along with past records (before January 2024), yielded records of 21 snake species across six families, including three venomous and 18 non-venomous taxa. Rescue records were dominated by Naja naja (65.4% of all rescues), while other frequently recorded species included Platyceps ventromaculatus and Spalerosophis atriceps.

abstract: Background: The Sebatik–Tawau borderland presents an integration paradox in which intensive social and economic interactions coexist with underdeveloped tourism governance and legal mobility facilitation. Objective: This study examines how tourism governance and regional security shape border integration and formulates an applicable governance framework for the Sebatik–Tawau borderland. abstract: Biological invasions are often recognised only after ecological damage has become visible in the wild, even though the human-mediated processes that drive introductions may already be underway through private rearing, trade, and release. abstract: ABSTRACT Informed by scholarship on climate change and polar bears, this paper analyses alternatives to images of polar bears stranded on ice floes. The empirical frame of reference is recent prize‐winning images and photo essays in popular media, drawn from a selection of news reports on targeted websites. abstract: Rural elementary science education presents a wide array of opportunities to provide connection between classroom learning and lived experiences. abstract: Advances in subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) forecasting have broad socioeconomic benefits. Stratospheric variability has been identified as a major source of surface predictability on S2S timescales, yet its influence on forecasting North American cold extremes has not been fully understood. abstract: Abstract Numerical simulations are performed for hypervelocity water entry of spherical projectiles, validated against experimental data. The scaling of principal phenomena is investigated using time histories of the pressure at the stagnation point, the axial portion of the shock wave, and the radial portion of the shock wave. The scaling analysis of the pressure is performed via a parameter sweep of projectile impact velocity, density, diameter, and impact kinetic energy. title: The Juliánov Housing Estate in Brno – Its Art and Landscape Architecture
abstract: The study deals with public space in the Juliánov housing estate in Brno, built in the 1960s, examining it as an exceptionally coherent environment where architecture, landscape and visual art – including a rare ensemble of functional sculptures – were conceived as an integrated whole. Based on archival research, fieldwork and comparative analysis, it interprets Juliánov as a Gesamtkunstwerk and an important reference for the assessment and preservation of post-war housing ensembles.

title: Benchmarking control strategies for wave energy converters: From idealised knowledge to realistic operation
abstract: Maximising energy extraction in wave energy converters remains challenging due to the non-causal nature of the optimal control, complex interactions and real-time constraints. This paper presents a benchmarking of four strategies: LiTe-Con, LiTe-Con+, model predictive control (MPC) and spectral control. The evaluation transitions from idealised scenarios with perfect knowledge of the wave excitation force to realistic conditions accounting for estimation and forecasting. The study is conducted using a 1:20 scale pitching WEC model subjected to representative wave climates in the Gulf of Biscay

title: Safeguarding Vietnamese Traditional Musical Instruments in the Digital Era: A Cultural Management Perspective
abstract: Safeguarding Vietnamese traditional musical instruments in the digital era requires management of more than physical objects or isolated digital files; the relevant unit is a living heritage ecosystem comprising instruments, sound, skills, knowledge, context, and communities of practice. Objective: This study examines how digital technologies can support the safeguarding of Vietnamese traditional musical instruments and develops a cultural management framework for linking digital resources with living heritage continuity. Methods: A structured narrative review was combined with policy analysis
journal: Journal of Social Science and Human Research Studies

title: The Persistent Fragmentation of Gulf Foreign Aid: Bilateralism and the Limits of Regional Humanitarian Coordination
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines why Gulf foreign aid has remained predominantly bilateral and fragmented since its emergence in the 1960s, despite the establishment of regional institutions, recurring regional crises and repeated calls for greater coordination. Bilateralism has been a persistent and defining feature of Gulf aid, and no effective regional humanitarian coordination mechanism has emerged even as Gulf donors have expanded and professionalised their aid institutions. Although Gulf states have occasionally cooperated on specific initiatives, such cooperation has remained episodic, info

title: Factores asociados a desenlaces adversos en pacientes con falla cardíaca crónica hospitalizados por SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19
abstract: Introducción: La infección por SARS-CoV-2 ha llevado a peores desenlaces en pacientes con cardiopatías.Objetivo: Identificar factores al ingreso hospitalario asociados a UCI, ventilación mecánica y muerte en pacientes con antecedente de falla cardíaca hospitalizados por SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19. title: Polyoxymethylene ethers as attractive hydrogen transport vectors? - Concept evaluation and steam reforming investigations
abstract: The efficient and safe transportation of renewable hydrogen remains a major challenge. Polyoxymethylene dimethyl ethers (OMEs) might be promising hydrogen transport vectors due to their liquid state at ambient conditions, low toxicity and high technical hydrogen capacity. However, two major bottlenecks for their application are identified: the direct synthesis of OMEs from CO 2 and H 2 and the catalytic steam reforming of OMEs for hydrogen release, which remains largely unexplored. title: ABCC9/SUR2 has a Complex Expression Pattern in Human Brain Gliovascular Unit Cells, Including Astrocytes
abstract: The ABCC9 gene and its cognate protein SUR2 play important roles in neurovascular coupling and are implicated in hippocampal sclerosis of aging (HS-Aging). However, prior studies have not focused on human brain SUR2 expression or SUR2 in glial cells. Here we analyzed cell type-specific ABCC9/SUR2 expression patterns, and correlation with known genetic risk variants, using multiple data sets and a novel antiserum. Existing single-nucleus RNA sequencing data sets and new spatial transcriptomics data indicated that SUR2 transcripts were expressed primarily in human brain pericytes, astrocytes, sm

title: Flash floods in traditionally less flood prone areas of southeastern Bangladesh
abstract: The growing threat of climate-driven urban flash floods signifies the need for rapid damage assessment tools. Understanding the impacts of sudden floods on populations and croplands in historically less flood-prone regions is essential for effective risk management. This study highlights the significant impact of the flood event that began on August 20, 2024, affecting three southeastern districts of Bangladesh Noakhali, Feni, and Cumilla that had experienced minimal flooding in the past three decades. Using Google Earth Engine and Synthetic Aperture Radar images, we mapped the extent of the f
institutions: Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

title: Climate change interventions for racialized communities: A global scoping review of equity‑focused policies and programs
abstract: Climate change disproportionately affects racialized communities, yet evidence on interventions designed to address these inequities remains fragmented. This scoping review maps the global landscape of climate-related interventions targeting racialized populations, focusing on intervention types, outcomes, and equity considerations. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched ten academic and policy databases for peer-reviewed and grey literature published between 2000 and 2025. Eighty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. Research increased substantially after 2019, although most studies

title: Order, security, and the rule of law: A global bibliometric analysis with implications for the Philippine context
abstract: This study aims to map the intellectual structure and development of research on the implementation of the rule of law through order and security, with particular attention to its relevance to the Philippine governance context. A qualitative descriptive bibliometric approach was employed to examine scholarly publications retrieved from Dimensions AI, Google Scholar, and selected secondary sources. Bibliographic data were analyzed using VOSviewer to identify publication trends, thematic concentrations, keyword relationships, and patterns of intellectual development. The findings indicate growin

title: Reforming Housing Policy, Regional Deliberation, and Governance
abstract: Problem, research strategy, and findings Metropolitan planning organizations (MPOs) have rarely taken on equity or housing agendas in the United States; rather, structural and political conditions have allowed for regional governance to be characterized by interjurisdictional competition or center on economic development goals. Expanding on research examining the contentious implementation of state housing reforms, I compared the processes through which the Bay Area and Southern California have recently formulated and implemented their regional housing allocations. Centering on public meetings
journal: Journal of the American Planning Association

title: Typology and differentiated development paths of rural revitalization in Hebei counties from an urban rural system perspective
abstract: Facing the strategic requirement of promoting rural revitalization in a region-based and categorized manner under the 15th Five-Year Plan, and considering the complex natural conditions and remarkable regional disparities in Hebei Province, exploring differentiated pathways for rural revitalization is of great practical significance. Taking 164 county-level administrative units in Hebei Province as the research objects, this study starts from the perspective of urban-rural system integration. title: Manganese‐Cobalt Oxides on Carbon Paper Self‐Supported Electrodes With Bimetallic Synergy and Oxygen Vacancies for Highly Efficient Water Oxidation
abstract: The development of efficient and durable non‐noble metal electrocatalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a critical challenge due to the sluggish four‐electron kinetics and the reliance on scarce iridium/ruthenium‐based materials. Herein, we report a facile one‐step calcination method to fabricate self‐supported manganese‐cobalt oxide electrodes on carbon paper (MnCoO x /CP) with tailored oxygen vacancies (O v ) and electronic structures. title: The 2026 cold wave brought northern Fennoscandia its coldest 2‐week period since 1987
abstract: Abstract During late December 2025 and January 2026, a severe and long‐lasting cold wave affected northern Fennoscandia. In this article, we aim to quantify the extremity of the 2026 cold wave and evaluate the atmospheric conditions that led to the persistent cold anomalies. Analysis of in situ temperature observations and ERA5 reanalysis indicates that the 14‐day period between 31 December and 13 January was the coldest 2‐week period since 1987 over a large area, and regionally since at least 1964. title: Global patterns of genetic diversity and evolution in chikungunya virus E2 glycoprotein
abstract: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of E2 genetic diversity using a dataset of sequences collected across regions, hosts, and epidemic periods. title: Cultural codes in Kazakh and Nogai traditional dress: a comparative semiotic analysis of museum and documentary evidence
abstract: Introduction Traditional dress constitutes an important medium through which cultural meanings, social identities, and collective memory become materially and visually communicable. This study examines cultural codes in Kazakh and Nogai traditional dress through a qualitative, comparative, and interpretive approach, focusing on how clothing communicated gender, social status, ritual transition, and collective belonging within historically situated cultural contexts. Cultural codes are understood here as socially recognizable configurations of visual, material, and embodied signs through which

title: Empowering edge intelligence through reparameterized lightweight transformers and distributed inference
abstract: Deploying advanced transformer-based models on resource-constrained edge devices remains a significant challenge due to their high memory footprint and substantial compute requirements. In this paper, we propose a reparameterized transformer framework that integrates High-Rank Factorization (HRF) during training, layer merging at inference, and dynamic, load-balanced distributed inference across multiple devices. title: Valuing and Protecting Inland Fisheries and Biodiversity for Livelihoods and Nutrition
abstract: Inland fisheries provide livelihood, nutritional, and leisure opportunities to people around the world; associated biodiversity and functioning freshwater ecosystems are necessary for sustainable inland fisheries. These connections and contributions, however, have largely been overlooked or under-appreciated by national and international development and conservation communities. As a result, inland fisheries, associated biodiversity, and the people that depend on them are at risk. title: Building National Analytics Capacity: Advances and Future Pathways
abstract: The capacity of nations to collect, govern, analyse and act upon data has become a defining determinant of public value, competitiveness and resilience. This paper synthesises the state of the art in national analytics capacity, the interlocking set of infrastructures, human capital, institutional and governance arrangements that allow a country to convert data into decisions at scale, and charts a forward-looking research agenda. We situate the discussion in the momentum generated by the United Nations “data revolution” agenda and the World Bank’s framing of data as a resource for development
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH

title: State-Subsidized Maritime Connectivity and Local Welfare: A Study of Pioneer Shipping Programs in Indonesia
abstract: As an archipelagic nation, Indonesia's maritime connectivity is a constitutional mandate for social justice. This study evaluates the impact of the Pioneer Shipping Subsidy (PSS) program on maritime access justice and public governance in 3T (Underdeveloped, Outermost, Frontier) regions. Using a mixed-methods socio-legal approach, data were collected between January 2020 and December 2023 across seven provinces (South Sumatra, Riau Islands, South Kalimantan, NTB, NTT, Maluku, and West Papua) involving a survey of N=75 stakeholders and in-depth interviews. title: Transitions in institutions for water allocation and rights: path dependence and performance
abstract: ABSTRACT Many countries are already contending with relative water shortage where water demand structurally exceeds availability. Demographic and economic growth combined with deteriorating catchments and climate change will affect more countries and deepen this stress. To manage allocation effectively, institutional instruments are applied, comprising regulatory, economic and collective-action measures. title: Wireless sensor network coverage optimization based on the innovative enhanced whale optimization algorithm
abstract: Abstract In Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), optimizing network coverage is crucial for improving performance in applications such as environmental monitoring, surveillance, and socio-economic cyber systems. Although the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) has demonstrated potential as a swarm-based optimization technique, it suffers from limitations such as inadequate exploration capability and a tendency to become trapped in local optima, particularly under random sensor-node deployment, resulting in suboptimal coverage. title: Physics-guided interpretable ensemble learning for daily reference evapotranspiration estimation in arid regions
abstract: Dependable estimates of reference evapotranspiration (ETo) are fundamental to managing water sustainably across arid regions, yet conventional empirical methods have limited capacity to represent the complex non-linear interactions among meteorological variables governing ETo dynamics. This study develops a physics-guided interpretable ensemble learning framework that integrates rule-based (RuleFit) modeling, Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Generalized Simulated Annealing (GenSA) optimization, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). title: Overcoming urban climate injustice: synthesising global pathways and principles
abstract: Urban communities continue to face unequal exposure to climate impacts and exclusionary governance; however, cities are increasingly deploying joint mitigation and adaptation interventions. This paper presents a rapid review of global case studies to map promising pathways for achieving urban climate justice. Interrogating evidence, we find that the core pillars of justice—distributive, procedural, and recognitional—are being engaged with in climate action. Additionally, our conceptual framework integrates epistemic and restorative justice to address deeply rooted systemic exclusions. We argue

title: The Resilient Mercantile Hub: An Evidence-Derived Architectural and Governance Framework for Sustainable Waterfront Regeneration in Port Harcourt, Nigeria
abstract: This article develops and presents the Resilient Mercantile Hub, a conceptual architectural design framework for sustainable waterfront regeneration in Port Harcourt, Nigeria, synthesising historical building condition data, community survey findings (n = 364), and semi-structured interview testimony from informal traders and built-environment professionals into a coherent, three-zone spatial and governance model. title: The nuclear-climate nexus for net-zero pathways: Opportunities, challenges, and policy directions: A review
abstract: Rapid decarbonization is now a central sustainability challenge because electricity demand is rising while climate risks are increasingly affecting energy infrastructure. Although solar, wind, storage, efficiency and electrification remain essential for net-zero pathways, many power systems also require firm low-carbon resources, resilient infrastructure and governance arrangements that can sustain reliable energy services under extreme weather, geopolitical disruption and growing industrial demand. title: Land Triadic Nexus: A conceptual framework for land governance through the strategic adaptive alignment of land use, rights, and values
abstract: Land governance persistently fails to achieve its stated objectives, producing unintended outcomes, coordination failures, and inequality. This paper argues that a major reason is the treatment of land use, land rights, and land value as parallel administrative domains rather than as mutually constitutive components of one recursive governance structure. The Land Triadic Nexus, developed here, explains governance outcomes as a function of the degree of alignment among these three domains. title: Research on a Safety-Perception-Oriented Image Enhancement and Lightweight Object Detection Model for Power IoT
abstract: To address image quality degradation, difficulty in recognizing small defect targets, difficulty in quantifying external-damage risks, and limited computing resources of embedded devices in edge inspection of the power Internet of Things (Power IoT), this paper proposes an image enhancement and lightweight object detection model for power safety perception, named EEL-YOLO. title: Applications of the InVEST Habitat Quality model: A literature review of methodological trends and model integration, with implications for human-wildlife interactions
abstract: The Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Trade-offs Habitat Quality (InVEST HQ) model offers a spatially explicit approach for assessing habitat quality utilizing relatively simple, readily available data and an intuitive interface. In this paper, we provide a literature review of the InVEST HQ application based on 61 scientific papers, which have been systematized, analysed, and interpreted using a detailed and structured original template. title: BERTRAG as a BERT-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation framework for preserving Awori and Ogu indigenous knowledge
abstract: Indigenous cultural knowledge is frequently distributed across heterogeneous and low-resource sources, including oral histories, archival records, ritual texts, community narratives, and locally produced documents. Such knowledge is often context-dependent and governed by community protocols, making it susceptible to distortion, hallucination, and loss of contextual meaning when processed using generic large language models (LLMs). title: Coupled drought–land use dynamics and agricultural resilience in mainland Southeast Asia
abstract: Abstract Drought is initiated by climatic anomalies, but its development and consequences often unfold as a coupled socio-ecological process shaped by interactions among land use, water infrastructure, resource management, and governance. This coupling is particularly pronounced in Mainland Southeast Asia (MSEA), where strong monsoon dependence, rapid land-system transformation, expanding hydraulic infrastructure, and intensive water use influence how climatic water deficits propagate through hydrological, agricultural, and livelihood systems. title: A multi‐objective decision‐analysis framework for addressing human–wildlife conflicts
abstract: The costs and frequency of negative interactions between people and wildlife (that is, human–wildlife conflict or HWC) are increasing globally and hindering conservation efforts. Practitioners are challenged to manage wildlife populations and consider human health and livelihoods simultaneously. Principles and tools of conservation decision‐making can help relevant parties navigate the complexities, uncertainties, and difficult trade‐offs involved in managing HWC. journal: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment

title: METimE: A maximum entropy framework with data-derived micro-scale dynamics
abstract: The Maximum Entropy Theory of Ecology (METE) derives probability distributions for micro-scale variables, such as species abundances and metabolic rates, solely from macro-scale observables like total abundance and species richness. While METE performs well in systems with relatively constant macro-scale observables, its predictive accuracy declines in disturbed or rapidly changing systems due to its inherently static approach. title: Mapping justice claims for solar geoengineering
abstract: Solar geoengineering is a set of controversial emerging technologies that seek to cool the planet by reflecting sunlight. These technologies may be able to reduce the worst impacts of climate change by lowering global temperatures temporarily. They also come with great risks, including as related to technological lock in and mitigation deterrence, among others. Balancing these potential risks and benefits demands a careful interrogation of justice and ethics. Unlike many scholars who assert a clear justice landscape, we argue here that the terrain is complicated, nuanced, and not fully mapped.

title: Global patterns and trends in event-scale runoff generation reveal disproportionate declines in arid catchments
abstract: Abstract Event-scale rainfall-runoff analyses improve understanding of runoff generation processes and efficiencies, complementing long-term analyses. We present the first uncertainty-aware global synthesis of event-scale runoff generation, which is quantified by events occurrences, typical runoff coefficients, and their full empirical distributions across individual catchments. title: Automatic evergreen forest mapping based on Harmonised Landsat Sentinel-2 and existing broad-category land cover product within Google Earth Engine
abstract: Evergreen forests retain green foliage throughout the year and exhibit distinct phenological and biophysical characteristics. However, although many regional and global land cover products are available at 30 m resolution, most adopt coarse classification schemes and do not explicitly distinguish evergreen forests from other forest types. This study proposes a novel Automatic Evergreen Forest Mapping (AEFM) framework to generate annual evergreen forest maps at the city scale using dense Harmonised Landsat Sentinel-2 time-series data on the Google Earth Engine platform. title: Capturing Typhoon Rapid Intensification and Abrupt Recurvature Using an IAU‐Based 4DVar Scheme
abstract: Abstract Dynamic imbalances in model initialization severely constrain the predictability of the rapid intensification (RI) and abrupt track recurvature of tropical cyclones (TCs). In this study, the effectiveness of an incremental analysis update (IAU)‐based four‐dimensional variational (4DVar) data assimilation scheme in forecasting Typhoons Doksuri and Khanun in 2023 was investigated. title: Reproductive hesitation in the Norwegian petrostate
abstract: This article responds to calls for critical engagement with the entangled politics of reproduction, population, and climate breakdown by exploring analytical avenues that refuse both the individualization of responsibility and the logics of population. Taking as our empirical point of departure Andy Lautrup’s ethnographic engagement with the eco-reproductive considerations of young climate activists fighting to end oil production in Stavanger, Norway, we ask what it means to hesitate about one’s reproductive future from a position of privilege and complicity within the Norwegian petrostate, an

title: Effects of Renewable Energy Adoption on Public Health Outcomes in Nigeria's South-South Region
abstract: The worldwide transition to renewable energy is crucial for tackling environmental deterioration, climate change, and health issues related to reliance on fossil fuels. This research focused on the influence of renewable energy on public health and examined perceptions, possibilities, and obstacles concerning the energy shift in Nigeria's South-South area. A mixed-methods approach was employed, involving 400 questionnaire participants and 60 interviewees chosen from six states in the region. title: TB-YOLOv8n: an improved YOLOv8n-based model for tip-burn detection in plant factory-grown pakchoi under LED lighting
abstract: Introduction Plant factory-grown pakchoi is prone to tip-burn under high-density cultivation, limited airflow, and rapid growth conditions, which reduces leaf integrity and commercial quality. Image-based detection of small or mild visible tip-burn symptoms remains challenging because the affected regions are usually small, irregularly shaped, low in color contrast, and easily disturbed by red-blue LED lighting, leaf overlap, curled leaf margins, and heart-leaf occlusion. title: Study on AGV scheduling in automated container terminals considering staggered battery swapping
abstract: Driven by low-carbon and environmental sustainability initiatives, automated container terminals (ACTs) increasingly employ automated guided vehicles (AGVs) as horizontal transportation equipment. As AGVs are electrically powered, battery swapping operations can affect their continuous operational capability. To address the concentration of battery-swapping demand and the resulting queuing phenomenon during AGV operations at ACTs, this study proposes a probability-based staggered battery-swapping strategy. title: Still seeking permission to narrate: On international law and the question of Palestine
abstract: Abstract At the foundation of knowledge production is the question of who exactly is doing the producing, on what basis, when, where and for whom? Are all views equal? Whose views are or ought to be included? And with what implications? In this 2025 LJIL Lecture, Professor Ardi Imseis meditates on these and other related questions through the prism of one of the most pressing international legal and moral issues of our time: Palestine.

title: Genome Microbiology at 20 Years: Who We Are and Where We Are Going
abstract: The International Symposium "Microbial Growth and Behavior: From Bench to Nature" was held as part of the annual meeting of the Society for Genome Microbiology, Japan. This session was designed to highlight challenges in modern microbiology: how to connect molecular insights obtained from laboratory model systems with the dynamic and complex responses of microbes in natural environments.

title: A socio-environmental analysis of households’ livelihood vulnerability to agricultural drought in Kwara State, Nigeria
abstract: Agricultural drought has significant consequences on agriculture, water resources and the livelihoods of rural communities. This study examined the key socioeconomic and environmental factors that influence drought risk and resilience and assessed how exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity interact to shape rural households' livelihood vulnerability, using the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change vulnerability framework. title: On Prizes
abstract: ABSTRACT This article discusses prize‐creation and prize‐allocation. Such activities may seem morally neutral, or perhaps even beneficial. A central thesis of this article is that such practices have significant moral implications and should be brought under the remit of moral reasoning. I suggest that in many cases, the harmful effects of prizes are overlooked, and that they stand in need of scrutiny, revision, and possibly abolition. title: Spatial coupling between historic buildings and tourism development in China’s historical and cultural cities
abstract: Historic buildings are an important category of built heritage, but evidence on their coordination with tourism is often based on local cases. Of 143 candidate city-level units, 127 were retained after screening. This study examines 1176 historic-building records and their relationships with domestic and international tourism. abstract: Alzheimer's disease and related dementias are increasingly understood as multicellular disorders in which neurons, glia, and vascular-associated cells may contribute differently to cognitive status and neuropathologic burden. This manuscript summarizes figure-level findings from a postmortem aging and dementia dataset that measured cortical cell-type proportions and tested their associations with dementia diagnosis, cognitive scores, time from last assessment, and common neuropathologies. abstract: The diachronic evolution of the adverb seguramente (‘surely’) reveals a shift from its original use as a manner adverb –expressing physical or psychological security– to modal meanings conveying first certainty and later high probability. Drawing on a corpus of more than 2,000 occurrences extracted from CORDE and CREA, this study examines the interaction between several linguistic parameters –including adverbial type, syntactic distribution, degree of integration, and verbal tense, mood, and semantics– in the semantic evolution of seguramente. title: Impact of Wupa Wastewater Treatment Plant Effluent on Wupa River as a Source for Consumption in Zhidu Settlement
abstract: The qualities of the treated effluent of the Wupa Wastewater Treatment Plant located in a rural community of the Federal Capital Territory (Abuja-Nigeria) were assessed over two seasons (wet and dry). This study evaluated the Wupa Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) with acceptable local (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency –NESREA) and international (World Health Organization-WHO) standards and the effect on the receiving surface water (Wupa River) sources around Zhidu Settlement in Abuja. title: Annual geospatial foundation model embeddings for landslide susceptibility assessment in Taiwan
abstract: Landslide susceptibility models (LSMs) must identify unstable terrain before failure is visible, yet it remains unclear whether compact geospatial foundation-model embeddings encode such pre-event information. We evaluate the efficacy of annual 64-dimensional AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings for LSM using Taiwan landslide inventories from 2017–2024. title: Intent to impact: United States case studies on equity measurement in energy efficiency programming

abstract: Abstract Recent reports of decadal-scale structural changes in the lowermost mantle and transport of strong heterogeneity in the outer core may offer important insights into core-mantle structure and dynamics. title: Spatio-temporal rainfall variability and trends in northern part of Bangladesh: A statistical and GIS perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates long-term spatial and temporal rainfall homogeneity, variability, concentration, and trends across northern Bangladesh, a climate-sensitive region where rainfall variability has important implications for water resources and agriculture. Daily rainfall records from eight meteorological stations covering the 42-year period (1982-2023) were analysed. title: Predicaments and Countermeasures in the Development of China’s Retail E-Commerce
abstract: After more than two decades of development, China has remained the world’s largest online retail market for 13 consecutive years, achieving a remarkable transformation from “the world’s factory” to “the world’s shopping center” and leading the development of the global e-commerce industry. However, the current development of China’s retail e-commerce is confronted with numerous difficulties and has entered a bottleneck. abstract: Accurate evaluation of radio access performance is essential for the design and optimization of ultra-dense fifth-generation (5G) networks, where the interactions between multiple users, base stations, and interference sources become highly complex. This paper proposes a comprehensive System-Level Simulation (SLS) framework for assessing the performance of multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems in indoor hotspot environments, following the standardized 3rd generation partnership project (3GPP) InH_B channel model. title: Multi-facility GNSS antenna calibration
abstract: Abstract Accurate antenna calibrations are a cornerstone of high-quality global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) positioning, time and frequency transfer, precise orbits, and troposphere estimates. The international GNSS service (IGS) antenna committee maintains antenna phase center corrections in the ANTEX file relying on five calibration facilities. title: Unraveling the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the 2024–2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion Island
abstract: Réunion Island experienced a massive chikungunya virus epidemic in 2024-2025, with >54,000 confirmed cases. This is the second major chikungunya epidemic on the island, following the first one that peaked 20 years ago. It has been asserted that this new outbreak finds its origin in a single introduction event into the island, offering an opportunity to exploit viral genomic data to understand the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the introduced transmission chain. abstract: Immovable cultural heritage (IMCH) constitutes a vital material record of human civilization and represents a precious asset shared by all humanity. This study integrates Geographic Information System (GIS) spatial analysis and the Geodetector model, taking 1,032 IMCH sites in Jiangxi Province as the research object, to systematically investigate their spatiotemporal distribution characteristics and driving factors, and on this basis proposes strategies for their conservation and sustainable development. title: TLCG-VMD: A two-layer coupled graph-constrained variational mode decomposition framework for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Variational mode decomposition has been widely used for vibration signal analysis due to its clear variational formulation and non-recursive decomposition mechanism. However, most existing variational mode decomposition–based methods mainly improve parameter optimization, initialization, or target-mode selection within a single-layer framework. abstract: The democratization of spatial information through WebGIS has emerged as a tool for engaging local communities in urban environmental management. This article presents the development of AGATA WebGIS (Advanced Geoenvironmental Analyses in Environment and Technology), a collaborative mapping platform designed to democratize access to environmental information at the local level and promote public participation. abstract: In low-literacy, climate-vulnerable agricultural settings, smallholder farmers rarely evaluate new technologies independently; adoption is mediated through trusted institutional intermediaries. However, the systemic factors driving intermediary-perceived adoption of AI advisory tools remain unmapped. abstract: Bureaucratic reform is a strategic agenda for realizing effective, transparent, accountable, and responsive governance to global dynamics. Increasing demands for quality public services, digital transformation, and strengthening institutional capacity have driven the development of research on bureaucratic reform in various countries. However, studies that comprehensively map the development of this research are still relatively limited. title: Significance of Environmental Justice for Human Dignity: A Nexus between Right to life and Right to Environment
abstract: The impact of environmental pollution, climate change, and loss of biodiversity poses a direct threat to the existence of human beings. This article examines the development and interaction of these two fields through references to legal instruments, constitutional provisions, and cases that support a sustainable environment for human rights. It posits that environmental rights should no longer be seen as secondary or optional, but as core, justiciable elements of contemporary human rights systems. abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe present study undertakes a bibliometric analysis of the scientific discourse pertaining to innovative financing. title: Autopoiesis and the Limits of Closure in International Law: Interpretation, Social Practice, and the Temporal Life of Legal Meaning
abstract: This article re-examines the claim that international law is an autopoietic legal system. Autopoiesis remains attractive because it explains how a legal order may preserve a distinct identity through self-reference, recursive norm production, and operational closure in the absence of a central legislator, compulsory jurisdiction, or unified enforcement. title: Molecular and Epidemiological Surveillance of Sporothrix spp. in Cats and Dogs from Southern Brazil
abstract: Sporotrichosis, a subcutaneous mycosis caused by Sporothrix spp., has emerged as a major zoonotic disease in Brazil, primarily driven by Sporothrix brasiliensis. The southern state of Rio Grande do Sul exhibits distinctive ecological and climatic conditions that may shape the persistence and distribution of this pathogen in this region. abstract: The introduction to this special issue describes the ‘parasite’ as a concept through which to understand the problems and possibilities of cohabitation, with its attendant strategies of shelter and expulsion, its affects of gratitude and resentment. title: Cross-regional emission reduction based on government-enterprise-public collaboration in the construction industry
abstract: Excessive carbon emissions are recognized as a significant contributor to climate change and environmental degradation. Achieving carbon neutrality has become an imperative for sustainable development. This study examined carbon emission reduction mechanisms in the construction industry, focusing on collaborative efforts among key stakeholders to achieve balance, coordination, and sustainability in carbon emission control. abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective community surveillance of respiratory diseases relies on the timely collection and analysis of high quality clinical and virology data. The aim was to develop interactive dashboards for general practice, public health, and researcher groups. This would improve the visualisation, utilisation, and quality of virology data from an English sentinel network, support disease trend monitoring, early outbreak response, and thereby reduce poor health outcomes and their societal impact. title: CRISPR-Cas immune repertoires as an ecological record of bacterial interactions with mobile genetic elements in the human gut
abstract: Bacteria in the human gut influence host physiology and disease risk, but their ecology is strongly shaped by mobile genetic elements (MGEs) such as phages and plasmids. title: Impact of piece-wise linear receiver clock modeling on sub-daily PPP coordinates for highly stable IGS H-maser stations
abstract: Abstract Modeling highly stable GNSS receiver clocks helps to increase the stability of correlated parameters, especially the station height. The use of a piece-wise linear receiver clock model, which is a common method for clock parametrization in Very Long Baseline Interferometry, has not yet been extensively investigated for GNSS. In this work, we examine piece-wise linear receiver clock modeling for GNSS. Based on a one-month series of kinematic Precise Point Positioning analyses for 56 highly stable hydrogen maser stations, the effects of piece-wise linear clock modeling are demonstrated.

abstract: The aim of this study is to reveal the development trends, conceptual structure, and research gaps of the literature on supply chain disruptions and digitalization. Therefore, bibliometric methods have been employed to systematically analyze the intellectual structure of the literature. abstract: Summary We propose an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)‐assisted three‐phase protocol based on cooperative wireless power transfer for a primary system to enable spectrum sharing with a secondary system in a cognitive radio network. The primary system comprises an access point (AP) and an energy‐harvesting primary user (PU), whereas the secondary system consists of a secondary transmitter (ST) and a secondary receiver (SR). abstract: The study was focused on women and management of Oil-Related Conflict in Bayelsa, Rivers and Delta States; from 2013-2023. This was because the series of conflicts associated with oil are pervasive major societal issues in the Niger Delta area. title: Too hot to race? Demonstrating heat stress modelling as an adaptation tool for endurance events
abstract: Heat stress is an increasing concern as climate change drives more frequent and intense extreme heat episodes. In particular, participants in outdoor endurance events face a high risk of heat stress related health issues due to prolonged exposure to heat and physical exertion. The Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) is a widely used ISO-standard heat stress index that integrates air temperature, humidity, wind speed, and radiation (both shortwave and longwave) to assess heat stress. abstract: In a more competitive, digitally advanced and trust-poor market, customer satisfaction has become a key performance measure in general insurance. Unlike goods business, general insurance is intangible: its customers gauge it based on many indirect factors, including service, claim settlement experience, communication, and pricing transparency, and digital convenience. abstract: Abstract The accelerated decline of insects is driven by anthropogenic pressures such as habitat loss, pesticide use, and climate change. Species vulnerability varies according to their exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity to these threats. Artificial light at night (ALAN) further increases this vulnerability by disrupting nocturnal and crepuscular species, particularly moths. abstract: Many heritage institutions hold extensive collections of show programs. Too numerous to be cataloged individually, they remain difficult to access and are still largely undigitized. This paper presents a workflow for transforming such documents into structured, interoperable data by combining vision-language models (VLMs), a custom extension of the Linked Art ontology for the performing arts, and different approaches for automatic semantic data annotation. abstract: Astyanax Baird & Girard, 1854 is a widely distributed and species-rich genus of Acestrorhamphidae, whose abundant populations in Neotropical basins play a crucial ecological role at the trophic level. Taxonomic uncertainties persist within the genus, as seen in Astyanax sp. (formerly designated as A. fasciatus) from the Magdalena basin in Colombia. abstract: The gut microbiome plays a critical role in host health, yet its composition in African wild mammals remains underrepresented. We investigated how dietary groups (carnivores, non-ruminant, and ruminant herbivores) influence gut microbiota composition and diversity in coexisting wild mammals from the Kruger National Park, South Africa. After quality filtering, 89 samples (carnivores: n = 31; non-ruminants: n = 37; ruminants: n = 21) were included. abstract: Abstract Phylogenetic studies of insular radiations have traditionally relied on mitochondrial DNA, yet the increasing availability of genomic datasets has revealed numerous cases of phylogenetic discordance between mitochondrial and nuclear markers across animal taxa. The present study focuses on the Aegean Dailognatha, a group of six predominantly insular darkling beetle species. abstract: Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes provide strong error-correction capability for wireless communication systems, but their iterative decoding process introduces computational and energy costs that are particularly important in energy-constrained Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). This study comparatively evaluates the Sum-Product Algorithm (SPA) and the Min-Sum Algorithm (MSA) for LDPC decoding, with emphasis on the trade-off between communication reliability and estimated decoding energy. title: Performance over people: Mapping the absence of social equity metrics in green roof research
abstract: Green roofs provide a diverse array of ecosystem services, yet within the domain of natural and engineering sciences, where green roof research is most situated, performance-related studies are unevenly distributed across thematic dimensions. Socio-economic aspects such as affordability and social equity receive far less attention than technical and biophysical outcomes, despite their importance for public policy, municipal investment, and socially inclusive climate adaptation. abstract: Long-duration spaceflight raises a human question as well as an engineering one: how can crews maintain physical coordination, emotional steadiness, and supportive relationships when familiar conditions change? This conceptual article introduces the Cosmo-Embodied Adaptation Framework, a research map for connecting Tai Chi (Taijiquan, 太极拳) cultural practices with specific questions about space adaptation. abstract: BACKGROUND: The majority of children in developed economies attend childcare services during the first five years of life-a period coinciding with their developmental transition from regular napping to consolidated nighttime sleep. Whether childcare attendance affects this transition is not well understood. Previous studies have relied primarily on cross-sectional designs or widely spaced longitudinal observations, limiting their ability to distinguish childcare effects from differences between children and families. abstract: Abstract Salt accumulation and surface fouling remain major barriers to long-term solar-driven interfacial evaporation. Here we report a geometry-engineered Janus electrospun membrane that integrates asymmetric wetting with structural design to suppress salt buildup. abstract: To improve the cooperative positioning accuracy of urban intersections under conditions of global positioning system signal blockage and complex traffic flow, this paper proposes a cooperative positioning model that integrates a mathematical analytical Gaussian belief propagation robust filtering algorithm with a spatial attention mechanism. abstract: Introduction This study examines the intellectual structure and substantive evidence of research on governance, bureaucracy, and disaster risk reduction (DRR), addressing the conceptual fragmentation of scholarship across disaster studies, sustainability, public health, environmental governance, and public administration. abstract: Limiting global warming to 1.5 °C requires profound transformations of production and consumption systems, yet the role of businesses in enabling such transitions remains insufficiently addressed in scenario-based sustainability research. Existing scenarios often conceptualize firms as implementers of mitigation measures rather than governance actors shaped by policy, institutions, and societal expectations. abstract: Published records of nickel (Ni) hyperaccumulator and accumulator plants in Türkiye are relevant to serpentine ecology, metallophyte biogeography and future field studies. abstract: This review analyses the growing field of microbial metabolites in agriculture, moving beyond the widespread narratives to evaluate the scientific foundations, efficacy claims, and ecological implications of their widespread application. This article discusses the widespread benefits of using microbial metabolites in agriculture to enhance plant physiology, biochemistry, and defense. abstract: The adoption of virtualization/containerization technologies in industrial control systems promises improved deployment flexibility, scalability, and resource efficiency. title: HSF1-mediated proteostasis decline links aging and sleep disruption
abstract: Sleep disruption increases with age and is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, integrative analyses of human and mouse transcriptomic and proteomic datasets identify proteostasis pathways whose aging trajectories align with responses to chronic sleep disruption across tissues, cell types, and molecular layers. Mouse brain and human blood analyses independently recover heat shock factor 1 (HSF1)-associated proteostasis as a recurrent feature of sleep-aging convergence. title: Institutional drivers of sustainable development goals implementation in facilities management: evidence from South Africa
abstract: Purpose During the operational phase of buildings, facilities managers are uniquely positioned to implement sustainable development goals (SDGs) without expensive construction changes required. The ISO 41000 series of International facilities management (FM) standards provides high-level guidelines for implementing 17 of the UN’s SDGs across various aspects of facility operations. title: Multi-objective sensor network layout optimization method based on reference point sorting mechanism
abstract: Wireless sensor network (WSN) layout optimization requires the simultaneous improvement of coverage, energy balance, and network connectivity. However, conventional multi-objective optimization algorithms often suffer from uneven solution distributions and the loss of sparse or boundary solutions, which limits their performance in complex deployment environments. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Reference-Point-Based Multi-Objective Transit Search algorithm (R-MOTS) for WSN layout optimization. title: Adjustable extruders and nozzle geometry effects in additive manufacturing: a review
abstract: Extrusion-based additive manufacturing, such as fused filament fabrication and direct ink writing, is valued for its versatility and material compatibility. Nozzle geometry governs material flow, bead morphology, dimensional accuracy, and mechanical performance. Conventional systems rely almost exclusively on fixed-geometry nozzles, whose outlet size and shape are set at manufacture and remain constant for the entire print.
