title: Technical progress, democratic deficits: Communication and socio-environmental conflicts in wind energy expansion in Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil
abstract: In the context of global decarbonization imperatives, renewable energy expansion drives the energy transition while intensifying local socio-environmental conflicts. Although environmental and economic impacts of wind energy are widely researched, the role of democratic communication in legitimizing this transition remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by examining how communication practices influence environmental licensing and conflict resolution in Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil's leading wind producer, focusing on four municipalities: Rio do Fogo, Guamaré, Parazinho, and Galin

title: Intelligent diagnosis method of English learning disabilities based on knowledge mapand long-term and short-term memory network
abstract: Aiming at the problems of insufficient recognition accuracy and lack of explanation in the diagnosis process of behavioral indicators of potential learning disabilities, an intelligent diagnosis model integrating knowledge map and long-term and short-term memory network is constructed. Model learning behavior sequence and knowledge structure information are modeled in a unified way, and the relationship between time dimension and semantic dimension is established. title: Information Transparency and Firm Performance: The Mediating Role of Business Ethics in Organic Coconut Sugar Exporters
abstract: Organic coconut sugar exports depend on claims about origin and process that buyers cannot verify directly, so exporting firms are increasingly required to make their information verifiable. Previous studies have examined traceability systems and business ethics separately and have rarely tested how transparency reaches performance, which constitutes the research gap of this study. title: Evaluation of Comprehension and Views on Green Cities and Sustainable Urban Environment: A Developmental Perspective
abstract: Green cities and the sustainable urban environment have gained popularity worldwide, both in literature and in practice. It is, however, indicative that, it is still unpopular among Nigerians. Otherwise, the popularity could have translated to a green environment and sustainable urban development, lessening the rate of continual urban environmental degradation. Thus, this paper reviews the critically needed key to enhancing the green city, eco-friendliness, and sustainable urban environment in Nigeria. title: Political Recruitment and Pregnancy Resources: Anti‐Abortion Feminists Come to Campus, United States, 1990s
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Feminists for Life's (FFL) rhetoric and activism on US college campuses in the 1990s as a case study into the complexities of organizing against abortion in a historical context whereby few supports existed for young pregnant women. Members of this anti‐abortion feminist group understood college students as both the future of the right‐to‐life cause and especially “vulnerable” to abortion. title: Shāh-e Sarāb: A Hazara Solar Festival in Bamiyan and Connections with Ancient Khordādgān
abstract: Abstract The annual festival of Shāh-e Sarāb has been a major Hazara pilgrimage in Waras district of Afghanistan’s Bamiyan Province on the fourteenth day of Jawzā/Khordād (June 4). Drawing on published accounts, virtual ethnography, remote interviews, and satellite imagery, this article describes the shrine and the principal ritual components of the celebration in arguing that Shāh-e Sarāb represents a “Shi’i-ized” continuation of Khordādgān, the ancient Iranian month/day festival of the Zoroastrian goddess Khordād. title: Introducing shrubs enhances the representation of high-latitude vegetation and carbon cycling in the ORCHIDEE land surface model
abstract: Arctic–Boreal terrestrial ecosystems are rapidly changing under amplified high-latitude warming, including widespread expansion of shrubs, with consequences for regional carbon and energy balances. Yet, high-latitude vegetation diversity and vegetation–climate interactions remain under-represented in many global land surface models. In ORCHIDEE, the land surface component of the IPSL Earth system model, high-latitude vegetation is represented primarily as boreal trees or grasslands, omitting explicit shrubs. title: From order to species: Modelling Amphipoda distributions in the Hamersley Range
abstract: Groundwater amphipods in the Pilbara region of Western Australia are under pressure from the impacts of mining operations, particularly from groundwater extraction. To help inform conservation planning for this subterranean group, we model their distribution using a suite of environmental variables and occurrence data, and a Random Forest (RF) classification method. Given the taxonomic uncertainty and cryptic diversity in groundwater amphipods, we compared model results across nested taxonomic datasets to assess the potential benefits and limitations of higher-level taxonomic modelling. title: Conceptualizing Data Literacy for Citizenship
abstract: Abstract This survey paper opens a Special Issue of ZDM – Mathematics Education on “Enhancing data literacy for citizenship: Innovative approaches in data science and statistics education.” In this paper we aim to conceptualize ‘data literacy for citizenship’ (DataLitCit), going beyond prior conceptualizations of statistical and data literacies. title: Effect of Foliar Application of Micronutrients on Growth, Seed Yield and Yield-contributing Characters of Sesame (Sesamum indicum L.)
abstract: A field experiment was conducted at the Quality Seed Production Unit, Khanapur-A, VNMKV, Parbhani, during the summer season of 2025–26 to evaluate the effect of foliar application of micronutrients on growth, seed yield, and yield-contributing characters of sesame (Sesamum indicum L.). The experiment was laid out in a randomised block design with nine treatments and three replications using the sesame variety ‘TLT-10’. title: Assessment of Oil Spillage and Its Control in the Oil and Gas Industry in Nigeria
abstract: This project set out to examine the compensation of oil spill victims in the Nigerian oil industry. The compensation of these victims has become clumsy and dark in the wake of oil bunkering, pipeline vandalism, sabotage, since in the past, oil spill was as a result of the activities of the oil companies or operators. title: Invited Perspectives: Science for Comprehensive Disaster and Climate Risk Management
abstract: In this paper, we explore five core challenges that need to be addressed in order to move towards the Comprehensive Disaster and Climate Risk Management approach, which has been proposed within the newly emerging paradigm of a more holistic approach to managing the risks associated with climatic and/or non-climatic hazards and non-climatic risk drivers across varied time scales and levels. title: Laying the Groundwork for Moveable Heritage Disaster Risk Management: A Database-Driven Evacuation Tool at the Musée d’Archéologie Nationale
abstract: This paper presents a case study conducted at the Musée d’Archéologie Nationale (National Archaeology Museum) in France, to develop a dedicated database application to safeguard its moveable heritage from risks, as a foundational component of the museum’s wider Disaster Risk Management (DRM) strategy. abstract: Purpose. This study aims to improve the reliability of the classical Rock Mass Rating system by introducing a control-based DEMATEL-TOPSIS framework that explicitly incorporates parameter interactions and reduces classification uncertainty near boundary conditions. Methods. title: Rethinking Carbon Taxation as Strategic Management: Insights from Mintzberg’s Ten Schools
abstract: This study evaluates carbon tax policies from the perspective of strategic management, employing Mintzberg’s ten schools of thought as the analytical framework. These schools-comprising both prescriptive approaches (design, planning, and positioning) and descriptive perspectives (entrepreneurial, cognitive, learning, power, cultural, environmental, and configuration)-offer a multidimensional understanding of how carbon taxation strategies are conceived, implemented, and adapted over time. abstract: Abstract Background The field of interventional bronchoscopy (IB) has experienced rapid advancements over the past two decades, evolving from a predominantly diagnostic modality into a highly technological specialty encompassing use of endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS), electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy (ENB), robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB), transbronchial cryobiopsy, airway stenting, and image-guided interventions. title: Insights and opportunities from materials chemistry research at primarily undergraduate institutions in the U.S.
abstract: Materials chemistry research at primarily undergraduate institutions (PUIs) in the United States is often characterized by the constraints faculty face: limited instrumentation, smaller research groups, heavier teaching loads, and rapid student turnover. This Perspective argues that PUI materials chemistry research is better understood not as a diminished form of research university science, but as a distinct and productive research mode with its own logic and strengths. title: Residual-guided confidence learning and dynamic ensemble selection for semi-supervised hyperspectral image classification
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification with limited labeled samples remains challenging because unreliable pseudo-labels may propagate errors and individual classifiers may perform inconsistently across different data distributions. To address these issues, this study proposes a semi-supervised framework integrating residual-guided confidence learning and collaborative classifier strategies. Three key components are introduced. title: Black phosphorus quantum dot heterostructures: Adaptive interface engineering, electronic coupling, and predictive design
abstract: Black phosphorus quantum dot (BPQD) heterostructures have emerged as promising nanoscale platforms for energy conversion, catalysis, optoelectronics, and photoactive systems because their functional performance is primarily governed by interfacial electronic interactions rather than the intrinsic properties of individual components. This review examines how quantum confinement, excitonic behavior, surface electronic states, defect evolution, and environmental stability collectively regulate heterostructure functionality through interface-mediated charge redistribution and electronic coupling.

title: False kings and imagined protestants: why schismogenesis does not explain variation in inequality among Indigenous societies of the Pacific Coast
abstract: Indigenous societies along the temperate Pacific coast of North America embody diverse cultural institutions. This variation is conventionally classified into two distinct cultural areas: the Northwest Coast (NWC) and California (CAL). Discussion of the environmental, material, social, and ideological variation in these societies has a long and continuing history in anthropology. In the last few years, two divergent accounts of this variation have appeared. journal: Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute

title: Beyond “Chimerica”: U.S.–China strategic competition and African agency in a disordered world
abstract: The intensification of strategic competition between the United States and China has become one of the defining dynamics of 21st-century international relations, reshaping patterns of global governance, economic interdependence and geopolitical alignment. While existing scholarship has largely examined this rivalry through the lens of great-power competition, Africa is frequently portrayed as a passive arena in which external actors pursue competing interests. title: Amino acid homorepeats in tape measure proteins correlate with bacteriophage tail length
abstract: The tape measure protein (TMP) dictates the tail length of tailed bacteriophages. However, the sequence features that drive the process of length fine-tuning have not yet been described. Tandem repeats (TRs), stretches of aas organized as multiple adjacent copies of the same or very similar sequence motif, are contributors to TMP length variation. Homorepeats (polyX regions) are a specific type of TRs composed of stretches of identical aas, forming low-complexity regions that contribute to protein structural flexibility and dynamics. title: Geographic hazard and residential catastrophe insurance quotations: Evidence From Italy
abstract: Abstract This study examines residential catastrophe‐insurance quotations in Italy using 1512 property profiles collected from one insurer in 2025 across 108 provincial quotation units. Each profile contains earthquake and flood amounts; dwelling types and floor‐area values repeat across units. Peril‐specific Gamma‐log models relate these amounts to independently sourced provincial hazard, adjusting for recorded property characteristics and region fixed effects. title: Exploring the potential of large language models for public participation in urban redevelopment planning
abstract: Public participation is essential to human-centered urban planning, yet existing approaches often struggle to translate dispersed public opinions into clear and discussable preference expressions. This limits substantive deliberation between public preferences and expert knowledge, making it difficult to effectively incorporate public needs and experiences into planning decision-making. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to support participatory planning by helping organize diverse public preferences and facilitating deliberation between public perspectives
institutions: Jiangsu Provincial Urban Planning and Design Institute

title: Spatially informed demand-side policies for green hydrogen diffusion in Europe
abstract: Abstract Green hydrogen faces an implementation gap: demand substantially lags policy ambitions. Here, combining an installation-level model of green hydrogen demand with an original database of >14,000 potential offtakers in Europe, we show that, conditional on diffusion patterns mirroring natural gas power generation (a historical analogue), demand-side spatial considerations are critical for closing this gap. title: Digital sovereignty and jurisdictional complexities in the metaverse: Rethinking legal authority in virtual spaces
abstract: The metaverse disrupts long-settled allocations of legal authority by layering immersive virtual environments on top of distributed infrastructures that rarely map onto territory. This article argues that hierarchical, state-centric regulatory models cannot adequately govern such environments, because power is already distributed among states, platforms, protocol designers, and user communities. The article asks a precise legal question: how should legal authority be allocated across these actors to sustain rights, accountability, and coherence in immersive virtual worlds? abstract: Abstract Integration of Internet of Things (IoT) and Edge Computing (EC) presents significant challenges, particularly in guaranteeing secure communication amid IoT devices and cloud systems formerly to data aggregation. Existing aggregation schemes often compromise on cost-effectiveness while struggling to preserve data integrity and confidentiality in face of emerging quantum computing threats. title: Vat photopolymerization additive manufacturing: A critical review of materials, processes, applications, and sustainability
abstract: Vat photopolymerization (VPP) has advanced from a laser-scanned prototyping into a multi-material additive manufacturing platform whose chemistry, process variants, application reach warrant critical appraisal. This review synthesizes 355 peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus between 2018 and 2026, retrieved through a structured query within article title, abstract, and keyword fields and filtered for English-language journal articles. title: Untargeted LC-HRMS/MS and Feature-Based Molecular Networking Reveal Distinct Metabolic Signatures in Edible Dahlia Types
abstract: Abstract Edible flowers represent chemically diverse food matrices whose characterization increasingly relies on advanced metabolomic approaches. This study employed untargeted liquid chromatography–high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS/MS) combined with feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) to characterize and differentiate the metabolic profiles of flowers and roots from five edible dahlia types cultivated under organic conditions. title: A circular approach to reduce, recover and recycle graphene-based printed electronics
abstract: Abstract The shift towards renewable materials and circular processes is crucial for sustainable printed electronics. Conventional conductive inks rely on petrochemical-based solvents and synthetic binders that hinder recyclability and recovery of high-value materials. Here, we report a recyclable graphene ink formulated with a bio-renewable terpene solvent and cellulose-based binder for electrochemical sensing applications. title: Institutional Readiness and Performance in Flood Risk Management in Southwest Nigeria
abstract: Despite the efforts made to reduce risks, flood incidences in Nigeria have persistently led to loss of lives, property and infrastructure damage, as well as unsustainable environment. This study assessed the institutional readiness and performance in flood risk management in Southwest Nigeria. Survey research method was adopted, where data was collected from 66 respondents, selected purposely from Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states through the use of questionnaires. title: The cost-effectiveness of medical versus surgical androgen deprivation therapy for advanced prostate cancer in Tanzania: a Markov model-based analysis
abstract: Background Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is a recommended treatment for patients with advanced prostate cancer, mostly for palliative purposes. In limited resource settings, decision-making about palliative treatment should be guided by the overall survival benefit of one option over another, patient life expectancy, quality of life, and cost. Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of medical androgen deprivation therapy compared to surgical androgen deprivation therapy among patients with advanced prostate cancer in Tanzania. title: Institutional governance and climate–health–economic resilience in Africa: Multisectoral coordination, policy integration, and adaptation implementation
abstract: Climate change is a systemic threat to Africa’s health systems, economies, and development trajectory, with the continent projected to bear the highest climate-related disease burden by 2030. This systematic review examines institutional governance frameworks for climate–health–economic resilience in Africa, with a focus on multisectoral coordination, policy integration, and adaptation implementation. title: Adapting the emergency management enterprise to manage the climate emergency: a critical review
abstract: Climate adaptation has long been recognized as a key risk management tool for addressing the climate emergency. Despite evidence of progress in implementing adaptation in the United States, the Nation faces mounting disaster losses and an expanding adaptation gap driven by limited policy frameworks, financial constraints, lack of awareness, and deeply rooted social vulnerability. Recognizing these limits to adaptation, this paper critically examines the potential for leveraging the U.S. emergency management (EM) enterprise to enhance national resilience to future acute climate risks. abstract: MSME souvenir products are one of the local business sectors that help support regional economic growth by offering products that represent the unique characteristics of an area and are often purchased as gifts or souvenirs. To remain competitive and continue growing, MSME businesses need to understand consumer needs and preferences. Therefore, identifying the factors that influence purchasing decisions is important for improving business performance and competitiveness. title: Designing curriculum at the intersection of language, culture, and coloniality: reflections from primary French textbooks in Mauritius
abstract: Curriculum development, specifically textbook conception, in postcolonial contexts like Mauritius is neither a neutral nor a primarily technical undertaking; it remains a deeply situated process shaped by linguistic and cultural diversity, tacit colonial language hierarchies, and underlying ethnic tensions. This paper explores these dynamics as they manifested during the conception of Grades 5 and 6 Primary French textbooks within the Nine Year Continuous Basic Education reform. abstract: This study aims to reconstruct the paradigm of wasathiyah (moderate) character education based on Islamic humanism at the Al-Asror Islamic Boarding School in Semarang. It employs a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and the analysis of relevant documents. title: Revised diets and urban infrastructure can improve human health and the global environment
abstract: Current patterns of food production and consumption are widely recognised as unsustainable. This review explores opportunities to shift food systems towards healthy diets and secure food yields while remaining within planetary resource boundaries. Drawing on improved global data on the environmental impacts of different foods, we adopt a systems perspective to examine the interconnected nexus of health, diets and the global environment, with particular attention to the role of future urban food systems. title: Metabolomics and network pharmacology of Ethiopian antidiabetic medicinal plants: A comprehensive framework for mechanistic elucidation and drug discovery
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) affects approximately 537 million adults worldwide, and this number is expected to increase to 783 million by 2045, highlighting the urgent need for effective and affordable therapeutic strategies. In Ethiopia, where nearly 80% of the population depends on traditional medicine for primary healthcare, more than 30 medicinal plant species have demonstrated antidiabetic activity in experimental studies. title: Bryofloristic account of the genus Riccia L. from Girnar Wildlife Sanctuary, Gujarat
abstract: The plant genus Riccia L. comprises a highly diverse group of complex thalloid liverworts and accounts for a substantial share of bryophyte diversity. However, the literature indicates that Riccia liverworts are widely distributed but little is known about Riccia species from semi-arid environments of western India. In this context, this study aims at contributing to the national knowledge repository by carrying out detailed investigation of diversity, habitat preferences, spatial patterns and altitudinal variations of Riccia species in the Girnar Wildlife Sanctuary, Gujarat. abstract: Introduction Soil erosion (SE) is one of the major constraints to sustainable social and ecological development. The spatiotemporal dynamics and the driving factors of SE are critical to improve regional ecosystem services and guarantee ecological and food security. title: Pivoting in the pandemic: how HIV-focused community-health workers addressed COVID-19 disparities
abstract: Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic significantly overburdened the U.S. healthcare system and magnified pre-existing care delivery gaps in communities of color. In Miami-Dade County, Black residents account for 64% of AIDS-related deaths and experienced a COVID-19 mortality rate of 6.1%, compared to 3.9% among White residents. Community Health Worker (CHW) interventions represent a promising strategy to overcome social and economic barriers to care. abstract: This paper examines inflation dynamics in Türkiye within a state-dependent Phillips curve framework by jointly considering domestic and external factors. Using monthly data for the period 2005–2025, conditional relationships across different forecast horizons are estimated through the local projections (LPs) method. title: Bridging the gap between damaged infrastructures and disaster mortality
abstract: Abstract Driven by the lack of global empirical data, there is limited research that analyzed the relationship between infrastructure damage and disaster impact. In this research, we addressed this gap by scraping 79 Post Disaster Needs Assessment reports to collect disaster specific infrastructure damage data for 79 disaster events of this century. abstract: La presente investigación analizó el uso de la inteligencia artificial generativa en biología y gestión ambiental, con énfasis en su aporte a la conservación sostenible de los ecosistemas. El estudio se desarrolló desde un enfoque cualitativo, mediante una investigación documental de alcance descriptivo sustentada en la revisión sistemática de literatura científica reciente relacionada con modelos generativos, monitoreo ambiental y análisis de datos biológicos. title: Digital Transformation and Agricultural Supply Chain Resilience: The Mediating Role of Sustainable Consumption and Production
abstract: Digital transformation has emerged as a critical driver of agricultural supply chain resilience, yet the mechanisms through which technology investment translates into resilience outcomes remain inadequately understood. Addressing this gap, this study examines the mediating role of sustainable consumption and production in this relationship. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the SDG12 framework, an integrated model is developed and tested using survey data from 423 agricultural enterprises across six provinces in China. title: Why should fisheries professionals care about instream flow and water level conservation?
abstract: Abstract Conservation of instream flows and water levels (instream flows) are vital to sustaining healthy aquatic, riparian, and terrestrial ecosystems. Natural instream flow regimes provide habitat and life history cues, sustain ecological communities, influence water temperatures and other water quality attributes, and affect geomorphic processes. title: Mediamorphosis and Resilience: An Analysis of the Survival Strategies of African Newspapers Limited (Nigerian Tribune) in a Digitally Disrupted Environment
abstract: The Nigerian print media industry is currently grappling with an "economics of decline" and digital disruption, resulting in high mortality rates for legacy publications. This qualitative phenomenological study investigates the strategic management and adaptations adopted by the Nigerian Tribune (African Newspapers Limited) to sustain its operations as Nigeria’s oldest surviving private newspaper. title: Strengthening evidence on migrant workers’ health in Nepal
abstract: Abstract Thousands of Nepalese labour migrants have died abroad in past decades, and morbidity is also high. The high volume of data collected through pre-departure health screening, unfortunately, remains largely unused. Making better use of health data, including by trusted public health researchers, could help develop health interventions for migrant workers.

title: Geological hydrogen storage in South Asian sedimentary basins thermodynamic considerations, geotechnical challenges, and energy perspectives
abstract: Geological hydrogen storage (GHS) is a critical technology for enabling large-scale, low-carbon energy systems in South Asia within the water–energy–carbon nexus. This review evaluates subsurface hydrogen storage potential across key sedimentary basins in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka, integrating geotechnical, environmental, and policy perspectives. Estimates from depleted gas reservoirs (5.8–7.4 billion Nm³) and saline aquifers (2.1–3.3 billion Nm³) highlight significant capacity, particularly in the Cambay, Krishna–Godavari, and Bengal basins. title: Brief communication: InSAR Svalbard Ground Motion Service – observing surface displacements in the High Arctic
abstract: The InSAR Svalbard Ground Motion Service (GMS) provides open-access surface displacement maps and time series in the Svalbard archipelago, derived from Sentinel-1 Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR). The service provides seasonal products capturing short-term 2016–2024 displacements and interannual products documenting long-term 2018–2024 velocity trends. abstract: Rural human-settlement systems in cold regions mediate the interaction between climatic stress, population restructuring and unequal access to housing and public services, yet the relevant evidence remains divided among building science, spatial analysis and governance research. abstract: Climate change has become a major threat to environmental sustainability and food security in Nigeria, particularly among rural communities that rely heavily on agriculture for their livelihoods. Increasing incidences of drought, flooding, desertification, land degradation, and erratic rainfall have significantly reduced agricultural productivity and intensified food insecurity. abstract: El emprendimiento en el ámbito universitario constituye una alternativa vinculada con la formación profesional, el desarrollo de competencias y las transformaciones del entorno socioeconómico. title: Grounded Youth
abstract: Across Europe, economically and demographically declining regions offer limited educational and occupational opportunities for young people. These opportunities are often restricted further for those in vulnerable life situations, as vulnerabilities are connected to and impacted by limited resources and capacities. abstract: As funders of health and care research increasingly mandate inclusive research practices, the Manchester Biomedical Research Centre (BRC) and Clinical Research Facility (CRF) developed a comprehensive Inclusive Research (IR) Strategy to embed the principles of inclusivity across their experimental medicine research. abstract: Abstract Achieving high‐peak‐to‐average power ratio (PAPR) remains a fundamental challenge in orthogonal frequency‐division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. abstract: This study investigates corporate legal liability for greenwashing practices that cause environmental harm in Indonesia. Growing global pressure for sustainable business practices has prompted many corporations to publicly commit to protecting the environment, but such narratives often serve as public relations efforts rather than genuine ecological responsibility. abstract: Chemical substances used in various industrial applications can pose serious environmental risks. Among them, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are of particular concern. These compounds have been detected in both environmental and biological samples, including human breast milk. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how Chinese television dramas socially construct corporate social responsibility (CSR) in the context of ethical family‐business succession. Drawing on stakeholder theory and qualitative content analysis, we analyze eight widely viewed TV series (including one negative case) that dramatize succession processes in Chinese family firms. abstract: ABSTRACT Persistent compensation disparities between privately owned enterprises (POEs) and state‐owned enterprises (SOEs), together with substantial pay gaps within POEs, are salient manifestations of income inequality in China. abstract: Clean beauty has emerged as a prominent category in the cosmetics industry, often associated with sustainability, ethical consumption, and environmental responsibility. However, its definition remains fragmented and is largely based on ingredient-focused claims, sustainability narratives, and consumer perceptions rather than systematic sustainability governance. abstract: The rapid expansion of the digital economy coincides with escalating environmental challenges, making Green Data Centers (GDC) an important form of digital infrastructure with potential implications for environmental governance. abstract: In China, two strategies are now being carried out, namely nationwide fitness and rural revitalisation, and under this background, sports activities in rural areas have gradually become more organised, no longer being the kind of casual events held in the past. This paper takes the Tanmen Beach Games in Qionghai, Hainan as a research case and uses it to illustrate some situations. title: A framework for AI-integrated models to assess agricultural resilience
abstract: Agricultural supply chains are vulnerable to disruptions through linked biophysical and economic systems. We develop a novel AI-powered tool that integrates economic models (GTAP) with biophysical models (APSIM) to analyze supply chain shocks, enabling policymakers and market participants to assess cross-disciplinary impacts through queries and responses written in natural language. The evolving landscape of remote sensing employment: a data-driven analysis of requirements, skills, and responsibilities in earth observation roles
abstract: Remote sensing and Earth observation technologies are expanding rapidly across scientific, commercial, and governmental domains, yet limited empirical research has examined how these roles are defined in practice. This study analyzes 250 public remote sensing job postings across 33 nations collected over an eight-month period in 2025. title: Desnutrición crónica infantil en Pastaza: entre el hipergarantismo legal y la desprotección territorial de la niñez amazónica
abstract: Este artículo examina la desnutrición crónica infantil (DCI) en la provincia de Pastaza, Ecuador, analizando la brecha entre el marco normativo garantista y la realidad territorial. La DCI afecta al 29,5 % de los menores de cinco años en la provincia, ubicándola como la segunda con mayor prevalencia en el país. title: Analytic hierarchy process-based criteria for assessing the site suitability of small water impounding projects in Bukidnon, Philippines
abstract: The engineering planning and design of Small Water Impounding Projects (SWIPs) necessitates proper site selection to ensure technical viability and sustainability. This study developed localized criteria for assessing the site suitability of SWIPs in the whole province of Bukidnon by integrating national engineering standards with local experts’ opinions using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). title: Comparing ‘degrowth’ with ‘green growth’ on the question of ecological sustainability: A way forward for ‘degrowth’
abstract: Debates on sustaining economic systems within ecological boundaries have intensified, with green growth and degrowth emerging as opposing theoretical standpoints. Green growth, the dominant policy approach, advocates technological innovation and policy intervention to align economic growth with environmental sustainability, yet often narrows its focus to climate change, overlooking other forms of ecological degradation. In contrast, degrowth critiques the growth imperative and proposes alternative pathways grounded in ecological limits and social equity. However, it remains largely theoretical

title: Risk Factors and Interventions in Juvenile Delinquency: A Multidimensional Study of Eight Districts in Bangladesh
abstract: Juvenile delinquency often arises when children face poverty, family problems, school dropout, harmful peer influence, and substance abuse. This study examines these risks and identifies practical ways to support prevention, rehabilitation, and safe reintegration of children into their families and communities. This mixed-methods study examined juvenile delinquency among 286 respondents with juvenile-justice experience across eight districts of Bangladesh.

title: The biodiversity we ignore: A global meta-analysis on taxonomic bias
abstract: As biodiversity decline continues, there is a critical need to document, monitor, and protect species equitably across the tree of life. However, both scientific research and societal perceptions of biodiversity are often biased toward large, colorful, charismatic, familiar, or otherwise "useful" species. We conducted a global meta-analysis encompassing 905 effect sizes from 78 studies across three decades of research assessing drivers of taxonomic bias. abstract: How to Increase Shade Availability and Improve the Outdoor Thermal Environment of Cities with Blue-Green Infrastructure. Rather than providing new empirical data, it collects existing research on green and blue infrastructure, urban microclimates and thermal comfort indices to propose a path for integrating vegetation and water in heat-resilient public spaces. abstract: Purpose The human extracellular matrix (ECM) provides essential cues for intestinal homeostasis. While most studies focus on ECM degradation by host cells, emerging evidence suggests that commensal gut bacteria may also contribute to these remodeling processes. Here, we systematically characterize the genomic diversity and functional activity of ECM-associated enzymes across Bacteroides, a dominant and metabolically versatile genus of the human gut microbiome. title: BEYOND THE BEAT: EVALUATING AWARENESS AND EFFECTIVENESS OF POLICE PATROL OPERATIONS TOWARDS STRATEGIC INTERVENTIONS
abstract: This study evaluated the implementation and effectiveness of police patrol operations in Northern Samar, Philippines, to establish an empirical basis for strategic interventions. Employing an explanatory sequential mixed methods design, the research integrated quantitative survey data with qualitative phenomenological inquiry using Colaizzi’s seven-step method. Quantitative data were gathered from a statistically representative sample comprising patrol supervisors, beat patrollers, and community officials, complemented by in-depth interviews with key informants. title: Would-be Émigrés: Navigating the Academic Job Market Under Fascism
abstract: Abstract What defines an émigré scholar? Drawing on personal correspondence between members of the Unity of Science movement, this article emphasizes the contingency of the category by reconstructing the social and material conditions that shaped academic life under fascism. When scholars became refugees, they had to find ways to move their knowledge with them. title: Uses of Native and Exotic Palms in Ecological Restoration
abstract: For its outstanding biodiversity Ecuador has been designated as one of ten megadiverse countries. Due to its location on the equator, it enjoys many climates, soils and diverse geological processes. In Ecuador, palms represent the group of native plants with the greatest diversity of uses per species. At the Mashpi Shungo Reserve in the Ecuadorian northwest, the authors have been working to restore degraded areas using regenerative practices through diverse agroforestry systems. abstract: Harga penutupan saham pada sektor komoditas agribisnis merupakan salah satu indikator yang penting bagi para investor, karena memiliki pergerakan yang fluktuatif dan dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor ekonomi. Pola data harga saham cenderung berubah-ubah menyebabkan proses peramalan menjadi sebuah tantangan, terutama pada data saham harian. title: Role of yeast MIG1 gene in glycolysis, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and glycogen and trehalose biosynthesis in response to DNA damage
abstract: Background: In eukaryotic cells, under certain stress conditions, the diversion of carbohydrate flux, either downstream toward tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle or upstream toward the hexosamine biosynthesis and pentose phosphate pathways, is governed by the activation of key regulatory genes and glycolytic enzymes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the transcription factor Mig1 (encoded by the MIG1 gene) regulates respiration, glucose repression, and gluconeogenesis. title: The role of improved seed variety and information access in moderating the effect of cluster farming on climate resilience: a global meta-analysis with a focus on Ethiopia
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens rain-fed agriculture in developing countries like Ethiopia. Cluster farming has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance smallholder resilience; however, existing evidence remains fragmented. Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 peer-reviewed studies (2000–2025), including eight from Ethiopia. title: Eschatologia Iranica IV: Automated Judgment in Zoroastrian Eschatology; The Way Činwad Bridge Works
abstract: Abstract The Zoroastrian eschatological bridge, known as Činwad, is razor-thin for the wicked, while the righteous can cross it easily. The present article demonstrates that some narratives describe this transformation as a revolving movement of the bridge’s deck. By assembling dispersed, concise, and intricate information derived from certain Middle Persian texts, the mechanics of this rotation can be elucidated. title: Research-Related Competence, Productivity, and Culture among Secondary Mathematics Teachers in the Schools Division of Dagupan City
abstract: This study examined the relationship among research-related competence, research productivity, and research culture of secondary mathematics teachers in the Schools Division Office of Dagupan City. The inquiry was guided by Shulman’s Pedagogical Content Knowledge, Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory, and the Framework Design Integration Model (FDIM), which emphasize the integration of knowledge, practice, and institutional support in teacher research. title: Effectiveness of emergency nutrition program for toddlers after Mount Semeru eruption in Lumajang: CIPPO evaluation
abstract: Malnutrition in toddlers remains a public health concern in Indonesia. East Java reports a relatively high prevalence of wasting (7.2%), while Lumajang Regency recorded a severe wasting prevalence of 6.9% in 2022, exceeding WHO public health thresholds and increasing from the previous year. The 2021 eruption of Mount Semeru disrupted food systems and limited access to health and nutrition services, increasing nutritional risks among affected toddlers. abstract: This study aims to analyze SO2 and NO2 concentrations around the PT.X power plant through direct measurements, model their distribution patterns using AERMOD, and evaluate the model’s performance using RMSE, MBE, and R statistical tests. Monitoring was conducted at two monitoring points (PLTU PT.X Area and Nii Tanasa Village) over four 1-hour intervals (morning, afternoon, evening, night) using an Impinger Air Sampler. abstract: Objective criterion weighting plays an important role in multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), particularly when decision outcomes depend on how differences among criteria are represented. However, conventional objective weighting approaches may emphasize specific statistical characteristics of the decision matrix without explicitly considering criterion heterogeneity as an integrated concept. title: Language shifts as a catalyst for social and educational cohesion in multilingual societies
abstract: Although the Indonesian New Capital City, or Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN), is a potential living laboratory of a multilingual society, studies investigating the extent to which language shift conditions stimulate educational cohesion remain limited. To fill this gap, this research aims to investigate language shifts at schools in IKN to achieve equitable education. title: Tracing the development of primary students' expressed sustainability conceptions through SDG-based classroom action research
abstract: This qualitative classroom action research study traced the development of primary school students' expressed sustainability conceptions during an 8-week interdisciplinary process based on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Participants were 31 fourth-grade students (aged 9–10) in one intact classroom of a public primary school in Istanbul, Türkiye. Instruction comprised 24 class periods of 40 min across eight weekly action research cycles; the second author taught all lessons while the first author observed every session. title: Fear of abandonment and the US alliance – the paranoid logic in Australian foreign policy
abstract: For more than seven decades, the US alliance has been a central pillar of Australian security policy. Yet the last decade has seen US commitments become increasingly conditional and uncertain. Why has Australia responded to growing uncertainty about the reliability of the US by binding itself more deeply to the alliance? Building on Allan Gyngell’s account of Australia’s ‘fear of abandonment’, I argue that Australian foreign policy has been shaped by a recurring pattern of anxiety management. abstract: Successfully addressing and resolving water challenges, in a global context where the vectors of population growth, urbanisation, climate change and globalisation are at work, is a key element to foster sustainable development and achieve an improvement in the quality of life of societies and people. title: Governing green enabling megaprojects: reconciling transformative risk-taking with megaproject delivery discipline
abstract: This paper introduces green enabling megaprojects (GEMs) to characterize an increasingly important class of infrastructure for climate change mitigation. GEMs are large-scale green infrastructure projects whose primary value lies in enabling broader socio-technical transformation through subsequent adoption, diffusion, and scaling. abstract: This commentary responds to Anthony A. Lee’s sounding, “The Declaration of the Báb in Bahá’í Imagination” (Bahá’í Studies Review, 2026). title: Developmental and tissue expression breadth define distinct but overlapping classes of housekeeping genes
abstract: Housekeeping genes are commonly defined as broadly expressed genes that support essential cellular function. However, their identification in genome-wide datasets typically relies on spatial variation across adult tissues, while largely overlooking developmental time as an additional dimension of gene expression diversity. abstract: Restructuring has transformed the United States (U.S.) electricity sector from cost-based, vertically integrated monopolies to competitive Wholesale Electricity Markets (WEMs), marking one of the major shifts in the modern energy industry. Independent System Operators and Regional Transmission Organisations (ISOs/ RTOs) have led this transition by coordinating generation, transmission, and market operations across large regions. abstract: As one of the biggest consumers of the world’s water and producers of emissions, the textiles industry has come under fire for sustainability issues in recent years. Sportswear firms stand out from their peers as big users of synthetic fibers like polyester and nylon produced from crude oil which can shed harmful microfibers into local waterways. abstract: El entrenamiento de modelos de inteligencia artificial generativa ha transformado los desafíos del derecho a la protección de datos frente a sistemas cuyo funcionamiento dificulta la eliminación de la información. title: Plant part substitution as a sustainable conservation strategy for some medicinal plants based on phytochemical equivalence
abstract: Abstract Medicinal flora represents an essential source of bioactive substances for both conventional and contemporary medicine; nevertheless, excessive extraction of non-renewable parts such as roots, bark, and heartwood has led to significant reductions in wild populations, especially among endemic and slow-growing species. abstract: This study scrutinizes the part played by the United Nations Human Rights Council [UNHRC] in protecting human rights in South-East Nigeria 2015-2022, a period distinguished by extra-security operations, arbitrary arrests, extra-judicial killings and other forms of human rights violations in the region. title: Evaluating geoscience campaigns in the conservation of water resources in the Western Region, Ghana
abstract: The Western Region of Ghana faces persistent water resource issues due to pollution, illegal mining, unsustainable land use, and degrading ecological integrity, public health, and livelihoods. Though geoscience-based water conservation campaigns have been initiated to remedy these issues, limited empirical data exist on their effectiveness in encouraging the conservation of water. title: On the Threshold of Feminism: Gender, Autonomy, and the Limits of Resistance in Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre
abstract: This study examines Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre (1847) as a proto-feminist text, analysing the ways in which the novel simultaneously advances and retreats from feminist ideals. It is argued that the novel’s treatment of female identity, economic independence, and romantic love both approaches and departs from feminist objectives. abstract: This experimental research examines the dynamics of turbulent circular wall jets developing over a smooth bed and three distinct rough beds. Acoustic Doppler velocimetry was employed to measure the instantaneous flow field. abstract: El tema del presente artículo trata sobre: Crisis del Derecho Liberal y el Tema de la Ampliación de los Poderes del Juez en la Producción de la Prueba en los Procesos Colectivos.El objetivo general de la investigación desarrollada fue comprender el instituto jurídico del Derecho probatorio en finales del Derecho liberal, trazando toda la evolución que tuvo para el Derecho Procesal Civil, específicamente en lo que se refiere a la ampliación del principio inquisitivo en la producción de la prueba en los procesos colectivos.

abstract: This article provides a concise review of the current literature on the circulation of influenza A viruses in cattle and the unprecedented emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 infection in this species. Particular attention is paid to the ecological and biological aspects of influenza A virus cross-species transmission, as well as to the potential implications of these events for veterinary medicine, livestock production, and public health. abstract: Objective Foodborne disease remains a major public health concern globally, with low- and middle- income countries disproportionately affected. In Ecuador, food environments are dominated by smaller food vendors, yet less is known about risks to food safety in this context. abstract: Severe sedimentation in the Sengguruh Reservoir has reduced its effective storage capacity to approximately 24% of the original value, creating persistent dredging and spoil bank management problems. title: Hybrid quantum-inspired secure and energy-efficient framework for wireless sensor networks using quantum key distribution and optimization techniques
abstract: Abstract Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) require secure and energy-efficient communication because sensor nodes operate with limited battery power, constrained communication range, and high vulnerability to interception, spoofing, and malicious forwarding. Existing methods usually optimize security, clustering, or routing independently, which reduces overall network efficiency under dense and adversarial conditions. abstract: Drainage pattern recognition is valuable for watershed hydrological simulation and geological structure exploration. abstract: This study investigates the cognitive attitudes of primary and secondary school teachers in Sichuan Province, China, toward the implementation of the “Double Reduction” education policy (DREP), guided by policy diffusion theory. A descriptive survey design was employed, utilizing stratified random sampling to collect data from 12,524 teachers across four regions of varying socioeconomic development levels. abstract: UAV engineering vehicle detection is a fundamental task for intelligent construction monitoring, as engineering vehicles directly reflect construction progress, equipment deployment, and potential safety risks in dynamic construction scenes. abstract: Ratio-based Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) methods provide practical approaches for ranking alternatives, but differences in normalization and aggregation mechanisms can produce different rankings and levels of stability. abstract: Abstract Russia’s war in Ukraine has revived the European Union’s enlargement policy, placing it at the forefront of the EU’s priorities. This process is being viewed as the next phase of EU enlargement, encompassing the Western Balkans, Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia. abstract: Vibrio natriegens is a promising biotechnological chassis distinguished by exceptionally rapid growth and dynamic metabolism. abstract: This article examines the Crusaders Super Rugby franchise’s partial rebranding after the 15 March 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks as a case study in how sport reproduces settler/invader colonialism, racial capitalism and white possessive power in Aotearoa New Zealand. While the attacks prompted public scrutiny of the franchise’s name, medieval crusading symbolism and pre-match performance culture, New Zealand Rugby and the Crusaders retained the “Crusaders” name and substituted the horseman logo with koru-inspired branding. title: The environmental consequences of rising political populism and growing economic inequality
abstract: This paper examines how political populist support and income inequality are associated with the ecological footprint and its two sub-components: the carbon footprint and the non-carbon footprint (land and water use). Using a panel dataset covering 16 high-income European countries from 1990 to 2022, we estimate a dynamic panel error correction model. Three findings stand out. Right-wing populist support is positively associated with the carbon footprint, whereas left-wing populist support is negatively associated with the carbon footprint. title: Arab nationalism and historicity in the 1980s novel: Haydar Haydar’s Walīma li-aʿshāb al-baḥr and Rachid Boudjedra’s Maʿrakat al-Zuqāq
abstract: Two 1980s novels from the Maghreb and Mashreq, respectively – Algerian writer Rachid Boudjedra's Maʿrakat al-Zuqāq (Battle of the Strait, 1986) and Syrian writer Haydar Haydar's Walīma li-aʿshāb al-baḥr (Banquet for Seaweed, 1983) - offer formal and thematic critiques of a regime of historicity that they link to Arab nationalist states after decolonization. title: Learning to start a new business with values: the challenge of sustainable entrepreneurship in university teaching
abstract: Purpose This study aims to present a teaching methodology that integrates sustainability and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into entrepreneurship education to foster the development of sustainable business models (SBMs) through challenge-based learning (CBL) in higher education. Design/methodology/approach The methodology was implemented over five years at the University of Valencia and the University of Turku, combining CBL with a proprietary framework for designing, testing and scaling SBMs. A systematic literature review (2003–2024) was conducted to support the approach. title: Integrating concept mapping and authentic assessment to enhance pre-service elementary teachers’ competence
abstract: This study examines the integration of concept mapping and authentic assessment in pre-service elementary science education using a four-phase professional development model. An embedded mixed-method design was employed, involving 82 seventh-semester students in a primary school teacher education program at a state university in Indonesia. title: Graph-guided MADQN based handover strategy for LEO satellite networks
abstract: In low earth orbit satellite networks, the high orbital velocity of satellites causes frequent communication link handovers, which adversely affects user service quality and the efficiency of network resource management. To maintain communication continuity, an effective handover strategy is required. Traditional handover strategies are typically based on fixed decision rules, which makes it difficult to balance handover frequency, signal quality, and network load balancing. title: Unlocking fast robotic locomotor propulsion through dynamic spine-leg synergy
abstract: Quadrupeds in nature achieve agile locomotion through a rhythmic flexing of the spine in coordination with leg movement. This dynamic synergy enhances their speed and stability, reflecting a kind of physical intelligence encoded in their bodies. However, identifying this spine-leg synergy and embodying it in robotics to enhance locomotor propulsion remains challenging. title: Modeling the pathway from transformational leadership to innovative work behavior via AI readiness: advancing SDG 4 and SDG 8 in Indonesian higher education
abstract: Drawing on a cross-sectional survey of 250 lecturers and administrative staff from Indonesian higher education institutions (HEIs), this study examined the statistical relationships among transformational leadership, AI readiness, and innovative work behavior (IWB) using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings showed that transformational leadership was positively associated with AI readiness (β = 0.654, p < 0.001) and IWB (β = 0.322, p < 0.001), while AI readiness was positively associated with IWB (β = 0.451, p < 0.001). abstract: The study investigated the contribution of Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC) toward healthcare delivery in Onne oil bearing communities. title: A high resolution urban energy atlas for spatiotemporal energy-demand assessment of 1.69 million buildings
abstract: Abstract The building sector is central to achieving climate neutrality because of its major contribution to final energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. abstract: Abstract Regulation and technology innovation are crucially intertwined in many cases and industries, notably in air transportation.
